pool.titulo: GTA 6 Truffade Thrax: How to get Andrew Node's supercharged version
pool.resumen: Scan the No Flusher graffiti to steal the fastest car in the game.
pool.contenido:
Grabbing a Truffade Thrax in GTA 6 isn't too hard, but if you want Andrew Node's supercharged version, the true fastest car around, you'll need to complete a little collectible hunt. Before you start, it's worth noting that this special Truffade Thrax costs 70k to register when you steal it, though you can also sell it to Randy for 20k (not that I would recommend this as it's a unique car).
The first step is scanning ten No Flusher toilet graffiti stamps around Vice Beach, the east portion of Vice City, with your WAiNK It app. Each symbol is basically a little blue toilet. After that, you'll have to head to a secret lockup, and then you're on for stealing the car.
1. Southeast of Nola - Ocean Beach This first one is southeast of Nola - Ocean beach on the pavement on the west side of the road.
2. East of Podium Sports - Ocean Beach The second is east of Podium Sports - Ocean Beach, on the south side pavement of the road leading out onto the grass towards the beach.
3. Near the bridge leading to Waxman Island This one is at the east end of the bridge leading from Vice Beach to Waxman Island, on the southern pavement. Also to the west of LTD Gas - Ocean Beach
4. East of Aural Expert This fourth one is east of Aural Expert and north of Venus Fitness, on the pavement at the side of the junction.
5. Out front of Banana Hole Main Bar This one is on the pavement directly in front of Banana Hole Main Bar, east down the road from the previous one above.
6. At the southern end of the park This sixth one is on the sidewalk on the far west of the road running along the bottom of the huge park in Vice Beach.
7. West of Podium Sports - Ocean Beach This seventh is west of Podium Sports - Ocean Beach, down the road you can see with the roundabout at the end on the map.
8. East of Shorefront - Ocean Beach bank The eighth is east down the road from Shorefront - Ocean Beach bank and south of Easy Electronics, on the pavement on the corner.
9. North of Marshal's Jewelry This ninth is north of Marshal's jewelry and northeast of Endzone - Washington Beach, at the east end of the big carpark bordering the beach.
10. At Oldby Island junction On the right side of the northern road at the Oldby Island junction, directly opposite Ron Gas - Washington Beach.
Accessing the secret hideout After you've found all ten, Cal's conspiracy theory chat (which unlocks after the first) will go dark, before you get a separate message giving you their hideout location, close to the tenth No Flusher tag at Oldby Island. Head there, read the note to the right of the garage door, and then flip it around to get the code for the lock:
8554013 Inside you'll have a bunch of evidence pointing to Andrew Node's house on Starfish island, so examine it all and then you're ready to steal the car.
How to steal Andrew Node's Truffade Thrax First off, Starfish Island is a gated community with security, so it's better to get a boat there. Head west from the hideout and steal a boat on the piers, then drive west across the water to the jetty of Andrew Node's house—it's the one on the southern side towards the centre, that looks like a backwards L.
Dock, head around the left side of the house to find a white garage on the right you can open up with Andrew Node's Truffade Thrax inside. You'll have to drive it off the island, but after that you can head to Randy and register it for 70k. Just make sure you have the garage space and the money before you steal the car.

pool.titulo: These budget-friendly pads are the cheapest, quickest way to instantly upgrade your setup for under $25
pool.resumen: Be a master controller on the cheap.
pool.contenido:
I've lost count of how many times I've settled down to play a brand-new game on Steam, only to be smacked in the face with a giant popup telling me to "Grab a controller and kick back!" instead of using my humble mouse and keyboard.
Thankfully for me I live in a multi-platform household, meaning a controller is never far out of reach. But I've also got staunch PC pals without a pad to pick up and who, rightly enough, don't want to fork out the kinda cash that PlayStation's DualSense or the Xbox controller require.
We're curating all the Cyber Monday PC gaming deals right here But I'm a firm believer that a good controller is a must-have tool in a PC gamer's repertoire these days, and we needn't immediately seek out the big names when it comes to a comfortable, robust gamepad. Tons of budget-friendly options have popped up on the market over the years, and while some of them are admittedly pretty naff there are also a bunch of great controllers that won't break the bank.
In fact, I've got three of 'em for under $25 for you right here. That's a third of the price of a DualSense controller! While they don't come with fancy haptics and adaptive triggers, they do offer stick-drift resistant, low-latency gaming. Which, as fun as the bells as whistles can be, are really the most important bits.
A new and improved version of the original Nova Lite, the Nova Lite 2 has Hall effect everything, 1000 Hz polling, and trigger locks. It even has a mechanical D-pad, which is absurd for the money, really.
Key specs: Wireless (Bluetooth and 2.4 GHz) | Asymmetric | Hall effect
Price check: Amazon $29.99 (Grey) View Deal
Out of the three choices, our pad professional James Bentley tells me he likes the GameSir Nova Lite 2 the best, currently going for $23 at Walmart . It boasts comfort, decent polling, and Hall effect—so much better protection against that pesky stick drift. It's also got our highest review score out of the bunch thanks to its affordability, mechanical d-pad, and choice of 2.4Ghz and Bluetooth.
It's not got great grip, however, and its budget is felt in the less-than-stellar plastic and rather simple software. But for the price you're paying? It's a great, basic choice for those who only need to reach for a controller occasionally.
Ultimate 2C: was $29.99 now $19.89
We've already raved about Hall effect joysticks and how they spell the end for the dreaded stick drift. In this wireless gaming controller, they're a welcome feature, but this handful of gaming hardware packs a few quirky surprises too. For instance, there are extra bumper buttons.
Key specs: Hall effect sticks, triggers | 2.4G wireless | 19 h battery
Price check: Best Buy $21.99 (Black) | Walmart $29.99 (Purple) View Deal
But if you're someone who's accustomed to the likes of the Switch Pro controller, you might find the 8BitDo Ultimate 2C a better fit, currently going for $20 at Amazon. It's got a pretty similar shape, and also sports those beloved Hall effect joysticks. It does have a little bit of a mushy d-pad but hey, look at that lovely colourway!
Finally, if you're looking to spend as little as possible, the GameSir Nova Lite comes in as the cheapest option at a mere $18 . It's got less mappable buttons than its successor thanks to no back paddles, and is overall a downgrade. For the extra four bucks I'd personally just go for the newer version, but if you're really looking to really squeeze every cent, it's certainly an option worth considering.
It's incredible to think you can spend so little and get a stick drift-resistant wireless controller that doesn't completely suck. Luckily for the GameSir Nova Lite, it does all of the above and manages to feel good and light in the hands, too.
Key specs: Wireless (Bluetooth and 2.4 GHz) | Asymmetric | Hall effect
Price check: Amazon $22.99 View Deal

pool.titulo: Should you participate in GTA 6's Safe Word mission?
pool.resumen: Grab the lotion.
pool.contenido:
Deciding whether to participate or not in GTA 6 's Safe Word mission is tricky. On the one hand, you don't want to blow your cover, on the other, the setup is incredibly funny. Jason and Lucia head to a mansion to steal a safe, masquerading as pool cleaners, but once Jay heads inside, it's clear that he's actually playing a poolboy in an erotic flick.
While applying lotion to the female performers, Lucia will get increasingly agitated in his earpiece, and then you'll finally have to choose whether to actually participate in the scene or not:
Participate : This will negatively impact your romance with Lucia and since the outcome is the same (Lucia immediately interrupts the scene by setting off a car alarm), Jason doesn't actually do anything. As Rockstar has previously said, you can't cheat on Lucia . After you leave the scene, Lu will be a little angry, but it won't hang over things. Don't Participate : This will positively impact your romance and as above, the car alarm will immediately go off afterwards, ending the scene anyway. Jason will say he needs to go to the bathroom and make his way inside the mansion, continuing the mission to find and steal the safe. So, on the whole, choosing not to participate is better if you care about your romance level and how it might impact things later. If not, say what you will.

pool.titulo: GTA 6 Players Have Found a Cheeky Method to Quickly Steal ATMs
pool.resumen: Somewhere around the middle of GTA 6 you unlock the ability to rob ATMs. Any ATM marked green can be pulled out of the wall and cracked open.
pool.contenido:
Warning! Potential spoilers for GTA 6 follow.
Somewhere around the middle of GTA 6 you unlock the ability to rob ATMs. Any ATM marked green can be pulled out of the wall and cracked open (check out IGN's guide to all ATM locations in GTA 6 if you need help finding one).
First, though, you need to be able to deal with marked bills through a fence called Yasmini, otherwise the money inside the ATM is worthless and a dye pack will explode in your face. When I got to snatching ATMs, I thought it was cool, but the juice didn’t seem worth the squeeze.
It’s kinda hard to keep things on the downlow when you’re backing a truck up to an ATM, ripping it out of a wall, and tearing down the street with the thing still attached, hoping it’ll burst open and spill its contents onto the street. And when it finally does break open, you have to shoot the money drawers open to get to the goods inside — all for a payout between $6,000-$10,000.
It wasn’t worth the effort, honestly. But there’s a new trick players have discovered to crack those eggs immediately and move onto the next before the cops even know you’re there. I’ve tried it, and like Todd Howard famously once said: it just works.
How to quickly steal an ATM in GTA 6 Here’s what you do. First, you need a truck or other heavy vehicle with a winch attachment at the back. You reverse up to the ATM like normal, and the winch connects to the machine. Now drive forward until the line is taut.
From there, get out of your vehicle and walk up to the ATM with a C4 charge. Hold down aim, and a prompt to place it on the ATM should show up, allowing you to set it on the front with Circle/B. Or throw it at the front of the machine — whatever works.
Once it’s in place, you want to get back in your car and accelerate hard. When it pulls out of the wall, keep dragging it but immediately press unhook, followed by the same button to detonate your charge. It’s important these two actions happen immediately after each other, because the ATM needs to be moving when the explosion happens or the drawers can stay inside the machine.
Done correctly, you can walk over and scoop up the cash and escape before the cops even arrive at the scene. They’ll still be figuring out what happened while you’re hooking up to the next machine, pulling, and sparking up a Cuban. If you need more C4, there’s a free stash of the stuff in the back of Yasmani’s. You can also top up at any Ammunation.
A Simple Trick for Faster ATM Robberies GTA 6 https://t.co/lo6aWdupew
— LUCKY (@Badboy1B) November 25, 2026
Players have been trying to find ways to make quick money in GTA 6 since launch, but most of them are boring exploits. This, though, I can get onboard with because it’s just playing the game as intended in an efficient way, and it’s great fun to slip in and out without the cops getting a whiff of you.
We’ve got the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide here on IGN, complete with comprehensive walkthroughs up to Chapter 4 , guides for the Optional Missions and Illegal Operations you’ll find in Leonida, and much more. Just getting started in Chapter 1 ? Check out our Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks , and make a note of the Best Free Weapons to Find Early . If you're already driving all around Leonida and want to know everything there is to find and do, see the Leonida interactive map .

pool.titulo: Every Current Model Apple Watch Has Dropped to New Price Lows for Black Friday
pool.resumen: Starts at just $179 for a brand new watch.
pool.contenido:
The Apple Watch is essentially a natural extension of your iPhone and anyone who uses an iPhone, in my opinion, could benefit from an Apple Watch. If you've shied away because of the cost, then these Black Friday deals might change your mind. Every new model - the Apple Watch SE 3, Apple Watch Series 12, and the Apple Watch Ultra 4 - have all dropped to the lowest prices of the year on Amazon. This is a great opportunity to see what you've been missing out.
Black Friday Deal: Apple Watch SE 3 for $179 The latest generation Apple Watch SE just dropped to its lowest price ever. For Black Friday, Amazon is offering the Apple Watch SE 3 starting at just $179 with free shipping for the 40mm model after a 30% off instant discount. The Apple Watch SE has nearly all of the essential watch, tracker, and fitness functions of the Apple Watch Series 12 at nearly half the price.
The Apple Watch SE 3 was released back in September of 2025. It's Apple's least expensive Apple Watch. Despite its low price tag, it's stylish and boasts great build quality with a 100% recycled aluminum case and Ion-X scratch resistant glass face. It comes in both 40mm and 44mm case sizes. The always-on Retina OLED LTPO display features a pixel density of 326ppi and up to 1,000 nits of peak brightness. The Apple Watch SE uses the same S10 processor used in the Apple Watch Series 11 , which is only one generation older. The only difference is that the Apple Watch SE isn't equipped with the second gen Ultra Wideband chip for Precision Finding.
Black Friday Deal: Apple Watch Series 12 for $299 The Apple Watch Series 12 , which was released in September 2026, has also hit a new price low. The base 42mm GPS model just dropped below $300 for the first time since its launch. The Series 12 comes with a host of incremental upgrades including the S11 processor, Health Sensing System heart rate chcker, Audio Intelligence, and more.
The Apple Watch Series 12 is the best smartwatch for most iOS users . It's stylish, boasts excellent build quality, and seamlessly integrates with your iPhone. It's loaded with tons of practical health and fitness features, including activity tracking and heart rate monitoring. There are a number of notable upgrades over the previous generation model. The biggest one is the new Apple S11 chip with 4GB of RAM. Also new to the Series 12 is Audio Intelligence, which can automatically identify sounds and music as well as record and recap conversations. Other upgrades include a Health Sensing System that checks your heart rate every 5 seconds, HRV tracking, and daily "Readiness" score.
Black Friday Deal: Apple Watch Ultra 4 for $650 The Apple Watch Ultra 4 was also released on September 18 alongside the Series 12. It's $150 off for Black Friday and is the first major discount I've seen for Apple's newest flagship watch. Upgrades over the previous generation include a newer S11 chip with increased 4GB of RAM and longer 50-hour battery life. Like the Apple Watch Series 12, the Ultra now supports Audio Intelligence and the Health Sensing System with "Readiness" score. It still features the same 49mm titanium case, 1.89" always-on Retina LTPO3 OLED display with 3,000nits of peak brightness protected by a sapphire crystal face, and 100m water resistance.
Can you use an Apple Watch with Android phones? Although it's technically possible to use an Apple Watch with an Android phone, we wouldn't recommend it. Apple made it so that a lot of the functionality of the Apple Watch requires a smartphone with an iOS operating system. There are some workarounds to implement some of its features, but for the average person, the hassle is not worth it. If you're absolutely intent on getting an Apple Watch, then getting an iPhone first would be the best option.

pool.titulo: Watching TV in GTA 6 Is More Depressing Than Fun, Except for One Show
pool.resumen: GTA 6's TV content is impressive on a technical level, but apart from one standout show, it's not all that fun to actually watch.
pool.contenido:
It seems there’s almost nothing you can’t do in Grand Theft Auto VI, other than solicit prostitutes . Far more than just being a murder and crime spree simulator, the game allows you to kick back and do everything from play basketball to remodel your house to work out at the gym. And yes, that long list of side activities includes watching television.
GTA 6 includes multiple channels of original programming , featuring everything from breaking Vice City news reports to Adult Swim-style animated sitcoms to cheesy telenovelas. As with so much about the new game, the level of detail Rockstar undertook here is impressive. But despite all that, I found that actually sitting down to watch TV in-game wasn’t quite the entertaining experience I was hoping for. If anything, it was a little depressing.
Weazel News: Satire or Sad Reality? To recap, there are three live TV channels in GTA 6 - the Fox News-spoofing Weazel News, the Telemundo parody Megamundo, and the travel-focused Visit Leonida. For the purposes of this piece, I’m mostly focusing on the former channel. Megamundo is a fun sendup of traditional Spanish-language soap operas, but not having any real attachment to that genre, it’s a joke that only has so much mileage for me. And Visit Leonida is definitely the most limited of the three channels.
With Weazel News, you have a smorgasbord of faux-TV content, all of which focuses on lampooning the right-wing news sector, reality TV, and general American culture. This stream cycles through various breaking news reports, a mockumentary-style series called “The Tyrone Show,” and several different animated sitcoms. And commercials. Dozens and dozens of satirical commercials for all sorts of in-universe products and services.
Initially, you can’t help but sit back and admire the sheer effort that went into making all this content. The TV channels are a very minor feature in the game, and I’m sure many people won’t even really pay attention to them amid all the other countless side activities. The simple fact that you can spend literal hours just sitting in front of a fake TV and not really see any repeat content is impressive.
But once the initial novelty wears off, watching TV isn’t what I’d describe as one of the more rewarding pastimes in GTA 6. Weazel News actually left me feeling a bit stressed out and unhappy after a while. It was hard to put my finger on it at first, but I think what it comes down to is that the political and social satire hits a little too close to home.
For a Scottish-based studio, Rockstar North is generally pretty adept at satirizing American culture with these games - whether it’s remixing the best elements of classic crime films or lampooning the average American’s love of fast food, beer, and guns. You get a heaping helping of all of that with Weazel TV, particularly in the many faux-commercials where colorful characters hawk various brands of alcohol or campaign for a missile launcher in every home or what have you.
The problem is that this material no longer feels as outlandish as it once might have. The sad truth is that real life in the US moved beyond parody at some point in the last 10-15 years. It’s something that a lot of sources of satire have dealt with lately, from South Park to The Onion. How do you top reality when reality has become so unhinged and unbelievable?
GTA’s TV content is in the same boat. A lot of it doesn’t feel particularly far removed from reality anymore. There really are people unironically spouting the same kind of jingoistic nonsense you see in these fake commercials. Between extreme right-wing news channels and the digital hellscape that is social media, there’s a real cultural brain rot that’s taken hold. Watching Weazel TV is more an uncomfortable reminder of where we are as a society than a truly unbelievable parody.
That’s part of it, anyway. The other issue is that some of the Weazel TV humor feels a bit unnecessarily mean-spirited, particularly anything involving the news broadcasts and Tyrone’s sexually charged misadventures. Rockstar really goes all-in on the “Florida Man” humor, mirroring the sorts of kooky regional headlines and weird characters we’ve all read about online. Through the fictionalized state of Leonida, it paints the real Florida as this unending wasteland of deranged hillbillies and unrepentant criminals. And, yes, Florida has more than its fair share of odd residents, but many perfectly lovely people live there also.
Some of the Weazel TV humor feels a bit unnecessarily mean-spirited, particularly anything involving the news broadcasts and Tyrone’s sexually charged misadventures. I always look to King of the Hill as the gold standard when it comes to satirizing a specific American subculture. That animated sitcom is a clear parody of small-town Texan life, but it never settles for leaning on stereotypes or punching down on its colorful cast of characters. They’re all surprisingly nuanced and fully realized for what might seem at first like a bunch of goofy, beer-chugging rednecks.
GTA’s main cast of characters may get a similarly nuanced treatment, by and large, but the same can’t really be said for the goofballs who appear on Weazel News. Unlike King of the Hill, this TV content does gleefully punch down, and that means it doesn’t fully sit right.
The Joy of Rockstar’s Right Wing That all being said, there is one good reason to keep Jason’s butt planted on the couch and stay tuned to Weazel News. The channel’s animated sitcoms generally do a better job than the other shows when it comes to providing an amusing dose of escapism. It’s easy to picture any one of these shows having a run on Adult Swim in between reruns of Rick and Morty, whether it’s the stoner humor-focused Macca & Friends or the aggressively copaganda-minded “children’s program” Barnyard Blue.
But the real success story in this area is definitely Right Wing. Right Wing is basically a superhero cartoon about a dimwitted defender of Truth, Justi

pool.titulo: South Park Season 29 Finale Review: 'City Endings'
pool.resumen: South Park caps off a very uneven Season 29 with the messy but still very enjoyable finale episode "City Endings." Read our full review.
pool.contenido:
Full spoilers ahead for South Park Season 29, Episode 6!
There hasn't been a real, concerted effort to build an overarching narrative in South Park Season 29. Sure, certain plot threads have carried forward, like the arrival of Little Randy and Kenny's latest brush with death, but by and large this season has just drifted from one topic to the next. But that doesn't stop Trey Parker, Matt Stone, and the rest from trying to tie everything together in the finale. It's a pretty messy conclusion - a City Ending, even - but a mostly entertaining one.
As was teased throughout this season, everything culminates with November's big event. Not the US midterms, but the long-awaited arrival of GTA 6. Literally everyone in town is busy playing Rockstar's masterpiece, which makes things kind of awkward when it turns out the majority of South America's power grid is being hijacked by billionaire weenies and their data centers.
I definitely would have preferred a more focused and organic approach to weaving together this season's various storylines, but I do appreciate the effort to tie it all together here at the end. "City Endings" does a pretty good job of lampooning all the AI-related headlines that have swirled as of late, from the Jensen Huang/AMD situation to the recent spate of technical meltdowns. It's especially fitting that we see the characters collectively lose their minds over imagined Chinese cyberattacks rather than look inward and realize the problem is coming from inside the house.
It doesn't hurt that the show swings back around to focus on Mr. Kim and the latest evolution of City Wok, which has now been transformed from a clearing house for crappy e-bikes to a sordid massage parlor. It's pretty amusing to watch Kim frantically run around trying to "please" his growing lineup of customers while his disinterested wife goofs off in the back. I complain a lot about the series regurgitating the same jokes over and over, but here I think there's a nice sense of escalation over the course of the episode. I'll also be curious to see if the ending holds and whether Kim returns from his little sojourn in space.
"City Endings" also makes solid use of Butters and his family, as we see how thoroughly corrupted Butters has become thanks to his proximity to power and wealth. We get a fun little parody of The Twilight Zone episode "It's a Good Life," at least until Butters is exposed. That's a great way of paying off on the whole antivax subplot from earlier in the season. There's even a hilariously sad little bit involving Peter and his hapless attempt to insert himself into the Kenny-shaped hole in the group.
Read IGN's South Park Season 29 Reviews Episode 1: "South American Biker Gangs" Episode 2: "Billionaire Weenietown" Episode 3: "You Like That On Your Face" Episode 4: "Guinea Pig on a Stick" Episode 5: "We Be Clubbin'" Again, this episode is nothing if not chaotic in its attempts to weave all of Season 29's ongoing threads together. There are certain things I would have liked to see more payoff for, including the Little Randy of it all (is this just the ongoing status quo for that character now?). I also felt the Kenny subplot deserved a little more focus than it receives here. But despite those concerns, "City Endings" works as a largely satisfying conclusion to a very uneven season of South Park. And now we don't have to refer to the show as "South America" any longer.

pool.titulo: GTA 6's Cartel Heist Might Be Rockstar's Best Ever Mission, But Only If You Do It Badly
pool.resumen: GTA 6's chapter three heist might be Rockstar's best ever mission, but only if you do it badly.
pool.contenido:
Warning: This article contains spoilers for chapter three of GTA 6.
Chapter 3 of GTA 6 ends with a bang. It’s arguably Rockstar’s greatest ever mission and a culmination of every bank job the developer has designed since GTA 4’s Three Leaf Clover burst onto the scene. A daring raid on the Sinfrontera National Bank in downtown Vice City, what starts out as a slick operation quickly goes haywire, resulting in shootouts with armored police, helicopters chasing a bus that has had the roof ripped off, and the death of one of your gang members.
The funny thing is, you may be reading that and thinking that’s not what happened to you at all. That’s because the back half of The Cartel Heist can go in wildly different directions. You can do it much more cleanly, but it’s nowhere near as fun. Sorry, Nicole.
A lot has to go in your favour to execute the perfect heist. Making sure you correctly prep is key, meaning you’ll have to extract all of the info possible out of Monty when he’s dangling over reptilian teeth, protect Pete’s shipment of weapons correctly, and plant enough explosives on the cell towers. Then there’s also everything you have to get going your way inside the mission itself, which is mainly tied to not wasting time and nailing the vault minigame. You can get the full details on everything you’ll need to do, step-by-step, on our excellent guides page .
Nail it, and your getaway driver will turn up as planned by the underground entrance; you’ll load up the truck with stacks of cash and simply drive off undetected. There are obvious benefits to doing this. Not only is there the satisfaction of pulling off such a complex job cleanly, but you’ll earn $150,000 from it, rather than the $100,000 you’d otherwise get, plus Nicole, your charming safecracking tutor, will survive. What you will miss out on, though, is one of Rockstar’s finest blockbuster sequences.
It makes Three Leaf Clover firmly look like the first draft that it was back in 2008. The path truly branches once you leave the bank’s vault, but in all truth, your fate has likely been long sealed by that point. You’ll have needed to keep a keen eye on your time in the bottom right corner and have made sure all ten bundles of bills have been secured by the time the alarm goes off and all hell breaks loose. That’s when things kick up a notch, and legions of Vice City police and NOOSE enforcers turn up at the front doors. A lobby shootout commences, with enemies turning up from all directions in an effort to stop you from leaving with your haul. It's a fantastic encounter that borders on sensory overload thanks to the rattle of gunfire, thick smoke, and blaring alarms.
The slick transitions between characters only add to the sense of cinema, with Lucia throwing a smoke grenade launcher up to the balcony for Jason to catch, punctuated by a highly satisfying second or two of slow motion. This elegantly moves the action onto the streets, allowing you to get a glimpse of the full challenge awaiting you and your gang outside. Michael Mann’s Heat has long been an influence on Grand Theft Auto, but never has the sensation of watching the movie’s signature heist been replicated as well as it has here. It makes Three Leaf Clover firmly look like the first draft that it was back in 2008.
As the fight moves outdoors, Raul’s backup plan comes to fruition with Karim arriving behind the wheel of a public bus. Up to this point in GTA 6’s story, the heist leader has remained a mysterious presence, slinking in and out of scenes with an undeniable air of cool. It’s not until now, though, that we get to see him in full flow, leading with calm authority. He’s quickly become one of my favourite characters across the whole Grand Theft Auto series — embodying the swagger and ruthless execution of a lusciously long-maned Danny Ocean.
Of course, it would all be too simple for everyone to walk onto the bus and drive off into the sunset. Lucia, Raul, Andrea, and Karim all make it on board, but have to make the tough decision to leave without Jason and Nicole. Having to find an alternative escape route, it calls on Jason to flex all of his military muscles and escort Nicole to safety. Bleeding out thanks to a gunshot to the stomach, she makes it to a SWAT van that Jason takes the wheel of. The chase is on.
GTA 6’s big-scale missions are when the dynamic player-switching really comes into its own. Before we know it, we’re back on the bus and having to hold off cars, trucks, and helicopters as Lucia from the back seat. Nothing can prevent the roof from being torn off by some hooks from a nearby truck, though, in what might be the whole mission’s most jaw-dropping moment. It’s just pure flexing from Rockstar at this point, and I’m all for it. Not only does it add to the spectacle, but it makes you rethink how to take down your pursuers due to your cover being violently rearranged.
All of that prep work you did on previous missions may not have led to you getting the perfect heist escape, but it still has its benefits here. Manage to protect all of the weapons cargo provided by Pete? You’ll get a very fun grenade launcher to wield here and blow away the opposition with. The number of variables within this mission is staggering, and a real showcase of how the little choices you make as Jason and Lucia affect their story. The whole of chapter three has been building up to this moment, and knowing that every step before it actually meant something makes it all the more rewarding.
One final character switch is then made, with Jason tasked with catching up with the bus and getting both him and Nicole on board. pool.titulo: The Rings of Power Season 3 Ending Explained With Showrunners J. D. Payne and Patrick McKay
pool.resumen: The Rings of Power Season 3 just ended, so showrunners J. D. Payne and Patrick McKay break down everything that happened - and what to expect next.
pool.contenido:
Spoilers follow for The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3.
The last frame of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 focuses on Sauron (Charlie Vickers) looking straight to camera as he bows before the crowing King Pharazôn (Trystan Gravelle) and the very sober-looking elves Galadriel (Morfydd Clark), Celeborn (Jamie Campbell Bower) and Gil-galad (Benjamin Walker). A slight smirk has never been more dangerous.
With the fourth season of The Rings of Power confirmed, series creators and showrunners J. D. Payne and Patrick McKay spoke with IGN to preview what’s coming in Season 4 and beyond. From the Galadriel/Celeborn/Sauron triangle to Queen Miriel’s (Cynthia Addai-Robinson) sacrifices that seem for naught to Gandalf’s future trials and beyond, the two break down how Middle-earth will fare in the planned last two seasons.
More From Middle-earth
The Rings of Power Season 3 Finale Recap and Review Showrunner Explains the ‘Different Side’ of Simon Pegg’s Balrog: It ‘Actually Is True to the Books’ Rings of Power Stars React to Those Big Season 3 Deaths Where the Rings Are at the Start of Rings of Power Season 3 The Rushed Rings of Power Episode Release Schedule Explained Breaking Down Theo's Shock Moment in Rings of Power Season 3 The Rings of Power: Season 3 Ending Explained Payne told IGN that they settled on Sauron’s last look for the season early on, despite mulling whether they should close on the forging of the One Ring instead. “There was maybe a half a second where we said, ‘Gosh, the forging of the ring is such a climactic moment. Should we end the season there and then let all the next season be about Númenór?’” he said. “Very quickly we were like, ‘No, no, no!’ You want to actually give all the other storylines a chance to coalesce. You had Gandalf out in the east working to try to take the Dark Wizard either off the field or onto his side. And Númenór in the west are figuring out their civil war and Pharazôn and Miriel's marriage. We felt like if we ended on the forging of the ring, you would feel a little frustrated.”
McKay added that they wanted to downplay this finale after two seasons of massive, action-centric season endings. “We wanted a season that was tighter, tauter, more psychological,” he explained. “And we have this great moment from mythology – that Sauron surrendered with a plan of a longer game.
Sauron falls to his knees in front of the army. ... We were just like, ‘Let's stop right there and leave them hanging.’ “Now, that's scary as showrunners making a show in 2026,” McKay admitted. “Are people going to be like, ‘Wait, what ?’ I think that's still scary. Reactions are just coming in right now. But we also felt that it was bold, and we hadn't seen it before. When we were really [story-]beating out the very ending of the season, Sauron falls to his knees in front of the army — that image felt so strong. We were just like, ‘Let's stop right there and leave them hanging.’ It felt like a satisfying ending.”
The Fall of Númenór A huge event in the Second Age of Middle-earth is the Fall of Númenór to Sauron, and McKay and Payne confirm that that train is now on the tracks.
“It’s a real opportunity to show a civilizational decline,” Payne said of what’s to come. “Fall is one of Tolkien's recurring themes [that] he goes back to again and again. We've already seen the cracks in Númenór. We know they're there, so how do you exploit those to get the mightiest empire of men that has ever existed and totally take them off the map?”
Without spoiling, Payne said they’re very excited to show it in a “multifaceted way,” along with its effect on many different characters and storylines. But there’s also the interpersonal drama to come between Pharazôn and Sauron. In prior seasons, audiences have already seen the Dark Lord pick apart Galadriel and others, so how will Pharazôn be undone?
“Pharazôn is a very skilled and savvy manipulator in his own right,” Payne said of the King. “He's a massive politician. He's one who is always looking seven moves down the chessboard and trying to figure out how to outsmart his adversary. When you get two snakes in a barrel, each one trying to outmaneuver the other one and look ahead, how is Sauron able to concoct a lose-lose scenario that even someone as savvy as Pharazôn might fall prey to?”
McKay was also gleeful about it. “The idea of putting Charlie Vickers and Trystan Gravelle on a collision course — that's a potent mix. Those are two very exciting actors with very different approaches, playing very different kinds of characters. We're pretty excited.”
Also in that Númenórean psychological soup is the sacrificial Queen Miriel, who only married Pharazôn to join his army with her Faithful in order to bring down Sauron. And now the Dark Lord is coming home with them?
“It is a terrible compromise she has made, but one that she believes is the best given everything on her plate,” McKay pointed out. “She's trying to save her people and save the world, and she's sacrificing herself in the process. Now extrapolate – what does that person do when Sauron's here with the influence he's having? There's two things that person could do. They could continue doubling down and trying to fix it, digging the hole even deeper to protect her people. Or she could say, ‘I'm out.’ I think if you look at Cynthia's amazing performance and the journey this character has been on, it's going to be a rough road ahead for the Queen. The Queen has a big story next season. Everyone in Númenór does.”
The Galadriel/Sauron/Celeborn Triangle In Season 1, Sauron/Halbrand really created a connection with Galadriel, and his betrayal has continued to pull on both of them through Season 3. With the return of the long-lost Celeborn this season, a choice was made. In the finale, the married elves chose one another, but Sauron was clearly looking right at Galadriel when he took the knee for Pharazôn.

pool.titulo: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth Director David Fincher Sparks Backlash for 'Wildly Dystopian' Vision of AI-powered Filmmaking
pool.resumen: Director David Fincher has sparked a backlash after setting out what some have called a “dystopian” vision for AI-fueled filmmaking, amid controversy over AI use in Netflix movie The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.
pool.contenido:
Director David Fincher has sparked a backlash after setting out what some have called a “dystopian” vision for AI-fueled filmmaking, amid controversy over AI use in Netflix movie The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth .
Fincher, who directed Seven, Fight Club, and The Curious Case of Benjamin Button, has reunited with long-term collaborator Brad Pitt for The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, which was written by Quentin Tarantino. It is a standalone sequel and spinoff to Tarantino’s Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, with Pitt reprising his role as stunt double Cliff Booth.
In a recent interview with Sean Fennessey on The Ringer’s Big Picture podcast , Fincher confirmed that he used AI to sync the best take of a line reading with the best performance take when they didn’t align on camera, in order to speed up production by cutting down the number of takes needed. Essentially, he used AI to replace dialogue and adjust actors’ lip movements in post-production.
“We could use AI to re-lip that thing,” he said. “So it was freeing, it was the freeing up of… think of this entirely plastically. We’re not chiseling this out of marble. We’re working with plasticine. You know what I mean? Just giving ourselves that freedom to go, ‘what is the best thing on the eye, and then what is the best thing on the ear,’ and f***ing do not worry about how we’re going to get there, because we will figure out a way. And we did, in most cases. I think there’s a couple of shots [that] didn’t quite work, but they’re getting there. By the time it’s on service.”
Fincher added that the actors spent just a handful of days re-recording dialogue. Dialogue replacement was just 5% conventionally done, the rest “all AI.”
But it was his comments made later in the interview, where Fincher described how he sees directing with AI going in the future, that have sparked the most vociferous response.
Here’s the relevant section in full:
“I’m imagining — and what I’ve seen with AI technology — I’m imagining a world in the next year where everything that humans do great, like sculpting, painting, ageing, blowing fake spider’s webs into the corner, smoking up a volume, putting a shaft of light in it, putting a crazy f***ing wig on somebody, doing all their makeup… like, I can imagine a world where — and I don’t think we’re far away — you hire all the same people. And you walk into a set that’s beautifully handcrafted, and you hire all those people, and you shoot the master. You shoot the master 20, 25 times till you get it worked out exactly. And you’re doing surface capture at the exact same time that you’re filming. And then you go in and you sit all the actors in chairs wherever they land, and they perform from the clavicles up, same scene, but you move the crew. The crew’s now moving to the next stage, they’re pre-lighting that, they’re getting that ready.
“So essentially, the filmmaking process is about just shooting the masters. And all of the iteration, the over-shoulders, the close-ups, all that stuff is derived from the material that you do sitting in a chair after everyone leaves.
“And then, the part that seems to provoke such a violent, vitriolic response in people — ‘Oh my God, he made me do it 20 times!’ — it’s like, now I don’t need to do that, because I won’t miss focus in AI. And I will land a stick the dolly shot in AI. And I will be able to make sure that that hair doesn’t cross right in front of your cornea in AI.
“And it’ll still be based on real human beings, and it’ll still be based on real human — the way humans move and how they traverse a set and however they pull up their trousers before they sit down or take their coat off — all that stuff will be there, but people will only have to do it 15 times.”
In the interview, Fennessey then asked: “Does working that way appeal to you?”
“Totally,” Fincher replied.
Fincher’s comments were roundly criticized on social media, where people hit out at not just the heavy use of AI in The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, but the prospect of seeing a performance from the likes of Brad Pitt that isn’t real.
“David Lynch: The camera accidentally caught a crew member in the mirror so I incorporated him into the story and ended up with one of the most memorable characters in TV and movie history,” writer and critic David Hering said in a post on social media . “David Fincher: I spent $400m to change the shape of Brad Pitt’s mouth when he says ‘hello.’”
“Any movie that uses even a sliver of AI should be immediately disqualified from awards consideration,” said another person . “Disgusting.”
“Saying, ‘I wanna take an actor’s eye movement from Take 1 with an actors lip movement from Take 3’…that’s not the performance the actor gave on set! You don’t get to create the perfect performance by Frankenstein-ing a ‘perfect version’ of the performance and call it directing,” actor Mike Kalinowski commented .
“I’m not saying Fincher is not an incredible director. But he’s also known for doing an ungodly amount of takes to get exactly what he wants. But you’re when you’re working with actors, it’s never gonna be perfect. That’s what makes it art.”
One person called Fincher’s proposed production process “wildly dystopian,” another “depressing as f**k.” Another quipped: “there is no longer a need for David Fincher.” "Imagine doing 135 takes just to be asked back for an ADR session where the Ben Grokfleck Machine updates your lips," another said .
“Fincher's vision of a largely A.I. production is undeniably bleak but I suspect people would be less perplexed if it was more widely understood (as a friend remarked to me recently) that Fincher's filmmaking process was always more about control than perfection,” writer Brendan Hodges said .

pool.titulo: Here Are the Top Black Friday 4K TV Deals You Don't Want to Miss, From Budget to Best
pool.resumen: Deals start on Thanksgiving day.
pool.contenido:
Whether you're looking for the TV with the best image quality and you've got money to spend, or you've got a tight budget and value is paramount, Black Friday has got you covered. If you're planning to upgrade to OLED this year, you'll find a deal for it. If you're looking for something bigger, like a 75" or dare I say 100", you'll find a deal for that too.
The Best Black Friday TV Deals
The Best Black Friday Budget TV Deal 65" model for $299.99 (was $550) 75" model for $379.99 (was $700) If you're looking for an affordable TV that offers solid image quality, the Hisense QD5 is hard to beat. For Black Friday, you can pick up a 55" model for under $200 or a 75" model for under $400. This 2026 Hisense TV offers great image quality that punches above its weight class thanks to Hisense's proprietary Hi-QLED panel with direct-lit LED backlighting. The QD5 officially supports a number of HDR formats including HDR10, Dolby Vision, and HLG. Roku smart interface is also integrated, which is considered one of the best built-in smart interfaces you can get from a budget TV. It's definitely a favorite of mine; I prefer it over Google TV and Fire TV.
The Best Black Friday Budget Samsung TV Deal Not everyone feels comfortable buying a TV brand that isn't Samsung, LG, or Sony (although, technically, Sony TVs are now made by TCL). In that case, the best budget TV deal from one of these brands is easily the Samsung M80H TV . This is a new 2026 model TV that features a mini LED panel and a native 144Hz refresh rate so you can play supported PlayStation 5, Xbox, and PC games at up to 144fps. The 65" TV is currently less than $500 and you can't find many (any?) TVs in that price range that offer this level of features and a Samsung/LG/Sony brand name.
The Best OLED TV Deal (so far) LG's most popular OLED TV is on sale for Black Friday. Amazon currently has the 65" LG Evo C6 4K OLED TV for $1,349.99 with free delivery. To be perfectly honest, I think this is a rather lukewarm Black Friday price for LG's current model C-series OLED TV. There's a possibility that if you wait a couple of days, a better deal will drop. That said, this is the lowest straight-up price I've seen so far this year by $50.
The C6 is LG's current 2026 model in the LG's C-series OLED TV lineup. LG's C-series OLED TV in general has been our favorite TVs for console gaming for many years thanks to its outstanding image quality, low input lag, and high refresh rate. This is one of the best TVs you can get for streaming 4K HDR content in its intended glory. It boasts the near-infinite black levels, near-infinite contrast ratio, and near-instantaneous response times you'd expect from any OLED TV. The C6 is also equipped with modern gaming features including a native 120Hz panel that can be pushed to as high as 165Hz, HDMI 2.1 inputs, variable refresh rate and auto low latency mode.
The Hisense UR8 RGB Mini-LED TV Gives OLED a Run for Its Money Last year, Hisense pioneered the first RGB Mini-LED TV with its 116UX model. Granted it was only available as a massive 116" screen that retailed for $20,000. In 2026, Hisense released its second generation RGB Mini-LED tech at a much more affordable price point with its UR-series lineup. For Black Friday, you can get it for even less. Best Buy has just discounted the 65" Hisense UR8 RGB Mini-LED TV from $2,000 all the way down to $899.99 and the 75" model from $2,500 down to $1399.99, both with free delivery. These are the lowest prices since launch and beats previous lows by $200.
RGB Mini-LED is an evolution of Mini-LED technology. Traditional mini-LED TVs consist of an array of blue LED that are passed through RGB filters to produced the desired color. RGB Mini-LED TVs use red, green, and blue LEDs instead of just blue, which means the pixels no longer need filters to produce the desired color. The result is more accurate color reproduction, less blooming and, most importantly, a wider color gamut. Color gamut of RGB Mini-LED surpasses that of OLEDs, since current-generation OLEDs also use color filters combined with blue OLEDs. How does that translate in the real world? It means that you see richer, more accurate colors, smoother gradients and less banding than even OLEDs.
TCL introduces its own SQD mini LED tech in the QM8L TV 75" model for $1,397.99 (was $3,000) 85" model for $2,297.99 (was $4,000) 98" model for $2,997.99 (was $6,000) One of the best new TVs of 2026 dropped to its lowest price ever ahead of Black Friday. The QM8L is a pretty significant upgrade over last year's QM8K model thanks to the introduction of TCL's highly-touted SQD technology. SQD - which stands for Super Quantum Dot - is a more refined version of QLED tech. Quantum dot panels have a layer of microscopic crystals measuring a few nanometers in size that are able to separate light into precise colors. SQD tech uses even smaller crystals - as small as a single nanometer in width. This allows SQD panels to pack in even more dimming zones, usually numbering in the thousands, which in turn produces a brighter image with higher contrast and richer colors.

pool.contenido:
Summary Grammy Award winner Lenny Kravitz makes his World of Assassination debut as Bawma, the Pirate King of Aleph from 007 First Light , in The Mutiny, a new Elusive Target available starting today through December 24. For once, the client briefs Agent 47 personally, as Bawma guides him across Ambrose Island to deal with three rogue lieutenants, and a set of Voodoo Dolls offers one of the most creative ways to take them down. The mission is free for new players via the Free Demo and for all HITMAN World of Assassination players, and launches alongside the new Rockstar Pack.
Agent 47 has a new client, and he isn’t usually the type to stay in the shadows. HITMAN World of Assassination’s latest Elusive Target, The Mutiny, stars Lenny Kravitz as Bawma, the magnetic and unpredictable Pirate King of Aleph, first brought to life in 007 First Light . Kravitz lends both his likeness and his voice to the character, who crosses over into the World of Assassination for the first time.
The Mutiny Elusive Target mission is available globally on Xbox Series X|S, Xbox One, ROG Xbox Ally X, ROG Xbox Ally, and PC starting Thursday, November 26, through Thursday, December 24, 2026.
From the opening briefing, it’s clear this assignment is unusual. Diana never lets a client brief 47 directly, but Bawma has paid the Agency generously and insists on directing the operation himself. Little is known about the man behind the alias: intelligence suggests he was raised as a child soldier before building Aleph, a sprawling black-market hub in the Western Hemisphere that he calls his kingdom.
Now he’s hiding out on Ambrose Island, and 47’s objective is simple: find Bawma, make contact, and await further instructions.
Once 47 tracks Bawma down through the island’s ruins and jungles, it soon becomes clear that something far more valuable is at stake. Three of Bawma’s rogue lieutenants stand in the way, and none of them will part with what they’re holding easily.
Bawma stays in 47’s ear throughout the mission, and with its bright, upbeat tone and easygoing holiday feel, The Mutiny is one of the most laid-back contracts in the World of Assassination. On Ambrose Island, though, nothing is ever straightforward, and fortune favors the bold.
Bold players will want to pay a visit to Madame Serafine. All three targets can be eliminated with a Voodoo Doll: gather the ingredients, add them to the Ritual Bowl, and pick up the doll Madame Serafine creates.
Then “kill” the doll to take out its target, whether that means stabbing it with a knife, throwing it in water, shooting it or blowing it up, hitting it with a thrown sharp object, or exposing it to fire or electricity.
As with all Elusive Targets, The Mutiny will be removed from the game when it expires on December 24. However, players who own HITMAN World of Assassination or the Ambrose Island location will keep access to The Retaliator, the Arcade version of the mission, as well as its Special Assignment, completely for free.
Players who complete The Mutiny with an IOI Account while it’s live will also unlock the Rock Royalty Duck, a regal rubber duck in flashy sunglasses that detonates when it detects nearby motion.
Launching alongside The Mutiny, IO Interactive is also releasing the Rockstar Pack, a collection of outfits, weapons, gear, and Freelancer Safehouse cosmetics inspired by the bold style and electric energy of rock ’n’ roll icons. The pack is available for $5.99/€5.99/£4.99 and includes:

pool.titulo: Aspects of GTA 6 are inspired by Red Dead Redemption 2's honor system because its player agency 'was a hard thing to ignore and walk away from'
pool.resumen: "As the resolution goes up, you want the sophistication of the experience to go up."
pool.contenido:
Grand Theft Auto 6 doesn't just mark a huge, and at times unbelievable, step forward for graphics; it's also at the forefront of what an open world game can be, just look at the existential crisis it's given Cyberpunk 2's creative director . With thousands of enterable buildings , unpredictable and slightly scary NPCs , and systems that help you determine what kind of criminal you want to be. It all really does feel like a milestone for what videogames can do.
"As the resolution goes up, you want the sophistication of the experience to go up, and obviously the sophistication of the mechanics," Rob Nelson, Rockstar's head of development, says in an interview with Eurogamer. "So it just naturally flowed that we give players choices to interact with the world beyond just violence, beyond just 'down the barrel of a gun', because it's fun."
The sophisticated mechanics that Nelson is talking about here pertains to GTA 6's Criminal Profile , a system that evaluates your escapades across Leonida and gives you a rating. There's Professional, Hardened, Violent, Psycho, and Irredeemable. The more stealthy and non-lethal you are, the higher your profile will be. It's similar to Red Dead Redemption 2's Honor System .
"There was maybe more emotional resonance in the story of RDR2 than we had, certainly in a GTA before," Nelson says. "So we liked that idea. We didn't necessarily come to GTA 6 going: 'We must have emotional resonance,' but all of those things combine. It's more that those systems and that element of player choice and agency, and the way that affected the narrative, was a hard thing to ignore and walk away from."
Nelson explains that most of the groundwork started as "simple things" in principle, "but they create a lot more work in terms of development of the sophistication of the systems." It's all about choice in GTA 6. You choose whether you want to be a criminal with a conscience or a loose cannon.
"It's still a world of violence, but you could threaten somebody by aiming a gun at them and just robbing them, and they have a chance to comply. So you don't have to beat them to death to get their money."
The part that sticks out the most is that you "don't have to" approach crimes in a certain way, there's still the option to go into every encounter guns blazing because redemption only works from a storytelling perspective when it's the player's choice, and not as Nelson puts it, something that is "foisted upon you".
"You can still go on those rampages and basically smash your Criminal Profile until it breaks," Nelson adds. "And then you enter this irredeemable state, which basically says, 'I reject your criminal profile system! I don't want it.'"
Am I brave enough to reject the criminal profile system entirely? Hell no. I replay sections of dialogue if I accidentally upset someone, and cannot do an "evil run" of a game without giving myself stomach ulcers because of the guilt — but I appreciate having the option.

pool.titulo: Rockstar workers vote overwhelmingly against union recognition
pool.resumen: The IWGB says efforts will continue, but with only 25% of Rockstar workers voting in favor, there's a long way to go.
pool.contenido:
After two weeks of voting that bracketed the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, Rockstar Games employees have voted overwhelmingly against a recognition agreement with the IWGB Game Workers Union.
25% of Rockstar employees voted in favor of the recognition agreement, the union said, while 75% voted against it. 1,544 employees took part in the vote, representing a turnout of just over 93%.
Rockstar workers actually founded a union earlier this year—the Rockstar Game Workers Union, a subsidiary of the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain—and it will continue to operate as it has. The IWGB said the outcome will not prevent Rockstar workers from organizing or exercising union rights, but the company will not be required to regularly meet with union representatives for collective bargaining or other relevant matters.
Despite the vote, the union said it will continue with organizing efforts at Rockstar.
"For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society—this isn’t a sign to retreat, it’s a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues," the IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union said. "We’re ready to put in the effort to make that happen.
"Whilst we haven’t emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for new kinds of conversation to start happening. People entirely unfamiliar with unions were for the first time debating employment conditions, collective bargaining rights, and our contracts. We heard from many more colleagues about what mattered to them, and we hope people will continue to engage so that we can see where these new discussions can lead us."
The power to shape our working lives has always been, and always will be, in our hands
— @iwgbunion.bsky.social ( @iwgbunion.bsky.social.bsky.social ) 2026-11-26T16:08:25.065Z In a separate statement, Rockstar head of publishing Jennfer Kolbe said the studio is "extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we've built together and the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6."
"This result reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong," Kolbe said. "As we look ahead, we're excited to build on all we've accomplished together."
Rockstar, which said it worked with the IWGB to ensure employees were able to make an informed decision in a fair and transparent vote, came under fire in October 2025 for firing more than 30 employees, all of whom were members of a private trade union Discord channel. The IWGB called it " the most ruthless act of union busting in the history of the UK games industry ," while Rockstar says they were fired for leaking information about "upcoming and unannounced games." That matter is now before an employment tribunal ; closing submissions were made last week.

pool.titulo: Rockstar Games Issues Statement as Union Vote Fails
pool.resumen: The Rockstar Games union vote has failed, with 75% voting against a recognition agreement with the IWGB Game Workers Union.
pool.contenido:
The Rockstar Games union vote has failed, with 75% voting against a recognition agreement with the IWGB Game Workers Union.
The shock result comes following the hugely successful launch of GTA 6 , which has set records as the biggest entertainment launch of all time.
Workers at Rockstar Games voted 25% in favour of and 75% against a recognition agreement with the IWGB. The terms of the recognition deal were agreed following months of negotiations that took place even as the IWGB and Rockstar clashed over the firing of 31 workers for allegedly leaking company secrets in October last year. The IWGB has alleged the workers were unlawfully fired, and have accused Rockstar Games of union busting. The vote overlapped with the closing submissions of the employment tribunal, which ended earlier this month. Judgement is currently pending.
If the IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union had won the vote, it would have become the biggest recognised union in the UK games industry.
The ballot saw 93.2% turnout, with 1,544 employees across Rockstar’s UK sites in Edinburgh, Leeds, Lincoln, Dundee, and London participating. 1,163 team members voted against IWGB recognition (75.3%), while 381 voted in favour (24.7%).
In a statement issued to IGN, Rockstar Games head of publishing, Jennifer Kolbe, said the company was “extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we've built together and the launch of GTA 6.”
“This result reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong,” Kolbe continued. “As we look ahead, we're excited to build on all we've accomplished together.”
The IWGB insisted that Rockstar workers would keep organizing without a formal union recognition deal after the ballot.
The IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union shared the following statement:
“For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society — this isn’t a sign to retreat, it’s a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. We’re ready to put in the effort to make that happen.
“Whilst we haven’t emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for new kinds of conversation to start happening. People entirely unfamiliar with unions were for the first time debating employment conditions, collective bargaining rights, and our contracts. We heard from many more colleagues about what mattered to them, and we hope people will continue to engage so that we can see where these new discussions can lead us.
“A recognition agreement would have marked a path towards greater workplace democracy. But it’s one route of many. At Rockstar we have already won, and will continue to win, tangible changes that improve our everyday lives. We’ll keep fighting for a say. For pay transparency, contractual overtime pay, and protections against AI and layoffs.
“The power to shape our working lives has always been, and will always be, in our hands.”
Kolbe had indicated Rockstar’s willingness to work with staff on union recognition, recently telling Bloomberg : “We go where the team goes. So if they want a union, they will have a union.”

pool.titulo: Everything You Need To Know Ahead of The Delta Force Invitationals Grand Final
pool.contenido:
After last year’s inaugural event in Hangzhou, this weekend sees the Delta Force Invitational make its first move outside Asia, as an official competitive title at DreamHack in Stockholm, Sweden, from 27th-29th November. The Grand Final of the tournament will take place on November 29th at 11am UTC+0 through to 4pm UTC+0 after three days of global competitive action.
It’s the first Chinese esports title to reach DreamHack, featuring teams that have been selected through a full professional league system. Six regions offered a route to the offline finals, and the twelve squads competing this weekend are as follows:
Americas: Spacestation Gaming and GODL, via the 2026 RISE Series Americas Chinese Mainland: TES, RSG and IBG, via the Delta Force Pro League Korea: Nongshim RedForce, via RISE Series Korea Japan: FENNEL, via the 2026 Delta Force: Invitational Japan Qualifier Pan-Pacific: RX, MKK and ONIC via the Pan-Pacific Operations Cup S2 EMEA: Alliance and Fnatic, via the 2026 RISE Series EMEA
Fnatic are, of course, well known to DreamHack audiences, having won the first League of Legends World Championship there back in 2011, as well as the first CS:GO Major in 2013. Alliance, being a Swedish team, will be playing on home soil, but only time will tell if this gives them an additional boost. They, and the ten other teams to have gone the distance, will once again be competing for a share of a $500,000 prize pool.
One core aspect of Delta Force that’s attracted new fans over the last twelve months is its commitment to extraction as an esport. Whereas in traditional FPS competitions there’s an obvious focus on winning fights, in Delta Force’s Operations mode, information gathering, firefights, resource management and extraction decisions all play out within a single match.
Viewers who tune in to watch on Twitch via @DeltaForceGameOfficial or @DeltaForce_Esports can also bag a bunch of in-game rewards:
15 minutes: Armament Voucher 20 minutes: Calling Card - Delta Force Invitational 30 minutes: Standing Gear Ticket 45 minutes: AKM - Wandering Dragon 60 minutes: Action - Cheer
Plus, GOTAGA, HutchMF, Summit1G, Panda and Timmy will also be streaming the matches on their channels during the event.
There’s also a tonne of in-game incentives around the event, so be sure to login between the 11th November and 3rd December to get your hands on these:
Log in for 1 day during the event - DFI-themed Spray Paint ×1 Log in for a total of 2 days - Elite Gear Ticket ×2 Log in for a total of 3 days - Featured Keycard Copy Pack ×1 Log in for a total of 4 days - Elite Gear Ticket ×2
If you correctly predict the outcome of the Invitational in-game, there’s a couple of other other rewards to be had:
One of your selected teams reaches the Grand Final - Cosmetic Item: ASV - Northern Frontier - Assault Vehicle ×1 One of your selected teams wins the championship - Cosmetic Item: Overtime - AK 12 - Unstoppable (orange-tier weapon)
In the two years since its launch, Delta Force has steadily gained momentum, with developers Team Jade determined to grow the tactical FPS into a globally recognised esports title. With three days of intense competition on the horizon, its future certainly looks bright.
Delta Force is free to play and available now on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Android, iOS, Google Play, Epic Games Store, and Steam.

pool.resumen: Rockstar North has explained why it was so important that GTA 6's big early story reveal stayed under wraps before the game came out.

Warning! This article contains spoilers for the prologue of GTA 6 .
GTA 6’s prologue hides a surprise that somehow managed to stay a secret all the way up to players finding out for themselves. And Rockstar North, it turns out, was praying for it not to leak ahead of launch.
During the game’s opening stretch, the story of how Lucia ends up in a Leonida prison is told. This isn’t the surprising part — ever since GTA 6 Trailer 1 we’ve known she’d end up behind bars at some point — but the person she was at a diner moments before her arrest is. Tomás, a few-month-old baby and son of Lucia and Jason, is left behind by his mother in GTA 6’s first truly shocking reveal.
Given the history of leaks associated with GTA 6 , it feels like a minor miracle that Tommy’s existence remained a complete unknown until launch. This was something that Rob Nelson, co-studio head at Rockstar North, was keenly aware of.
“No, we never were going to [reveal it]," he told VGC in an interview that took place just before GTA 6 came out last week. "I am still holding on. Fingers crossed, how many more days? I’m praying it stays under wraps. Given everything that we’ve gone through, every day I’m just like, ‘Please, please don’t do that, please don’t do that.'”
As we’ve written about at IGN, the existence of Tomás in GTA 6 is the key to its whole design . It’s what powers Jason and Lucia’s tale, and encourages the player to strive to make more and more money as those family savings goals get higher and higher. It connects us to the characters, and creates a shared objective between us and them. We aren’t simply committing crime for crime’s sake, but doing so with the prospect of being reunited with their son at the end of it.
You can see why such a powerful and surprising narrative device would want to have been kept under wraps by Rockstar. It’s the first, and by no means the only, shocking revelation of GTA 6, all the more effective when witnessed firsthand.
“We never were going to [reveal it],” Nelson explained. “It’s meant to shock. We were watching everyone speculate about the nature of their relationship and Jason’s character, and that takes it in a completely different context. You have something to strive for beyond a huge bank account at the end.”
We’ve got the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide here on IGN, complete with comprehensive walkthroughs up to Chapter 4 , guides for the Optional Missions and Illegal Operations you’ll find in Leonida, and much more. Just getting started in Chapter 1 ? Check out our Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks , and make a note of the Best Free Weapons to Find Early . If you're already driving all around Leonida and want to know everything there is to find and do, see the Leonida interactive map .

pool.titulo: Creating Fresh Looks Is More Important in GTA 6 Than Any Game Before
pool.resumen: GTA 6 has Rockstar's best-ever customisation, with hundreds of amazing pieces. But it's about more that creating a fresh fit - clothes are key to surviving the cops.
pool.contenido:
This is an opinion piece from writer Jess Kinghorn. IGN's opinion columns represent the personal viewpoints of the writer, drawing on their own experiences and research to explore the exciting world of video games.
There comes a time in every professional criminal’s life when you’ve got to make a dear friend disappear. I’ll keep the spoilers light on when that happens in Grand Theft Auto 6 , but all you need to know is that our man Jason has been tasked with getting rid of a former contact’s car – plus all of their worldly possessions. Now, had I actually checked the trunk I would have seen a bright red gas can and then set the whole thing ablaze – unfortunately, I didn’t check the trunk. Instead, I drove the departed’s wheels straight into Leonida Bay in full view of witnesses. Now, our lad Jason is a wanted man looking to disappear himself.
Camped out in a bush, the police scanner crackles to life. “Suspect is a white male wearing a baseball cap” – well, the cap's the first thing to go, then, as I leg it back to the Ganado. I could keep running and try to outpace the police’s BOLO, but GTA 6 offers a fair few options for escaping suspicion. Losing yourself in customisation and creating a well-stocked wardrobe has become well worth your while beyond simply looking sharp, and it’s now as much a part of your criminal arsenal as carrying a piece.
I didn’t fully appreciate how GTA 6’s wealth of customisation options and the Wanted system interact until chapter two. I was already looking forward to playing dress up with Lucia, so when my new drug-shifting mum-doing-her-best pal Vicki points out the local vintage store, I can’t help but rub my grubby little gamer mitts together.
But besides introducing more fashion options I’m personally inclined towards, chapter two also introduces new crimes to commit. Stick-ups are hit-it-and-quit-it criminal operations – brandish a gun, take the money, and then run. Lucia got her criminal start boosting cars when she was a young teen, so carjacking is a big, lucrative part of this chapter as well. These opportunistic crimes are a complementary contrast to chapter one’s more organised approach – but better yet, Lucia's working for herself rather than Jason playing passive errand boy.
Dispatch advises to be on the lookout for someone matching my description. It's all the excuse I need to finally check out the vintage store. But, my Lucia has too much business to take care of to waste time hiding in bushes, waiting for the heat to subside. Sure, in a stick-up, I can scout around for security camera footage and destroy it like a true professional, or try to control a crowd to stop someone calling the police. Still though, it's tough to be a solo act when Lucia is striking out on her own – given my twitchy trigger fingers have flubbed entering the safe code three times already, I can't rely on making a clean exit every time.
As Lucia pelts out the back door, I keep an ear out for the police scanner on her phone (I’m not gonna think too hard about how that would actually work in real life, and I'm definitely not gonna Google it). Right on cue dispatch says “Suspect is a slim woman in her twenties” (Dispatch, you flatter me), and advises nearby personnel to be on the lookout for someone matching that description, wearing a bandana, a leather jacket, and cargo pants. Well, that’s all the excuse I need to finally check out the vintage store Vicki recommended earlier.
Stashing the bandana and putting on a more friendly face, I use my very recently ill-gotten gains to buy a whole new look. All the usual frumpy suspects are here – well worn trainers, faded sweatshirts, holy-moly jeans – but there are plenty of bangers too. When I’m done, Lucia strides out of the vintage store a whole new woman in a red dress and a pair of trainers a sneaker head would approve of. But diving into a clothes store and improvising a fresh outfit is just one avenue for misdirection.
After a fair few stick-ups, I’ve amassed quite a collection of second hand clothes. Hats, sunglasses, and – like in Red Dead Redemption 2 – bandanas (plus plenty of other 'masks') can be used to hide your face in a pinch. Checking in with the wardrobe at Lucia’s home base, I’ve lost a lot of time composing great fits and saving them for later. It’s a particularly worthwhile time sink as you can then stow these saved outfits in the trunk of your go-to getaway vehicle (for me, that’s an Imponte Ruiner '82 in bright red).
Suspect is a woman wearing a baseball cap and a yellow shirt? Not anymore, she’s not. That’s the secret of any great improviser – they’re not so much making it up as they go along, as they are phenomenally well prepared for every eventuality. And with the way playing dress up in GTA 6 now interacts with the Wanted system, I can play a whole load of different roles.
You can tell a lot about a community based on what turns up in their secondhand shops, and Port Gellhorn’s selection communicates the dire financial straits many of the locals are in. Customisation doesn’t begin and end with bits of tat you find at Leonida’s second hand shops either. The Wanted system can also keep tabs on how Lucia and Jason’s hair is styled, so popping into the salon frequently is another great shout. There, you can change the style of your protagonist’s hair, the length, and the colour, too – though I do kind of wish I could sling a wig or two in the trunk of my getaway car just to cover all of my bases (especially considering the platinum blonde number Lucia wears in at least one story mission). Still, when she rocks up with freshly braided hair, Jason says he likes the new look – and that’s really what it’s all about.
While Lucia is at it in the salon, she can also play around with make up. The full face looks are pretty limited to begin with, though these – and all other categories of customisation options – open up the more of Leonida you explore. pool.titulo: Target Is Giving Away Free Gift Cards on Black Friday, Here's How to Get One
pool.contenido:
The vast majority of Black Friday sales are already live online today. Gone are the days where you need wake up early, or camp out, to be one of the first people in line at the store the day after Thanksgiving. But what about waiting in line for free money?
Target revealed last week that it will be giving away free gift cards to the first 100 "eligible guests" at every one of its stores. The gift card amount will generally range between $25 and $100, but one person per store will win the grand $1,000 gift card prize.
How to Get a Free Target Gift Card on Black Friday If you're looking to grab one of these gift cards for yourself and take a crack at that $1K, you're going to need to be one of the first 100 people in line at the store when it opens. Target states that its retail locations will open at 6 a.m. local time, but you'll want to check your location to make sure it's the same there.
When should you get in line? Every Target is going to have different levels of interest in this promotion, so there is no right time to go that fits every situation. There are always going to be people who are willing to camp overnight for free things, so it's worth driving by tonight and see if its busy or not. If nobody is already waiting, you're probably fine to just get there a couple hours early.
Target states that the promotion won't start until one hour before opening and will end one hour after opening. That gives you a two hour window of eligibilty for the promotion.
How do you actually get your gift card? According to Target's official press release , you won't immediately be handed a gift card. Upon entering the store you will be handed a ticket, which you'll then need to redeem at the "in-store event cart". It's there that your gift card value will actually be revealed.
You do need to redeem your ticket within the first hour of the store opening, however, or you'll risk forfeiting your right to receive your gift card. You can see official details at Target.com/BlackFridayGiveaway.

pool.titulo: Los desarrolladores de GTA 6 han decidido su futuro y el resultado es muy diferente a lo que muchos imaginaban. Rockstar dice 'no' al sindicato
pool.resumen:
Los desarrolladores de Rockstar han decidido rechazar el reconocimiento de un nuevo sindicato . El equipo ha llevado a cabo una votación para decidir su futuro y la mayor parte de los miembros de la compañía se han mostrado en contra de la iniciativa. Se trata de un giro inesperado, pues el despido de más de 30 empleados como consecuencia de sus actividades sindicales (que la empresa justificó con una supuesta filtración de información clasificada) supuso el comienzo de una larga campaña en la que hubo acusaciones de "represión", visitas a los juzgados y un esfuerzo constante para instaurar un sindicato en la desarrolladora. Y este último paso se iba a materializar con un sufragio general, pero ahora sabemos que el movimiento no ha llegado muy lejos y Rockstar, por lo tanto, se quedará sin esta organización para sus trabajadores.
De hecho, el sindicato ni siquiera ha estado a las puertas de hacerse realidad. Jason Schreier, de Bloomberg, profundiza brevemente en los resultados señalando que la diferencia de votos entre el 'sí' y el 'no' es más grande de lo que se había previsto: "El 75 % de los trabajadores de Rockstar UK han votado en contra del reconocimiento del sindicato", indi
