pool.resumen:
Aunque la inteligencia artificial ha abierto la puerta a que prácticamente cualquiera pueda desarrollar su propio videojuego sin tener grandes conocimientos de programación, hay quienes quizá no han elegido el mejor momento para hacerlo. Sam Corcos , uno de los responsables del Departamento del Tesoro de Estados Unidos , lleva días trabajando en su propio clon de Civilization con ayuda de la IA , algo que no ha sentado nada bien a los jugadores y que seguro que a Take-Two , dueña de la licencia, tampoco. Sin embargo, más allá de las quejas por lo amoral que resulta copiar una licencia reconocida, la polémica escala considerablemente al tener en cuenta su contexto: el organismo gubernamental está lidiando con un importante incidente de ciberseguridad mientras su director de informática sigue "jugando con la IA".

pool.titulo: Talking Point: Ocarina Of Time Revolutionised The 3D Swordfight, But How Does The Remake Hold Up In A Vintage Year For Clashing Blades?
pool.resumen:
Finding the cutting edge of sword combat.
Forget the hubbub around Grand Theft Auto . Big Walk ? Big deal. It’s all noise designed to distract us from 2026’s real legacy: that it’s been one of the best years on record for video game swordfighting.
Onimusha: Way of the Sword broke free of parryslop with exciting, flexible and immensely satisfying katana combat. Blood of Dawnwalker ’s directional combat recreated a scintillating sense of strike-and-counterstrike rhythm rather than asking players to hide behind defensive blocks. Then Phantom Blade Zero swans in with cinematic style and a dazzling flurry of wuxia sword strikes and somersaults.

pool.titulo: Rockstar Games Has A GTA 6 Hit On Its Hands, But Its Union Vote Is A Loss
pool.resumen:
Roughly 75% of Rockstar Games staff in the UK have voted against a formal recognition agreement with the Independent Workers' Union of Great Britain (IWGB). The news came in the wake of GTA 6 's record-breaking launch , and had the IWGB been recognized, Rockstar Games management would have been legally obligated to negotiate collective bargaining terms with the union on topics such as pay, hours, and conditions.
Voting took place across two weeks, and turnout was massive, with over 93% of UK staff casting their ballot (roughly 1,544 employees). The IWGB said it was undeterred by the result and would continue working to build support among Rockstar employees. "While the result means Rockstar will not be formally required to hold regular meetings with union representatives under a recognition agreement, it does not prevent workers from continuing to organize and push for workplace improvements through the IWGB, joining the union or exercising their individual trade union rights and protections," the union said in a statement.

pool.titulo: Microsoft-Owned GitHub Stuns Followers as It Celebrates AnyPS5 Repo in Now-Deleted Tweet
pool.resumen: In a post that’s since been deleted, Microsoft-owned code and software collaboration site GitHub celebrated the AnyPS5 repo “passing 58k stars” from users on the platform as a result of the launch of GTA 6. GitHub even told followers "Happy GTA VImas!" in a tweet that will almost certainly have infurated Rockstar Games, parent company Take-Two, PlayStation, and Xbox.
pool.contenido:
In a post that’s since been deleted, Microsoft-owned code and software collaboration site GitHub celebrated the AnyPS5 repo “passing 58k stars” from users on the platform as a result of the launch of GTA 6. GitHub even told followers "Happy GTA VImas!" in a tweet that will almost certainly have infurated Rockstar Games, parent company Take-Two, PlayStation, and Xbox.
“GTA 6 is finally here, sparking one of the biggest weeks in gaming and open source on GitHub,” the post said, before jumping into celebrating the repo. “Does changing where games run cross a legal line?” the tweet asked.
This is insane https://t.co/mwU6VIy1nI
— MVG (@ModernVintageG) November 26, 2026
There was also an official video attached to the tweet, which highlighted a post from an AnyPS5 coder, via Kotaku . The post in the video said: “We have 3 days until GTA 6 everyone[…]get your agents or deevs[sic] and work.”
While the post could easily be the work of a rogue social media person, the optics aren’t good at all. GTA 6 is only officially available on PS5 and Xbox Series X and S, so both Sony and Microsoft have benefited greatly from the game's record-breaking launch. To see a the Microsoft-owned GitHub post a message to its followers essentially encouraging potential piracy is remarkable.
IGN has asked for comment, but GitHub obviously realized its mistake — it deleted the tweet, after all — but how it even got approved in the first place is a mystery until the company comments.
Take-Two is currently working to take down various homebrew community efforts from GitHub, as the race to release an unofficial GTA 6 PC port heats up. This follows Cyberleek's alleged released of the executable file for the incomplete GTA 6 Xbox build they reportedly leaked the week prior. There’s even a website tracking the various attempts to recompile, emulate, or port the leaked Xbox Series build to PC.
The big question for Take-Two is, can it do anything meaningful to stop a working, playable build of GTA 6 on PC from getting into people's hands? GitHub takedowns can only go so far, as the homebrew scenes uses AI to speed along development. Take-Two stands to make billions of dollars more from the official PC release of GTA 6, so any unofficial version is a significant business risk. In a recent interview with IGN sister site RPS , former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij said that Rockstar Games may be keen to port GTA 6 to PC as soon as possible , due to the explosion of AI-generated clones and ports.
It's also worth noting that there is extra interest in a PC version of GTA 6 because the console versions target 30fps. The PC version, resumably, will run at 60fps or whatever frame rate your rig is capable of .
Earlier this month, Strauss Zelnick, the boss of Take-Two, responded to the threat of AI-assisted reverse-engineering and decompilation of games in an interview with IGN. He said he was taking the issue seriously, and insisted that fans will prefer to play GTA 6 officially, with all its bells and whistles as Rockstar intended, over an unofficial PC version.
Here’s the exchange:
IGN: We've seen hackers using AI to clone games much faster than ever before, even try to jailbreak consoles. And there is some concern about this leading to potentially GTA 6 being made available on PC unofficially or places that you aren't releasing it. I was just wondering how much of a threat this is to your business? And, is there anything meaningful you can do about it?
Strauss Zelnick: I don't think it’s a financial matter, in terms of a threat to our business. I do think it’s a creative matter. It's important to everyone, our developers and our consumers alike, to deliver the experience Rockstar envisions. And at the same time, of course, we protect our intellectual property vigilantly. So we are focused on these concerns. We're not in the least cavalier about them. Technology is advancing quickly. And at the same time, I do think that pretty much everyone wants the Rockstar experience as Rockstar intended.
IGN: Related, last week Anthropic confirmed they took steps to block Claude from reverse engineering video games. I would assume you would welcome that. And would you like to see other AI companies like OpenAI do the same thing to prevent people from using these powerful AI models to clone your games?
Strauss Zelnick: I think all companies should be protecting intellectual property, their own and everyone else's. And if you're in the intellectual property business, which Anthropic is and OpenAI is, then it seems ironic on the one hand to stomp on someone else's IP and hope that yours is protected.
During an investor-focused Q&A following the release of Take-Two’s latest financial report, attended by IGN, Zelnick was asked multiple times about the AI reverse-engineering problem. He, again, had strong words in response, suggesting Take-Two was ready to lawyer up.
“This business has been largely immune to piracy concerns forever because of file sizes, complexity of piracy, being connected to servers and the like,” he began. “And undoubtedly, it would be very difficult to replicate the experience of consuming our game as intended because of technical limitations.
“That said, it's going to become more of a challenge, as you said, and we're aware of that. So we are utterly focused on enhancing our technical defenses and enhancing our legal activities appropriately. And at the same time, without in any way being cavalier, every entertainment business that exists is subject to some element of piracy. So this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent. I think it will be manageable and we are focused on it.”
Zelnick’s talk about legal activities sparks an obvious question: what can game companies do about AI-assisted reverse engineering? It's a question IGN recently asked when people started to work on a PC port of Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake .

pool.resumen: RGB Mini-LED tech boasts richer colors, a brighter picture, and wider viewing angles than ever before.
pool.contenido:
Last year, Hisense pioneered the first RGB Mini-LED TV with its 116UX model. Granted it was only available as a massive 116" screen that retailed for $20,000. In 2026, Hisense released its second generation RGB Mini-LED tech at a much more affordable price point with its UR-series lineup. For Black Friday, you can get it for even less. Best Buy has just discounted the 65" Hisense UR8 RGB Mini-LED TV from $2,000 all the way down to $899.99 and the 75" model from $2,500 down to $1399.99, both with free delivery. These are the lowest prices since launch and beats previous lows by $200.
The Hisense UR8 RGB Mini-LED TV Gives OLED a Run for Its Money
RGB Mini-LED is essentially the next generation evolution of Mini-LED technology. Traditional mini-LED TVs consist of an array of blue LED that are passed through RGB filters to produced the desired color. RGB Mini-LED TVs use red, green, and blue LEDs instead of just blue, which means the pixels no longer need filters to produce the desired color. The result is more accurate color reproduction, less blooming and, most importantly, a wider color gamut. In fact, the color gamut of RGB Mini-LED surpasses that of OLEDs, since current-generation OLEDs also use color filters combined with blue OLEDs. How does that translate in the real world? It means that you see richer, more accurate colors, smoother gradients and less banding than even OLEDs, especially in 4K HDR content.
RGB Mini-LED TVs have several other features that out-class standard Mini-LEDs. They're brighter (far brighter than OLED TVs), making them perfect for daytime watching in bright rooms with little light control. They offer much better viewing angles, which means everyone you're hosting will enjoy the game wherever they're positioned around the TV. Gamers will benefit from this TV as well. The Hisense UR8 boasts a 180Hz native refresh rate, the highest I've ever seen for a TV, with HDMI 2.1 inputs that will pair seamlessly with a PlayStation 5 console for seamlessly running games in 4K.

pool.titulo: Chainsaws 'Would Have Been Too Much' Even for GTA 6, as Rockstar Explains Why Some Extra Violent Weapons Are Missing
pool.resumen: Rockstar has explained why some extra violent weapons like chainsaws and katanas are missing from GTA 6.
pool.contenido:
You can commit an extreme amount of violence in GTA 6 , with a wide variety of weaponry. Guns, baseball bats, even tanks can be your chosen tool of destruction. But that hasn’t stopped some from wondering where some series favourites have disappeared to.
Among those are the likes of katanas and chainsaws, which were staples during Grand Theft Auto’s “3D universe” games, including Vice City and San Andreas. The chainsaw, in particular, holds a special connection to Vice City given its clear Scarface inspirations, and memorable scene involving the power tool from the 1983 movie.
But despite some being spotted around the latest version of Leonida in GTA 6, neither Jason nor Lucia can wield them as weapons. Why? Well, Rockstar co-studio head Rob Nelson explained the decision in an interview with VGC .
“As far as the chainsaw — I think it would have been too much for this game at this resolution and these characters,” Nelson says. "It’s not a resource thing. Even at the most psycho, did Jason and Lucia really need that — what’s that going to look like?”
When asked specifically about why chainsaws are lying about the world, but can’t be picked up, Nelson explained that, “you’re always trying to find what is the right sort of line and the right balance; it really just depends — you want to feel like you can interact with as much of the world as possible.”
I have to somewhat agree that it just wouldn’t feel like it fit either Jason or Lucia’s characters to be roaming around looking for limbs to chop off with a mechanised serrated blade. Ultimately, their story is one about committing crime to escape to a better, more “normal” life, not one about two psychopaths with a lust for blood going on a rampage.
That being said, when whatever the online component of GTA 6 launches, I could see objects like this becoming weapons, allowing for people to roleplay as whatever brand of criminal, psychopath, or tree sculptor they wish. There’s a world of possibilities out there.

pool.contenido:
Spider-Man: Brand New Day rerelease includes a scene cut from Avengers: Doomsday , according to a new report.
The New York Times published an article on the potential for the release of Avengers: Doomsday and Dune: Part 3 — dubbed DunesDay by fans — to set box office records, and within it is a tease for the extra footage set to be included in Spider-Man: Brand New Day’s return to theaters.
According to the NYT, Spider-Man: Brand New Day will have a scene cut from Doomsday added to the end of the movie as a bonus. We don’t know what’s in the scene, but it’s meant to serve as an ad for the upcoming MCU film. Spider-Man: Brand New Day made an eye-watering $2.5 billion at the global box office, so I assume you've seen it. If so, has the promise of a new Avengers: Doomsday scene convinced you to double-dip? Let us know in the comments!
What we know for sure is that Rosario Dawson will return as Claire Temple in the rerelease , marking her long-awaited comeback to the MCU.
Warning! Spoilers for Spider-Man: Brand New Day follow.
Last week, Dawson revealed a photo of her in costume for her first Marvel appearance in a decade, standing in nurse scrubs next to Tom Holland's Spider-Man. It's a scene that fans thought they'd never get to see after it was deleted from the final cut of the movie . Now, however, it is being reinstated for the film's extended edition rerelease , entitled Spider-Man: [Brand New] Brand New Day, alongside a handful of other moments previously left on the cutting room floor.
It's pretty obvious when this scene will take place, as Dawson's character stands next to Tom Holland's Spider-Man who is wearing a hospital gown and his Spidey mask. Of course, Spider-Man finds himself in hospital towards the end of the movie, and Dawson's return will likely answer fan questions surrounding how the superhero got patched up with no one else discovering his identity. (The answer, surely, is that Dawson takes care of him directly — having been used to keeping numerous superhero identities secret in the past.)
Spider-Man: Brand New Day returns to theaters on December 4, 2026, now with Rosario Dawson and an Avengers: Doomsday cut scene included. Avengers: Doomsday itself launches on December 18. Today, we got our first look at Magneto vs Doom in a new teaser for Avengers: Doomsday.

pool.titulo: Steam isn't doing 'an official Black Friday fest,' but it does have a page with hundreds of discounts and 'Black Friday' splashed across the top so you might want to check it out anyway
pool.resumen: Updates to Steam's 'Discounts and Events' page are now live, and Valve wants to show them off.
pool.contenido:
Steam isn't running an official Black Friday fest—it says so right here in this update , "Steam isn't running an official Black Friday fest"—but plenty of game developers have marked their stuff down to take advantage of the big sale season, and so Valve is helping them all out a bit by "dressing up" its Discounts and Events page in the appropriate seasonal garb.
Is there a little bit of wink wink, nudge nudge to that 'not a Black Friday fest' business? Hey, maybe.
In fair play, though, Steam traditionally hasn't run Black Friday sales, because its Autumn Sale was always happening at the same time. The realignment of seasonal sales in 2025 changed that, however, leaving a hole that was filled by the first-ever Steam Black Friday Sale last year.
Valve has other priorities this year, though, which could explain the absence ( wink wink, nudge nudge ) of an official Black Friday event on Steam in 2026. In September, Valve announced changes to Steam's Discounts and Events page to make it prettier and more personalized, and it said in today's update that Black Friday is "the perfect time to share the updates we've been working on to make the Discounts & Events page a better experience altogether."
With that all cleared up, I'll say that the Black Friday non-fest page is definitely an eye-catcher, and it will be interesting to see how Valve puts this section of Steam to work in the future. If it's treated like an 'almost a Steam sale' that never really ends, I have to think that developers and gamers alike will benefit—at least until we all get used to it and Valve has to figure out some new way to tweak the formula.
For now, since we're here, let's check out some deals:

pool.titulo: Dev team who delayed their game a year to avoid Silksong says they won't do it again for whatever Team Cherry announces tomorrow: 'This time we're staying put'
pool.resumen: Aeternum Game Studios does have a question, though: "Is it just us, or does the universe have it in for us?"
pool.contenido:
In August 2025, Aeternum Game Studios announced that Aeterna Lucis , the sequel to the well-liked 2021 metroidvania Aeterna Noctis, would be delayed from its planned launch in September of that year to sometime in 2026, for one good reason: Silksong. Just prior to that, Team Cherry surprised everyone by announcing that the Hollow Knight: Silksong launch was imminent, and Aeternum—and a whole bunch of others —decided the smart move was to just get out of the way.
Well, here we go again. Yesterday, Team Cherry announced that " Cherry Time " is coming on November 27, with "a bunch of exciting announcements, plus an update on Hollow Knight: Silksong - Sea of Sorrow," the Silksong expansion announced in December 2025. Some fans are hoping that means the Sea of Sorrow release date will be announced—or maybe even that it will actually be released.
Whatever's coming, Aeternum says that this time around, it's standing firm.
"Dear Team Cherry," Aeternum wrote in an Official Statement: Part 2 message, riffing on the "Official Statement" it put out in 2025. "A little over a year ago, just as we were about to launch our game, you announced Silksong. We stepped aside, pushed the whole project back a year, and, honestly, it was one of the best decisions we've ever made: The genre had an incredible year, and we got to enjoy Silksong as fans and polish Aeterna Lucis into the game we always dreamed it would be.
"Now here we are again, just days from launch. Aeterna Lucis, our new Metroidvania, comes out on December 3... and you announce Cherry Time.
"This time we're staying put. Not to go against you, but because a lot of people have been waiting for the Queen of Light for a long time, and we don't want to make them wait any longer."
Official statement, part II. Here we go again…
— @aeternathegame.bsky.social ( @aeternathegame.bsky.social.bsky.social ) 2026-11-26T18:31:21.537Z You might say that there's some element of opportunism at work here. Aeterna Lucis launches on December 3, one week from today, and since that's surely way too close for another delay (not to mention it was pushed back a year already), the next-best option is to leverage this new Silksong moment in whatever way possible.
Still, it's hard not to have sympathy for Aeternum. Maybe this Cherry Time announcement won't be a big deal, but then again, maybe it will be a very big deal. Aeternum is being a good sport about it, but I have to think there's some real frustration behind its message.
And with good reason. This isn't a situation like Devolver Digital launching Volvy alongside GTA 6—that is, two completely different games with virtually no meaningful audience overlap. Aeterna Lucis and Hollow Knight: Silksong are both fantasy metroidvanias, and there's a lot of potential crossover there. If Team Cherry does unload Sea of Sorrow before the end of the year, that could—almost certainly will — cut deeply into Aeterna Lucis.
"We have to ask, with all the love in the world: Is it just us, or does the universe have it in for us? Hahaha. And since you're about to wreck our lives all over again, the least we can do is make a bundle together."
Hey, you can't blame 'em for taking a shot, especially under the circumstances. "Hahaha," indeed.
Aeterna Lucis launches on Steam on December 3. Cherry Team, whatever it turns out to be, will kick off at 10 am ET/1 pm PT on November 27.

Tandem OLED stacks multiple OLED layers on top of each other instead of a single layer. pool.titulo: 32 Years Later, Disney's Most Notorious Cash-Grab Sequel Is Better Than You Remember
pool.resumen: The Aladdin sequel The Return of Jafar is often derided as a bad, cheap sequel which started Disney's direct-to-video sequel trend, but I love it
pool.contenido: Ever since former Disney CEO Bob Chapek released his autobiography last September, a rather unexpected Disney movie has been a topic for discussion: the direct-to-VHS sequel to Aladdin titled The Return of Jafar . Released in 1994, The Return of Jafar was the first in a long line of direct-to-VHS (and later direct-to-DVD) sequels to theatrical Disney films. Besides Aladdin , Disney made sequels to The Lion King , The Little Mermaid , Pocahontas , Mulan , and several other then-modern Disney animated features, as well as some much older classics like Cinderella and Bambi . These movies used cheaper animation produced by Disney’s TV division and were developed in far less time than Disney spends developing animated feature films .

pool.titulo: 7 Years Later, Hollywood’s Most Notorious Fantasy Flop Deserves Another Shot
pool.resumen: Seven years later, a first watch of Tom Hooper’s Cats on Netflix finds plenty to enjoy, especially Taylor Swift’s catnip number.
pool.contenido: I vividly remember learning the phrase “uncanny valley” in 2019. First came the trailer for Sonic the Hedgehog that April, with those alarmingly human teeth. Then came the first trailer for Tom Hooper’s Cats in July. Suddenly, there was a name for a feeling I’d had my whole life. The uncanny valley is that uneasy feeling you get when something looks or moves almost like a real person, but some small detail makes the whole thing feel wrong. That feeling is a lot more common these days, now that AI-generated videos are everywhere. But it was Cats that really brought the uncanny valley into the popular lexicon.

pool.titulo: 'Blizzard I'm looking at you': Path of Exile 2 boss criticizes 'truly terrible' game announcements that hold the juiciest details until the end
pool.resumen: Grinding Gear Games' Jonathan Rogers urges devs to lead with their best stuff.
pool.contenido:
Every few months, Grinding Gear Games resurfaces with livestreams to showcase all the new toys in the latest updates for Path of Exile 1 and 2. They play out quite differently from your usual game announcements, cutting straight to showing new gameplay features ahead of any preamble.
According to Path of Exile co-game director Jonathan Rogers, this is a key part of Path of Exile's success over the last 13 years. Speaking at games industry conference DevGAMM FTW! , he explained how GGG came up with a winning formula for PoE's seasonal update schedule.
The announcement streams aren't just marketing, he explained, they help dictate what kinds of things the team should focus on with every update. If it doesn't sound exciting enough to rally players around a new league, it doesn't get made.
After a teaser trailer reveals the theme and title of the league a few weeks before the full announcement, the stream dives right into the juiciest details—an approach that Rogers believes is paramount when it comes to selling the update.
Rogers says he's seen some "truly terrible livestreams for game announcements," before slipping in a quick jab: "Blizzard I'm looking at you."
I've watched enough Diablo 4 new season streams to know exactly what he's talking about even if I don't quite agree that it's strictly a bad way to do it. Blizzard typically likes to lead with some introductions before having individual developers break down what's coming in an update.
Admittedly, these can drag on for too long, especially if you don't particularly care about percentage changes to some item or stat. But I appreciate hearing the thought process behind each decision from the people responsible for that aspect of the game. In a time when certain very vocal segments of the audience prefer to think of studios as machines, it's a good way to remind people that real human beings are behind it all.
That said, I think Rogers' specific point about too many studios wasting everyone's time by holding the best announcements for last is often true. For something like a new update to an ongoing game, everyone is watching to find out why this one is worth logging back in for. I want to see the standout details so I don't feel like I wasted 45 minutes for something I'm not that into.
Sometimes I do like the build-up and eventual payoff for a big reveal, though, like the way Blizzard dropped Diablo 5 at the end of the Diablo portion of this year's BlizzCon or how Larian surprised everyone with Divinity last year. Certain games earn the theatrics. If anything, Rogers' approach just underlines how important it is for studios to read the room and craft their announcements around the things that will actually spark interest rather than putting everyone to sleep.

pool.titulo: Dawn of War 4's campaigns differ based on your choices: 'which character you choose and what decisions you make with them lead down different experiences of an overlapping story'
pool.resumen: Dawn of War 4 writer John French lays out how it works.
pool.contenido:
The original Dawn of War's Winter Assault expansion added campaigns that let you play two factions at once, with different final missions based on which one you triumphed with. Dawn of War 2's campaign was even more player-led, with distress calls that had different outcomes based on what you prioritized and, in the Chaos Rising expansion, a morality mechanic with Corruption and Redemption points. It even chose a different character to be a traitor based on who gained the most Corruption by the story's end.
I asked John French, Dawn of War 4's writer and a Warhammer novelist, whether Dawn of War 4 would follow this noble tradition by having player decisions alter the plot. "The player's decisions very much change the perspectives that they'll experience the game from," he replied. "So, depending on which heroes from each faction they choose, they'll have a very different experience of the game, in that they'll see different parts of the story and sometimes different views on the same events."
Based on what we've seen of the Ork and Adeptus Mechanicus campaigns, that means partway through you'll be presented with a choice between two Commanders who have opposed goals and the one you pick will lead to missions with different objectives. Ork Beastboss Guzcutta is trying to unite his clan, the Snakebites, while his rival warboss, Gorgutz, is an off-world interloper trying to rebuild his damaged invasion force.
"With characters like Gorgutz and Guzcutta," French explained, "it can be as simple as one of them wants to do it the traditional, brutal ork way, and one of them wants to do it in a brutal but cunning way, so you have missions that focus on getting lots of shiny kit in one, while the other tries to get as many orks to follow them as possible.
"In a more complex narrative, like the Adeptus Mechanicus campaign, Potentia-Delta-9's main drive is the quest for knowledge, and she is on a very different path from Skitarii Marshal Sek-Ix-23, who is very much about enforcing the orthodoxy. The story for both overlaps, but which character you choose and what decisions you make with them lead down different experiences of an overlapping story."
Writing an RTS isn't all about plotting out the campaign missions. The Dawn of War games are legendary for their unit barks, like the saber-rattling Lord Commissar who shouts, from the top of an armored Chimera transport, "Drive me closer, I want to hit them with my sword!" Getting across so much personality in a short space is a real skill.
"You can do an awful lot with just a couple of words like 'More dakka!'," French said, "that tells you a huge amount about the orks on its own. Even with factions like the necrons, the way that the lower ranks respond to the higher ones with just 'Obedience,' one word, tells how their faction works."
Part of the appeal of Warhammer is the berserk variety of its armies, each with its own highly thematic identity. You walk into a shop and see the stoic space marines alongside spiky Chaos daemons and units of Astra Militarum who look like they stepped out of a trench in World War I before being given laser rifles.
"Dawn of War 4 is deeply Warhammer in that way because it's got all of these different textures of factions and characters next to each other," French said. "You have orks, and they are absolutely fixated on smashing everything they can in the pursuit of trying to have an even bigger fight. Then you've got the Adeptus Mechanicus, who revere machines as holy and worship the machine as god with complete sincerity and total conviction. Those two things literally exist side by side, along with alien races who have made themselves immortal by creating metal bodies with hyper advanced technology. And all of these different types of character come into conflict on one planet cut off in a sea of night—that's very Warhammer."
Dawn of War 4 is due out on December 3 and will be available on Steam . Owners of the Commander Edition will get advance access and can play from November 30.

pool.titulo: Microsoft's Github posts message celebrating efforts to port PlayStation 5 version of Grand Theft Auto 6 to PC, then quickly deletes it
pool.resumen: Guess who just got yelled at?
pool.contenido:
Microsoft-owned developer platform Github stepped in it earlier today when it posted a message on X celebrating the success of AnyPS5, an open source project that aims to let users port PS5 executables to PC, and then linked that success directly to efforts to port Grand Theft Auto 6 to PC. The message was deleted shortly after it was posted, but not before it was widely noticed and called out for being a very bad idea.
"GTA 6 is finally here, sparking one of the biggest weeks in gaming and open source on Github," the message stated (via Kotaku ).
"The repo AnyPS5 has passed 58K stars since its August launch, rewriting PS5 executables to run on Windows and Linux. Does changing where games run cross a legal line? Share your take. Happy GTA VImas!"
Lest there be any misunderstanding, a video that accompanied the post made the GTA 6 connection explicit: "The project rewrites a game's executable so Windows and Linux can run it directly. Performance seems to be the main issue for users wanting to run GTA 6, with one contributor telling the project's community to 'lock in and get your agents to help' if they need to."
The question of whether or not this sort of thing crosses a legal line has, predictably, sparked debate among those who think they have a clear understanding of the answer. What caught most by surprise, though, is that Github—which is owned by Microsoft—would put forth the question in the first place, implicitly suggesting that it might not. GTA 6 publisher Take-Two Interactive has been pretty aggressive with its efforts to keep recompiled versions of GTA 6 from landing on PC, and I can't imagine it would too thrilled with Github—which, I must emphasize, is owned by Microsoft —telling the world that it might actually be okay to go ahead and vibe-code it up.
That point wasn't missed by redditors, one of whom described it as Github " openly taunting Sony and Rockstar ." Even the AnyPS5 subreddit seemed baffled: Redditor superkickstart asked, "Do they have AI running their socials? Lol"
There's also a little bit of irony in the fact that, until earlier this week, the leading effort to get GTA 6 running on PC was based on an Xbox build of the game posted by GTA 6 leaker Cyberleeks. Beyond that, there are also some very obvious questions about how Github ( owned by Microsoft ) would react to AI-powered ports of, say, other software:
The whole thing is weird, really, because it seems like such an obviously bad idea. The only explanation I can come up with is that a social media manager either didn't think about it, didn't understand it (which would be weird in itself for someone doing social media posts for Github), or just had a big ol' brain fart. Whatever the reason, I imagine someone got a good old-fashioned talking-to about it.
I've reached out to Github and Take-Two for comment and will update if I receive a reply.

pool.titulo: WoW: Forever min-maxers are upset that its 40-player PvP mode now actually requires PvP to win
pool.resumen: Blizzard's latest patch prevents Alterac Valley from being a glorified reputation farm.
pool.contenido:
Despite being set in the past, WoW: Forever is an attempt to capture the spirit of the old game by injecting it with new quirks that challenge new and returning players alike to approach it differently than any other version of the MMO. This is why familiar old dungeons can drop new loot, like an armor set that turns you into a snake .
Blizzard has said that its goal is to "unsolve" the game as best it can so players don't settle into the same routines they're used to. This is especially true for min-maxed strategies that threaten to suck the fun out of enjoying the game, or "the journey", as Blizzard likes to call it.
It's a lofty goal that can't be achieved without persistently fiddling with the knobs that encourage players to do one thing over another—which is the very thing that differentiates WoW: Forever from WoW Classic.
This week, Blizzard stepped in to fix a problem that was brewing in its 40-player MOBA-esque PvP mode Alterac Valley. Players were avoiding PvP altogether, turning it into a glorified reputation farm.
"We’ve seen that players in Alterac Valley were frequently completing the battleground without capturing the objectives, so we’ve made some adjustments to incentivize a focus on the objectives rather than rushing to kill the enemy faction’s general," community manager Kaivax wrote.
The patch basically broke a popular 'zerg' strategy where one side rushed to end the match as fast as possible by beefing up the NPC defenders that stood in their way. Blizzard shifted some of the reputation and honor you'd normally get from killing the generals to the other objectives so players are encouraged to engage with the whole mode.
But, as I've seen with changes like this in the past few weeks, many players are upset that they can't just spam it for the rewards, and that others have already reaped the benefits of the old strategy. There are people in Reddit threads doing the math to highlight how much efficiency has been lost (it doesn't seem like much) and questioning the point of doing Alterac Valley at all.
While I sympathize with not wanting to do something that feels like a chore, it's a far worse problem to have an entire part of the game flattened into an AFK farm. Alterac Valley is supposed to feel like a large-scale war where you look at a big map and choose what objectives are worth fighting over as you try to weaken the enemy forces. The loot you get from maxing out your reputation with the associated factions is meant to be a reward for putting in the effort to learn what it takes to win.
The whole pitch for WoW: Forever is that it's not going to ditch everything with a new expansion every few years. Numbers can be tweaked down the line if the reputation grind is too much of a slog, but the mode should be fun to play so it's not treated like a box to check off in your character's journey. An inert PvP mode ruins the spirit of the MMO far more than a slightly longer reputation grind does.
I think this is a good example of a healthy change that shows Blizzard is committed to protecting core parts of the experience from becoming a treadmill that nobody enjoys. WoW: Forever's strengths are the ways it encourages you to participate in systems that aren't there to fill progression bars. As Harvey said in his WoW: Forever review , "Forever is proof that old-school MMO design deserves a second chance," and that requires taking a stance on what the game is and isn't meant to be.

pool.titulo: Lucia Actress Manni L. Perez Issues First Statement Since GTA 6 Launch
pool.resumen: Manni L. Perez, the actress who plays Lucia in GTA 6, has issued her first statement since the game came out.
pool.contenido:
Manni L. Perez, the actress who plays Lucia in GTA 6 , has issued her first statement since the game came out.
Perez’s role as Lucia Caminos was confirmed when she was nominated in the Best Performance category for this year’s The Game Awards , a day before GTA 6 launched on November 19. She’s now considered the favorite following the game’s critically acclaimed, record-breaking launch.
Now, a week later, Perez took to social media to thank fans for the reception to GTA 6.
“Life has been such a whirlwind these past couple of days and I just want to take a moment to say thank you,” an Instagram Stories post began.
“Thank you to all the new followers, to all the beautiful messages, and the positive reception the game and my character have received.
“I've dedicated almost a decade bringing Lucia to life. She's been such a significant part of mine and I am beyond grateful she now gets to be a small part of yours.”
“Happy Holiday's y'all.”
Perez is an actress with a smattering of credits to her acting resume, including TV guest roles in Jessica Jones, Chicago P.D., and Law & Order: Special Victims Unit. While she hasn't been up to much else over the past few years, it's easy to know why — GTA 6 sounds like it was a pretty involved project. Indeed, Lucia isn’t Perez's first GTA role. In GTA 5, she plays the background character of "Clubber #2," while in GTA Online she voices a blackjack dealer.
Meanwhile, Jason actor Dylan Rourke also posted a message of gratitude on Instagram Stories, saying: “Thankful for this wild ride. Gratitude won’t cut it. Make today about the ones you love.”
Manni L. Perez shouldn't be confused with Manny Perez, who plays Raul Bautista in GTA 6. This week, Manny Perez bought a PS5 just so he could play the game, saying in a video posted to social media: “Guy, I’m playing and this s**t is crazy! Look how real that looks. I’m learning, I’m loving this, it’s crazy.”
Other GTA 6 actors who've started to talk about their work on the game include Lexie Shoaibi, who recently spoke out about her "bittersweet" newfound fame after her character, Mandy, went viral online, and Cocoteo FM radio host Issa Lopez, who described the wild non-disclosure agreement she had to sign before working on the game .
Last month, the actors behind GTA 5's Franklin, Michael, and Trevor shared their advice for GTA 6's cast in a bid to ready them for the kind of fame few video game actors achieve.

pool.contenido:
It’s hard to believe it’s only been seven days since the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 . Still, with the staggering number of screenshots, videos, and everything else filling up social media feeds, anyone out of the loop would never know. I think much of this is due to just how many types of games Rockstar managed to cram into GTA 6. Everything from fixing up Jason’s house in the prologue to racing, billiards, birdwatching , and, of course, all the other gameplay we expect in GTA has created an almost Sims-like experience that is getting more people than ever to try the series. Seriously, though, the early sales numbers are bonkers.
My and many others' favorite things about GTA 6, in addition to just being a general menace to society, have been experiencing all the different kinds of gameplay and Rockstar fitting into it. pool.titulo: A pesar de las críticas por ser un 'código en caja', GTA 6 ha batido un récord en España con su versión 'física'
pool.resumen:
La revelación de que la versión 'física' de Grand Theft Auto VI consistiría solamente en un ' código en una caja ' generó un intenso debate en las redes sociales, pero eso no ha detenido a miles de personas de hacerse con esta polémica edición. Así lo confirman las primeras estimaciones al respecto: el título de Rockstar ha registrado cifras espectaculares con la venta de su formato 'físico' en varias partes del mundo. Y España también se incluye en este resultado, pues la venta de la caja del título ha sido tan elevada que hasta ha logrado batir un récord .
El dato ha salido a la luz por la firma de análisis Nielsen IQ, que ha desvelado nueva información relativa al rendimiento comercial de Grand Theft Auto VI en Reino Unido, Francia y España (vía The Game Business ). Los resultados obtenidos dentro de nuestras fronteras son tajantes: el viaje de Jason y Lucía por Leónida se ha establecido como el mayor lanzamiento en formato físico de la historia según los registros . En Francia, se ha contabilizado la venta de más de un millón de copias de GTA VI en su formato 'código en caja' durante sus tres primeros días en el mercado; una cifra que no se aleja mucho de lo que se observó allá

pool.titulo: Infinity Nikki Version 3.0 “Of Yesterday and Tomorrow” update live today on PS5
pool.resumen: Explore two new cities, experience nearly 10 hours of cinematic storytelling, discover new abilities and combat systems, and celebrate Nikki’s Birthday to enjoy 160 draws in total, plus 19 sets of clothes—all free. Today we announced Infinity Nikki Version 3.0, a major update that takes Nikki and Momo’s adventure to the Twin Cities of Art: […]
pool.contenido:
Explore two new cities, experience nearly 10 hours of cinematic storytelling, discover new abilities and combat systems, and celebrate Nikki’s Birthday to enjoy 160 draws in total, plus 19 sets of clothes—all free.
Today we announced Infinity Nikki Version 3.0, a major update that takes Nikki and Momo’s adventure to the Twin Cities of Art: Cicia and Ceremius, which releases on PS5 later today. Featuring nearly 10 hours of immersive story with cinematic presentation, the update introduces new exploration abilities, expanded combat systems, diverse open-world activities, and a more lifelike city experience. Alongside the new content, Version 3.0 and Nikki’s Birthday bring 160 draws and 19 sets of clothes, as well as improvements that make the adventure more accessible to new and returning stylists.
Twin cities of art, a new chapter: Of yesterday and tomorrow
In Version 3.0, Nikki and Momo’s adventure unfolds across Cicia and Ceremius, two cities that share a common origin but could hardly be more different.
Beyond everyday academy life in Cicia, the capital of art, Nikki gets caught up in strange anomalies on the streets and an investigation into the Rogues. Crossing the mist into Ceremius, she explores where the city’s past meets its present crisis, drawing ever closer to the truth about the Goddess des Arts.
New abilities, combat systems, and ways to explore
Across the two cities, stylists will have access to four key abilities: Veiling, Alchemy, Enhanced Floating, and Gemwork, adding more possibilities for exploration and puzzle-solving.
With the Veiling Ability, stylists can throw the Shadow Beetle and choose when to teleport. When it hits certain objects, they can switch to the object’s view and control it. Combined with the city’s anomalies and mechanisms in dungeons, movement becomes part of how stylists observe their surroundings, find their way, and solve puzzles.
Through Alchemy, stylists can gather materials in the open world and brew potions with Basic Recipes, or develop new recipes through trial-crafting. Potions can be used in combat, environmental puzzles, scene creation, and NPC interactions, connecting gathering, crafting, and exploration.
The Enhanced Floating ability allows Nikki to jump again in midair for a nimble double jump and dash forward through the air, while the Gemwork ability lets her discover and appraise uncut gemstones across the open world, then work them into gems for outfit crafting and Alchemy.
Combat also gains two new systems: firearms and magic, alongside a build system that adds depth and variety. Stylists can switch between the short musket for rapid fire and the long musket for aimed shots, while the staff allows them to cast different Oracle Arts based on their selected Nature’s Breaths and chant tiers. Combining these new ways of fighting with the build system lets stylists customize their combat style.
A living open world: From the streets of Cicia to the mysteries of Ceremius
In Cicia, stylists can drive through the city, run their own shop, and enjoy colorful urban life. Drive a car from Brise Automobile to complete passenger commissions, run the Warmhearted Boutique and put together outfits for customers, or discover activities such as the Scoop & Smile Creamery ice cream shop and Fuse Bead Art.
Meanwhile, Ceremius lies hidden in the mist. Stylists can awaken their alchemy skills, brew potions, and explore its fantastical flora and fauna. Unique activities such as relic restoration, old photo restoration, and divination turn the local lore into hands-on play.
Across both cities, immersive puzzle dungeons draw on stylists’ exploration abilities, combining miniature spaces, gear mechanisms, Rogue-style binding, and potion use to create new challenges as the story progresses.
The new Star Crown outfit: as stunning as it is powerful
Version 3.0 introduces the new Star Crown Resonance outfit, “Where Stars Shine Again,” alongside a lineup of new 5-Star and 4-Star Resonance outfits that combine artistic beauty with powerful abilities.
The Star Crown outfit comes with two weapons, the musket and the staff. With either equipped, unused dashes can be stored and released all at once or used one at a time. The outfit also adds four step-up bonuses and a free trial entry in the event hall, giving stylists the opportunity to experience its abilities before purchasing.
The new 5-Star Resonance outfit “When Light Falls Upon” unlocks Air Jumps and Air Dashes when equipped with its matching jump booster, alongside a stunning jump synergy effect. Meanwhile, the 4-Star Resonance outfits “Game for the Immortal” and “Beyond the Silence” summon chess pieces and a phantom from a fairy tale for playful interactions.
More outfits in a variety of styles will also arrive through anniversary celebrations, the Heart of Infinity, direct purchases, and cumulative top-up rewards.
More accessible, more lifelike: Version 3.0 Optimizations
Version 3.0 introduces a more flexible starting experience for stylists. New, veteran, or returning: every stylist can head straight to Cicia. New and returning stylists can skip the standard beginner tutorial, experience a new transitional tutorial, and use chapter select to pick a starting point from any story chapter released so far.
The update also enlivens the open world with large ambient NPC crowds, smoothly flowing traffic, and richer interactions across the city. Stylists will encounter taxi passengers with stories to tell, street musicians, NPCs dancing together, alchemy antics, and memorable character moments.
Ray-traced visuals have also received a significant upgrade. On supported devices, crowds and vehicles are now visible in reflections and shadows at medium and long distances, while reflections on wet roads, glass façades, and puddles feature greater depth and detail. Together, naturally moving crowds, traffic, and refined lighting create a richer atmosphere for exploration and photography.

pool.titulo: Microsoft announces it's deprecating the Telnet client in Windows, giving me a sudden flashback to when I used to use Telnet
pool.resumen: Just think what you'll be able to do with those extra 156 KB they're freeing up.
pool.contenido:
In its latest update on deprecated features in Windows , Microsoft casually mentioned that "Telnet Client is deprecated and will be removed from Windows in a future release."
This may not mean much to you if you didn't do a lot of computer networking in the 1990s or earlier, but the text-based protocol for remotely opening command-line interfaces was a workhorse we used for a bunch of things. It's how antique university lab computers that didn't even have Netscape Navigator installed connected to the internet, how I played text-based online games like the Discworld MUD back in the day, and how we used to connect to our routers.
By default, Telnet didn't encrypt all the data it was swapping back and forth between computers, which is why it's since been replaced by tools like SSH and PowerShell. So it's not a surprise that it's being deprecated, and honestly I'm impressed that it outlived both WordPad and Cortana .
A Windows feature being deprecated means that it won't be in active development and is a candidate for removal in a future update, so Telnet isn't being 86ed immediately. If you're still using it to test network connections because that's what you're used to then carry on as you were, but get ready to grumble and switch over to PowerShell when Microsoft finally does pull the plug.

pool.titulo: Vermintide 2 mod tools get a public release, and the game's 90% off on Steam too
pool.resumen: Holy Sigmar, bless this ravaged body.
pool.contenido:
Though Vermintide 2's had a Steam Workshop since 2018, it's mostly used for quality-of-life stuff like UI tweaks. That's set to change now that Fatshark has announced a public release of its internal developer tools, which they say "will allow modders to work their magic on both editing and creating anything from custom levels, models, textures, particles, animations, and more!"
Right now, only a select number of sanctioned mods can be used in Vermintide 2's "official realm" which is the one with loot and leveling that carries over, while unsanctioned mods can only be accessed in a "modded realm" where there are no progression systems. Obviously that's off-putting to a lot of players, so Fatshark has announced a change.
"We have an update releasing in early December which will see the Modded Realm have its own, local, offline progression. That means that playing in the Modded Realm will still result in you gaining loot and experience, but said progression will not reflect on the Official Realm. This should make playing on the Modded Realm feel much better and not be discouraging for those that want to try out all of the unsanctioned mods, both the ones that already exist and the ones to come thanks to the Mod Tools!"
I'm not sure how many players will be happy to start over from level one just to get access to a wider variety of mods, but I hope it encourages some folks to check them out. Another thing that'll encourage new players is that XP has been doubled from now through till Monday, and Vermintide 2 is on sale for 90% off on Steam . The DLC has been discounted too.
In less good news, the servers for Versus Mode are being turned off. "We have monitored the use of the dedicated Versus servers lately," Fatshark said, "and come to the conclusion that they are barely used. We have therefore decided to shut these down." Versus Mode will still be playable, but via the menu option for a custom game or the lobby browser. You'll have to find a crew to play with on Discord first, which is how everyone seems to play Versus at the moment anyway.
That shutdown is planned for early December, at the same time as the update that adds local progression to the modded realm. That update will also include balance changes to buff some unpopular talents, new weapon icons, and a Tome of Triumphs in the hub area that will point you at any event if there's a live one, or to the weekly event mode if there isn't. The next event planned is the annual return of Gifts of the Wolf Father in December.
Finally, Fatshark mentioned that focusing on the mod tools to get them ready for public release had to take priority from other updates. "The weapon pack and the level that we mentioned in the past has been put on hold," they wrote. "We still want to get back to that, especially the weapon pack, but for now there is no active development on that. It’s important for us that we have transparency here, and while we are not working on these things, we do stick with our games! We have plans both near and far for Vermintide 2."

pool.titulo: After Playing Infinity Nikki 3.0 for Four Hours, its New Cities and Outfits Are Just Some of the Additions Worth Returning For
pool.resumen: The new 3.0 update has tons of new stuff to explore including new locations, outfits and gameplay systems, although don't expect any kind of proper challenge.
pool.contenido:
When Infinity Nikki first launched in 2024, it introduced players around the world to the dress-up world of mobile game star Nikki in her first 3D console/PC adventure, an open world filled with wholesome fun, fashion and friendship. 2025’s V2.0 update introduced a new area to the world of Miraland, as well as new ways to traverse it. But now with the new V3.0 update titled Of Yesterday and Tomorrow, Nikki’s wonderful world has been expanded significantly – with its richest locations yet, and even a cute convertible to traverse it with.
To give you an idea of how huge this update is, I played for over four hours at developer Infold’s Shanghai office, focusing mainly on story content and with only the slightest bit of open-world exploration and lifestyle simulation gameplay, and didn't even see all of one of its two new cities. The golden path apparently offers some nine hours of story content, with two dense and exciting new areas to get lost in. Between the V3.0 launch and Nikki’s birthday celebration campaign, players can get 160 free draws and 19 new sets of clothing.
I spent most of my time in Cicia, a city of art, based loosely on Paris among other places, and lined with cobblestone streets and beatific brickwork architecture. Cicia was previously featured as a location in the mobile game Shining Nikki, and makes its 3D debut here. It’s a world where art nouveau, belle epoque and art deco collide, and home to the Cicia Art Academy where Miraland’s most promising students are taught lessons of art creation and appraisal by the finest tutors. When Nikki receives an invitation to study there, she and her catlike companion Momo embark on a new adventure of aesthetic discovery. But is everything at the academy truly as it seems?
Some of the outfits in the update grant Nikki new skills. Unlock and craft the preppy four-star Leaping Breeze outfit to gain a higher double-jump and airborne dash abilities, while the much darker and sexier Night’s Hidden Side outfit allows Nikki to “bind” with objects around the environment (think Mario’s possession skill in Mario Odyssey) and use them to warp to hard-to-reach places. These new skills allow for a new level of verticality in Cicia’s map and dungeons, helping you explore the castle spires or negotiate intricate dungeon maps.
You can also find a musket for long-range attacks (which is a new Whimtech item), and dress for the occasion in Cicia’s three-star, nine-piece outfit Song of Endless Youth.
V3.0 also introduces a new outfit category, Star Crown Resonance. The Star Crown Resonance outfit named Where Stars Shine Again comes with a musket and staff, and is designed for tougher combat situations. With either weapon equipped, Nikki’s unused dashes are stored, and you can release them all at once or use them one at a time, creating a sort of combo system that deals more damage.
While previous Infinity Nikki maps tended towards countryside locations, Cicia is a bustling city. Arriving by airship to take in the stunning views, Nikki and Momo step into a throng of students, teachers and residents, each with voiced dialogue to idly eavesdrop on as they prepare for a huge school festival, building an air of excitement as Nikki starts academy life. In this maelstrom of culture, recruiters for the drama club and literature club compete for Nikki’s attention.
And then she meets Béatrice Laviolette. A young ducal heiress, at first Béatrice is quite brusque, standoffish and snobby. It started to feel like meeting Glinda in the heightened magical environs of Shiz University, and when it was announced in a cutscene that the students would compete for the right to wear a legendary Miracle Outfit, I assumed Nikki and Béatrice were heading into a bitter rivalry. But Nikki has always been a relentlessly positive character, with a deep and forgiving heart and a desire to encourage those around her. Without wanting to spoil anything, let’s just say that she, Béatrice and earnest classmate Déphine Garnier foster a relationship that may surprise you.
Meanwhile, fellow student Sikong Ran invites Nikki to join his Society of Whispers and Wonders, a supernatural-obsessed group who study things that go boo in the night – lending more than a little taste of Wednesday or Riverdale high-school mystery.
Exploring the city is a reward unto itself. Rich and bustling with life, it features picturesque sunsets, glittering lakes, colourful flowerbeds, gargling fountains. It is filled with side missions and simple minigames, including one where you construct a street band to perform jolly jazz music in the castle plaza. In the streets, teachers guide students through artistic concepts that are interesting to read – for example, did you know that in music, technical perfection is no match for the heart of the musician? The characters you meet are endearing; and as before, the dialogue is filled with gentle humour – not least the central relationship between Nikki and Momo, which remains as heartwarming as ever.
But as you progress, Nikki learns that behind the magic of this idyllic city, there is a dark secret. Using her new binding skill to unravel environmental puzzles, she is drawn into a conspiracy that only Nikki can solve.
As part of this, I got to play through one of two new dungeons, titled The Ideal City. This is a clockwork house of tricks that recalls the steampunk-coded vibe of earlier Infinity Nikki dungeons, with huge cogs that alter the mechanical environments as they turn, and wooden theatre dioramas folding in and out of view in the background as you progress.

pool.titulo: Witcher 3 Remastered patch has lighting fixes, sign nerfs, and gets rid of a nasty werewolf bug
pool.resumen: Turns out they weren't meant to be that hard to kill after all.
pool.contenido:
If you replayed The Witcher 3 in its shiny new remastered form and got absolutely bodied by a couple of werewolf fights you thought were easier back when you had more youthful reflexes, don't worry—the problem wasn't your aging brain and hands after all. It was a bug that's been caught and exterminated in patch 5.02 . "Fixed an issue where werewolves could regenerate health too quickly on higher difficulty settings," the patch notes say, "making them impossible to defeat."
Another problem some players had with The Witcher 3 Remastered was its lighting, with interiors in particular looking too dark while some other locations were washed-out flashbangs. Good news: "Fixed various lighting issues across multiple locations and cutscenes," the patch notes say, "including overly bright or dark areas, inconsistent lighting transitions and flickering." They've also "Fixed various lighting issues with hair when Path Tracing is enabled" and "Made various Path Tracing and Ray Reconstruction optimizations and visual improvements, including lighting, shadows, and water rendering."
That's all positive stuff, but the balance changes to various signs and mutations will be more controversial. The Remastered version launched with buffs to Witcher signs that made them useful even if you didn't specialize in them, but it may have overdone things a little. This patch walks back some of the potential for you to dominate the entire game with an Aard build, though changes like reducing the Catalyst skill's bonus to Aard and Igni intensity by 10% don't seem like they'll totally change the way you play.
I get that people don't like skill nerfs in singleplayer games, but I can also see CD Projekt anticipating next year's Songs of the Past DLC . They don't want to hear a bunch of players say, "It sucked because I trivialized the whole thing with a broken build I got by copying a YouTuber." If some skill nerfs and a reduction to stamina regeneration in combat mean you have to drink more potions to get your signs off, it probably won't ruin your fun.
Oh, and if you couldn't complete your Gwent collection because Zoltan Chivay's card didn't show up, the patch notes say it'll now appear in the correct place under the Hanged Man's Tree in Velen. Time to go back and get that 100% achievement at last.

pool.titulo: Percy Jackson and the Olympians Season 3, Episodes 3 & 4 Recap and Review
pool.contenido:
Warning: This review contains full spoilers for Episodes 3 and 4 of Percy Jackson and the Olympians Season 3.
After a great season premiere to set up the show's new quest, Percy Jackson Season 3 dives straight into the action with Episodes 3 and 4. The Oracle's prophecy looms and death is in the air. The Greek mythology of it all is on full display as our heroes set out to save Annabeth, encountering ancient monsters and gods along the way. With four episodes down, the series is now firing on all cylinders.
Episode 3 kicks off right where Episode 2 left off. The Oracle has given the prophecy, the quest-goers have been chosen, and the mood is pretty somber. This is the first time in the series so far where we've seen the campers receive a quest that has the word "perish" right there. Artemis' Hunters and members of Camp Half-Blood were chosen to go on the quest, but Percy Jackson is noticeably absent from that list. Like every prophecy, however, the details are up to interpretation and Percy gets a surprising bit of help from Dionysus to bend the threads of fate and sneak him into the quest.
It takes Percy most of the episode to actually be reunited with the rest of the group, which means we get the chance to see Grover truly shine. Grover has been a part of two quests at this point and he knows exactly what to do. Even though he's with a daughter of Zeus and an elite Hunter of Artemis, he takes charge and gets everyone moving in the right direction. Whenever he pulls out that pan flute, you can trust him to find a way to hold everything together. And when he and Percy are finally reunited, he plays an essential role in evading the Spartoi and the taking on the Nemean lion .
And while Percy and Grover are the main drivers of the action in Episode 3, it's Bianca and Nico that bring the emotional depth. We watch Bianca (Olive Abercrombie) go from nervous protective sister to budding demigod warrior and can't help but root for her to succeed. Meanwhile, Nico (Levi Chrisopulos) pushes Percy to bring him along on the quest, showcasing his determination to help his sister. The di Angelo siblings' character development in this episode feels substantial, and it arrives just in time for the biggest tragedy of The Titan's Curse.
Episode 4 is Percy Jackson and the Olympians at its very best. The heroes are on the run from the relentless Spartoi and Nico is forced to part from his sister once again. But not before he makes Percy promise to protect her. This is a pivotal moment in the story, and Walker Scobell does an excellent job of portraying Percy's hesitation to make such a promise. He knows that at least one person is prophesied to perish on this quest, but he has this kid in front of him looking to put his faith in a hero, rather than a god. This promise adds to the weight Percy is already carrying, and things only get heavier for him from here on out.
The characters don't have much time to ponder the larger threads of fate as the Spartoi force the story forward with their relentless march After escaping the Spartoi (for now), Percy and crew have their first run-in with the gods. Ares is waiting outside a car with obvious hostile intent, which is only intensified by Thalia and Percy taking an equally aggressive stance to the meeting. But thankfully the God of War is only there on behalf of his lover, Aphrodite (Kate McKinnon). She reveals that not only are the gods planning a vote on whether or not to go to war, they will also be voting on whether or not to kill Percy and Thalia. It's their fear that one of the kids will slay the Bane of Olympus and fulfill the great prophecy, but Aphrodite says her vote is for Percy and the power of love. She then gives him the key to her husband's (Hephaestus) junkyard as a boon to help him on his quest.
Their encounter with Aphrodite is a good bit of storybuilding, unravelling just the right amount of the greater prophecy that haunts Olympus. It also sets Thalia down that same path of fear, working to convince Percy that it's now a kill or be killed situation they find themselves in. But the characters don't have much time to ponder the larger threads of fate as the Spartoi force the story forward with their relentless march. This all sets the stage for the reveal of the Junkyard of the Gods , which is a sight to behold.
As you might expect, the Junkyard of the Gods is a massive collection of legendary scrap. Huge piles of rusty metal tower into the sky and the atmosphere has an otherworldly orange desert hue. They may have escaped the Spartoi, but now they are somhwhere that feels dangerous on an entirely different level. It's out of the frying pan and into the fire as Percy and his friends accidentally activate a giant defense robot and find themselves having to split up. At this point, things are getting really serious and tensions are running extremely high.
Like any epic tale, impossible moments like these are what give heroes the opportunity to be heroes. While everyone is split into separate groups, Percy has found himself conveniently in a position where he can still hear everyone else, even if they can't hear him. And what he hears is the same fear that is plaguing Olympus, only it's creeping into the hearts of his companions. As the enormous robot stomps closer, he feels that same fear reaching him. It's only through a fortunate encounter with Tyson (via a magical call) that he is able to come up with a plan and shake that fear.
Bianca's character arc reaches its crescendo as fate puts her in a pivotal position to save everyone, and she leaps at the opportunity. With a plan in motion, Percy does what he does best and gives a rousing (if somewhat cheesy) speech to the group. Morale is lifted, fear is banished, and the group heads out to shut down the giant automaton currently hunting them. pool.titulo: Save 33% Off the Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 Sport Headphone With Bone Conduction Tech for Black Friday
pool.resumen: The best headphones for runners.
pool.contenido:
If you enjoy listening to music while you run or work out, then you should consider getting a headset that's specifically designed for it. Shokz is one of the best known and well-respected sport headphone brands and, fortunately for you, the Shokz Black Friday Sale has officially kicked off on Amazon .
As part of this sale, Amazon has dropped the price of the Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 open-ear wireless sport headphones in rose gold from $180 to just $119.99 with free shipping. All other colorways are on sale for $125, so stick with rose gold for the biggest savings. The OpenRun Pro 2 uses bone conduction technology to transmit sound without covering your ears.
33% Off the Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 Sport Headphones The OpenRun Pro 2 looks like a neckband style headphone except that a lightweight titanium band connecting the two ear pieces wraps around the back of your head instead of resting on your neck. This design does an excellent job of keeping everything in place, perfect for active exercise.
Instead of the traditional method of sending sound vibrations to your eardrums, the OpenRun Pro uses bone conduction technology to send vibrations through your cheekbones directly to your inner ear. As such, the headphones are actually placed in front of your ear instead of on your ear. The biggest advantage is that you can fully hear your surroundings; if you like running on streets, for example, you'll be aware of everything that's going on around you while your music is playing.
OpenRun Pro 2 is an obvious upgrade over the Open Run Pro The OpenRun Pro 2 is a substantial update over its predecessor. The most noticeable upgrade is arguably the switch from a proprietary magnetic charging cable to the USB Type-C standard. Another significant upgrade is the sound quality.
While the original OpenRun Pro has good bass response, it is slightly hampered by the fact that it produces tiny vibrations that are noticeable and sometimes ticklish or distracting. The new OpenRun Pro 2 utilizes Shok's DualPitch technology to virtually eliminate vibrations. Other smaller changes include increased battery life and improved mic quality.
The Shokz OpenRun are the best earbuds for exercise I have a pair of AirPods Pro that I use regularly, but I always set them aside for the OpenRun Pros when I run. The Transparency mode on the AirPods Pro does work well for most situations, but they still can't compare to the awareness you get without having any buds plugging up your ears. In my experience these headphones stay in place extremely well and the sound quality is great compared to other sport headphones I've tried.

While supplies last, you can pick up a Grade A refurbished Nintendo Switch 2 for just $409 after applying the coupon code BIGFRIDAY at checkout.
If you're a first-time Woot customer, there's an even better offer available. The same code knocks $60 off, bringing the console down to just $389 . Amazon Prime members also get free delivery, while everyone else will need to add $5 for shipping.
There are a couple of things worth keeping in mind before jumping in. This is a refurbished console, not a brand-new unit, and it comes with a 90-day Woot warranty. Still, if you're comfortable buying refurbished, it's a pretty substantial discount on Switch 2 hardware that's rarely included in major sales.
Best Switch 2 Game Deals for Black Friday 2026 Notably, the third-party physical game deals are considerably stronger than what's currently available for Nintendo's own first-party lineup.
Donkey Kong Bananza and Kirby Air Riders are two of the standout offers from Nintendo, but discounts are a little underwhelming for some of the more recent releases fans might have been hoping to see reduced, including The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Nintendo Switch Sports Resort, Star Fox, and more.
That's not to say there's a shortage of good games to pick up, though. There's still a healthy selection of third-party Switch 2 game deals worth checking out . Resident Evil Requiem, for example, is down to $39.99, while Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition is available for $59.99. Those are just a couple of highlights, with plenty more discounts worth digging through if you're looking to bulk out your library this Black Friday.
Walmart $30 Sale Walmart's Black Friday sale also featured a surprise drop of Nintendo games on sale for just $30 recently. Unfortunately (and as was expected) they sold out fairly quick. However, it's worth checking back on our rundown of this sale to see if any come back into stock.
The games in question are the Nintendo Switch 2 games Donkey Kong Bananza, Kirby Air Riders, Super Mario Party Jamboree + Jamboree TV, and the original Switch compilation Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy 2. That last one is a port of the 3D Mario classics from the Wii generation, if you can remember that far back.
Switch 2 Memory Card Deals One of the most worthwhile Black Friday buys for new Nintendo Switch 2 owners is a memory card . Nintendo's latest console comes with just 256GB of onboard storage, which might sound like plenty at first, but it can disappear surprisingly quickly once you start downloading games. And if you're planning to reuse a MicroSD card from your original Switch, I've got some bad news: it won't work.
While MicroSD Express cards might look almost identical to the older format, they're considerably faster and are the only type of memory card compatible with Switch 2. Samsung's P9 range is one of the options we've tested and recommended, with transfer speeds reaching up to 800MB/s.
Thankfully, there are some pretty decent discounts on Switch 2-compatible memory cards this Black Friday, including Samsung's P9 range.
Amazon currently has the highly rated Samsung P9 256GB MicroSD Express Card down to $44.99 with free shipping. That's a further $3 off the price we saw earlier this month, and one of the better offers I've spotted recently. The 512GB version is also on sale for $99.99.
Are these the lowest prices we've ever seen? No. Can you find cheaper alternatives? Absolutely, including this 512GB option from Onn . However, if you'd rather stick with a memory card we've actually put through its paces and recommend, the Samsung P9 is a solid choice. Our Samsung P9 MicroSD Express review is worth a read if you want the full breakdown.
And there's a pretty good reason to consider expanding your storage sooner rather than later. Switch 2 games are getting increasingly chunky, with Final Fantasy 14 currently taking the crown at around 117GB. That's almost half of the console's entire onboard storage gone on a single game.
Other particularly hefty downloads include Final Fantasy VII Remake Intergrade at 90GB, Split Fiction at 70GB, Cyberpunk 2077 at 60GB, and Hyrule Warriors: Age of Imprisonment at 44GB. Even The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time comes in at around 27GB.
Put simply, downloading just three or four particularly large games could leave you scrambling for storage space. That's why I'd argue a decent MicroSD Express card is one of the more sensible Switch 2 accessories

pool.titulo: Rockstar North Boss Knew Some GTA 6 Players Would 'Reject' New Systems Like Criminal Profiles, but Insists 'You Can Still Do Whatever You Wanted to Do Before'
pool.resumen: Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson knew some GTA 6 players would "reject" new systems like criminal profiles, but insisted "you can still do whatever you wanted to do before."
pool.contenido:
GTA 6 is by far the furthest Rockstar has pushed one of its games on a gameplay level. Perhaps nothing showcases that more than the criminal profile system ticking away in the background at all times, judging the way you act in its world as Jason and Lucia. No longer is Grand Theft Auto a sandbox where hedonism is widely encouraged, but a place that judges you for partaking in it.
It’s a system that has caused much debate within the player base, with some feeling as if they’re being punished for how they traditionally played GTA games. It was something that Rockstar admitted to have been a little worried about when YouTuber TGG visited the studio months ago and claimed it was "going to change GTA."
"I thought, 'Oh s**t, we’re in trouble,'" Rockstar co-studio head Rob Nelson told VGC . “But I said, 'It doesn’t change everything; it changes what GTA can be.' So for us, I think it opens a new range of choices and decisions for the player to make. You can still do whatever you wanted to do before, but now you have other options."
Warning! Spoilers for GTA 6 follow.
The criminal profile system reacts to how violently you choose to act throughout GTA 6’s open world and missions. Opt for headshot kills over debilitating kneecaps? You’ll move away from the "professional" end of the spectrum towards "psycho" and eventually "irredeemable." From experience, though, I can confirm that it takes quite the effort to reach that point on the scale after going on one murderous rampage after the next.
Which criminal profile you land on by the end of Jason and Lucia’s story will factor into which ending you get, but for the most part, it’s not something that necessarily needs to be playing on your mind at all times. My characters were considered “professional” at the end of my playthrough, and, believe me, I spilt my fair share of blood along the way.
Nelson appears to know that not all players will necessarily be on board with changes to the GTA formula like this, though, and expects some to "reject this new stuff we’re offering." He does hope it may help to make people think differently about how they approach Rockstar games in a post-Red Dead Redemption 2 world, though.
"I hope it changes the way players who want to engage with it play the game," Nelson continued to tell VGC. "In GTA 5 you started with a bank robbery in North Yankton, and you’re murdering like 40 cops off the rip, and you’re setting these guys up as what they are. We were conscious of that.
"Lucia takes the bullets out of the gun at the start of the game. She goes in, and it’s not like you can kill a bunch of people. So we wanted to start them off with a bit less baggage. They’re trying to make a go of this semi-legitimate life. When you pick up with Jason, he’s still a criminal; he’s still getting in trouble with Donnie and all that, but he’s sort of been living this relatively criminal-adjacent existence."
Whether GTA 6 feels like "classic GTA" or not is certainly a conversation to be had, but there’s no denying that the opening hours of Rockstar’s latest connects you to its characters more convincingly than the series has done in the past. Are you a fan of the criminal profile system? Let us know in the comments.
We’ve got the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide here on IGN, complete with comprehensive walkthroughs up to Chapter 5 , guides for the Optional Missions and Illegal Operations you’ll find in Leonida, and much more. Just getting started in Chapter 1 ? Check out our Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks , and make a note of the Best Free Weapons to Find Early . If you're already driving all around Leonida and want to know everything there is to find and do, see the Leonida interactive map .
