pool.titulo: Physical media is cool again, baby, so drop the needle on some videogame vinyls this Black Friday
pool.resumen: Music you can hold in your hands!
pool.contenido:
I am an absolute sucker for physical media—my bookshelves are adorned with generations of console games, I have a CD stash tucked away in my Mum's attic, and I still refuse to buy a Kindle in favour of good ol' fashioned paper and ink. And as we increasingly veer into a more digital age, I've noticed a huge uptick in people yearning to bring their hobbies and collections back into a more tangible form.
Music, especially, has seen a huge resurgence in physical popularity. Y'all, my best friend is buying CDs and ripping them onto his PC. Like the good old days! And we've also seen an increasing number of videogame soundtracks make their way onto CD and vinyl, which is something that I am a huge fan of. I love music. I love videogames. I love things I can hold in my hands. It's a triple win!
We're curating all the Black Friday PC gaming deals right here Unfortunately, this Black Friday hasn't brought about a ton of good deals on videogame vinyl. But that doesn't mean there aren't little offers to be found here and there. So if you're fixing to expand your physical media collection—or seeking out a gift for the videogame music lover in your life—I've got you covered.
If you're looking to scoop up a few albums at once, Target is currently doing a Buy 2 Get 1 Free deal on all its music. It's got a pretty tasty library of videogame OSTs among its 49 pages of soundtrack music, such as:

pool.titulo: Someone Is Making One of Baldur's Gate 3's Most Popular Villains Romanceable
pool.resumen: One of Baldur's Gate 3's main villains, Gortash, could be romanceable soon thanks to this new fan-made mod.
pool.contenido:
Baldur's Gate 3 has no shortage of romances and romantic encounters, but not everyone in Faerûn is up for a smooch.
When developer Larian was still rolling out updates, fans would often ask for more romances to be added, whether it be for Jaheira or Rolan, but it was never meant to be.
One of the most popular requests was actually for one of Baldur's Gate 3's main villains, Gortash. Larian was very much aware of this, and actually addressed these fans in the patch notes in 2024.
"Listen, he’s a complicated guy who’s busy contemplating the minutia of death cult office politics," Larian said at the time. "Babygurl doesn’t have time to kiss."
But now, a fan is stepping up, adding the Gortash romance that so many were asking for. TikTok user Equipouet has shared some clips from the mod, which is still a work in progress. It shows the player character being invited to spend time with Gortash, played by Lucius Malfoy actor Jason Isaacs, after his coronation in Act 3, all with new dialogue and animations.
We're told that we'll be able to make our own choices when we meet Gortash, specifically whether we want to "charm him, keep him guessing, or walk away." So, if you really hate Gortash, you could also use the mod to let him down.
Much more is teased for the mod, like a ball held by Gortash, letters to exchange with him, and "choices with consequences." There will also be changes to how the story plays out if your character is The Dark Urge, since it's in your backstory that you already have a history with Gortash.
The mod is still being worked on, but the author says they will submit it for console release approval once it's done. That process can be lengthy, however, and there's no guarantee that it will pass the approval stage, especially if it's too bulky for console.
In the meantime, Gortash kissers will keep having to use their imagination. Like us would-be Jaheira kissers. There are also plenty of other mods to try out, including a bunch that have Larian's seal of approval and can be installed within the game's own mod manager.
Image credit: Larian.

pool.titulo: PC Gaming Can Be Stupid Expensive Right Now, But I've Done My Best at Finding the Best Deals Possible for Everything You Might Need
pool.resumen: PC gaming is pricey right now, but these Black Friday 2026 deals on mice, keyboards, monitors and headphones can help you save a little chunk of money.
pool.contenido:
Let's face it -- 2026 hasn't been the best year for PC gaming when it comes to pricing. The AI boom has seen everything with memory in it shoot up in price, ranging from GPUs to SSDs, not to mention RAM itself.
This has obviously had a rotten knock-on effect when it comes to deals holidays such as Black Friday. Components that we'd usually bank on being discounted to a degree simply aren't at the moment, meaning I've had to look a little harder than usual to find some reductions for your delight and delectation.
There is a silver lining, though. Certain items relating to PC gaming haven't gone up at all - think peripherals, monitors and all the rest of it.
If you can't upgrade your gaming rig this Black Friday, then do something for me and take your setup to the next level outside of the PC itself. Everything from fast gaming keyboards to capable gaming mice, dazzling OLED monitors and more are discounted across the interwebs, and there are some real deals to be had. Read on below to find out more.
TL;DR: Best Black Friday Peripherals Deals Black Friday Gaming Mice Deals Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike We're starting off strong with a small, but important reduction on one of Logitech's top-class gaming mice - the G Pro X2 Superstrike is the first ever gaming mouse from the Swiss brand to feature rapid trigger and haptic feedback under its main mouse buttons for faster and more responsive inputs than more conventional gaming mice.
It's down to $150 on Amazon, marking out a $30 discount on its usual MSRP - granted, there is the new G Pro X3 Superstrike that released in September, but this remains a very capable and unique mouse for FPS gaming in my testing elsewhere. It retains the same super lightweight shell as the venerable G Pro X Superlight 2 (a deliberate decision to make it easier for pro players to transition to) and the more neutral and symmetrical shape. The two-tone black-and-white shell gives it a distinctive look, too, while the little crosses are a nod to crash-test dummies, according to Logitech's engineers.
As well as its innovative HITS haptic tech, the Superstrike also has a zippy 44,000 DPI sensor, and 8000Hz wireless polling for fast, responsive inputs. Connectivity is purely by 2.4GHz, as this rodent eschews Bluetooth in favour of trimming the fat -- this is a purely performance focused option. Battery life is up to 90 hours at 1000Hz, making this a competitive choice for extended play, too.
Corsair Sabre V2 Pro If the Superstrike is a step too far for your budget, the Corsair Sabre V2 Pro is a brilliant alternative, and at $50 it's roughly half its $99 MSRP. This is an ultralight wireless mouse built squarely for competitive FPS play, weighing just 36g, which is featherweight even among the best esports mice. It's a compact, symmetrical shape designed with fingertip and claw grips in mind, so it suits players who like to flick their wrist rather than plant their palm.
The spec sheet is impressive for the money. There's a 33,000 DPI Corsair Marksman S sensor for zippy movement, plus up to 8000Hz polling over 2.4GHz wireless, putting it in the same hyper-polling league as the Superstrike above. Customisation is handled through Corsair's browser-based Web Hub, which lets you remap buttons, set DPI stages and change the polling rate without installing bloated software. Corsair also includes spare mouse skates and grip tape in the box, which is a nice touch at this price.
There are a few trade-offs to be aware of. Battery life is rated at up to 70 hours at 1000Hz, but that plummets to around 16 hours if you crank the polling rate to 8000Hz, so you'll want to be selective about when to use it. There's also no Bluetooth, no RGB and no dedicated DPI button on the mouse itself. But if you want a lightweight, fast and very capable FPS mouse for pocket change, it's hard to argue with. Check out our best gaming mice guide to see how it stacks up against its rivals.
Black Friday Gaming Keyboard Deals Keychron K2 HE The Keychron K2 HE combines Hall effect magnetic switches with the compact, much-loved K2 layout, and it's one of the most accessible ways to get adjustable actuation on a wireless board. Inside are Gateron's double rail HE switches, which feel stable with virtually no key wobble. Instead of a fixed actuation point, you can set it anywhere from 0.5mm to 3.8mm in 0.1mm steps on a per-key basis, using Keychron's web-based Launcher software, which works on both Windows and macOS and also handles remapping and macros.
In my review elsewhere, I set WASD and my weapon-select keys to the shortest actuation distance in Counter-Strike 2, and the difference was noticeable: it's almost as if you barely need to breathe to register the input, which helps no end for quick-draw moments and grenade throws. The same switches feel smooth for typing too, as they're pre-lubricated, and the K2 HE sounds fantastic, with a creamy sound profile and no case rattle or ping.
Build quality is superb, with a hefty 966g chassis that shows no deck flex, a far cry from the lighter standard K2. Connectivity is flexible, too, with Bluetooth, a 2.4GHz receiver and wired USB-C all on offer, and the 4000mAh battery lasts up to 72 hours with the backlight on, or as much as 240 hours with it off. It's technically hot-swappable, but only a very limited selection of switches will fit given this is a Hall Effect product, so this is best bought for what's already inside it.

pool.titulo: This Star Wars Vehicles Encyclopedia Is Surprisingly Cheap For Black Friday
pool.contenido:
If you've been enjoying Star Wars Galactic Racer, this book is perfect for you. The Star Wars Complete Vehicles (new edition) is currently on sale at Amazon for Black Friday , and it's at its lowest price we've seen. Pick up the hardcover book for $17.30, down from its $40 sticker price. At this price, it's a good time to pick one up if you're on the hunt for good Star Wars gifts before the winter holidays are here.
Note : This is an Amazon Lightning Deal, so once the discount is fully claimed, the price will go back up.
Written by longtime Star Wars archivists Pablo Hidalgo and Jason Fry with illustrations by Richard Chasemore, the Star Wars Complete Vehicles hardcover book is a 264-page visual collection of virtually every ship, fighter, speeder, and other vehicles seen throughout the vast Star Wars universe. Each vehicle entry is an extremely detailed breakdown of the ins, outs, and mechanics of each vessel, with in-depth descriptions of parts, functions, lore, history, and even manufacturers.
Everything from X-Wings and podracers to TIE Fighters and even the Death Star's weaponry are displayed in great detail if you've ever been curious about how these machines function. Every era in the Star Wars universe is explored as well, so you'll see detailed markups of Clone Wars-era Republic Gunships and even Poe Dameron's X-Wing from the time of the First Order.
It's the perfect time to check this out with how popular Star Wars Galactic Racer has been since it came out a few months ago. We gave it 8 out of 10 in our review , thanks to its fast and frenetic racing mechanics and Roguelite setup.
Editor's Note : The Star Wars Vehicles Encyclopedia is rooted in Disney's version of Star Wars canon , which excludes anything outside of George Lucas' Star Wars trilogies and the Disney TV shows and movies that followed. That means you shouldn't expect to see characters or vehicles featured in Star Wars Legends media here.

pool.titulo: Despite Take-Two Takedown, Vibecoding Teen Behind Nuked GTA 6 PC Port Project 'Leonida' Vows to Continue
pool.resumen: The 15-year-old vibecoder behind a GTA 6 PC port project Take-Two recently shut down has vowed to continue their work despite the potential for further action from the company.
pool.contenido:
The 15-year-old vibecoder behind a GTA 6 PC port project Take-Two recently shut down has vowed to continue their work despite the potential for further action from the company.
‘NotRexed’ is behind ‘Project Leonida,’ which was at one point leading the race to create a PC port of GTA 6 following the recent leak of an Xbox build. Cyberleek, the infamous leaker behind many early GTA 6 gameplay clips, reportedly released the Xbox build of GTA 6 last week, and vibecoders have been attempting to port the game to PC since.
Fueled by AI, progress has been swift, with clips showing GTA 6 running on PC at a higher frame rate than on console, and one video even showing basic multiplayer. Obviously, Rockstar Games, which will no doubt release GTA 6 on PC officially at some point, and parent company Take-Two will be watching the homebrew scene’s every move like a hawk.
In the case of Project Leonida, Take-Two has already taken action. NotRexed was organizing and sharing work on a Discord group, and hosting their findings on a GitHub repository, when cease and desists from Take-Two hauled everything offline. NotRexed then took to social media to announce they'd decided to call it a day.
“I quit guys. I’m sorry,” NotRexed said. “I really want to make cool stuff but every single time s**t happens that I can’t control so I’m stepping away. Thank you everybody, especially in the Discord that allowed me to have this opportunity.”
NotRexed went on to insist that they were finding it tough to run Project Leonida while also going to school. “Rockstar taking my server down was only part of the reason. Like I’ve said before, I’m a 15-year-old kid,” they said. “Managing school and sports is hard enough without having middle aged men yell and complain to you on Discord. Goodbye.”
However, NotRexed has now returned, and promised to continue the project. “Ignore my other posts,” NotRexed said after changing their mind. “Something’s coming soon. Leonida is NOT dead. I have been doing a lot of work behind the scenes. I’ll have some stuff to show all of you soon.”
IGN spoke to NotRexed to find out why they’re doing this, whether they understand the risks, what they’ll do if they get in legal trouble, and what their parents think of it all.
“It’s just a hobby of mine,” NotRexed said in a private message. “I started doing similar things with porting games to the web back in the start of 2026, and I’ve always just thought of it to be cool.”
Before generative AI, NotRexed had no interest in porting games to other platforms, they said. But after finding out it was possible in 2025, they’re now taking on one of the most powerful publishers in video games. Interestingly, there’s no real motive behind it.
“I’ve always been interested in tech and mess around with it a lot,” they said. According to them, even their parents are aware of what they do and are largely supportive of it. “Yes, they know about all my projects and work I do, and they’re pretty encouraging about it,” they claimed.
It made me wonder if they were fully aware of the legal risks involved in such an undertaking. “Yea, they have warned me about what could happen,” NotRexed insisted when I asked if their parents knew about the potential legal issues. “I’m still continuing my work as of now tho because even tho T2 took down my repo and Discord they have never sent an email or message directly to me. If I do get into legal trouble I’m probably gonna stop working on it but possibly have a friend continue it.”
How feasible is this? IGN asked Matt Freedman, a veteran game developer with expertise in both traditional development and the controversial emerging technology of AI.
“A recompilation is different from a port,” Freedman said. “But yes, an AI driven recompilation of GTA 6 is very doable and wouldn't have the same 'game feel' problems that an AI-driven port would have.”
He went on to explain the differences between decompilations, recompilations, and ports. A decomp is where someone manually reverse engineers a game to run on other systems, like the Mario 64 PC port. “This is very time consuming and requires a human to do the work and effectively 'guess' how the game works,” he said.
A port takes existing assets or creates new ones and essentially builds a new version of the same game to work on another system. The Witcher 3’s Switch port is an example of this. “A team took The Witcher 3 code base and assets and then modified them by hand to work on the Switch,” he said.
For recomps, people use large language models (LLMs) to break down a game and rebuild it, essentially reverse engineering the title for whatever system the user wants. “Since LLMs natively can read binary, they're able to understand the specific code better than humans can,” Freedman explained.
A decomp or port of GTA 6 would not be easy — not least because Rockstar uses proprietary tech, including its in-house Rage engine, to power its games. “When it comes to AI, it'll depend on how well it has previously seen the engine or the low level SDK,” Freedman replied when asked about this complication. “A well studied proprietary engine with lots of public information would be easier for it to understand. A custom engine for an obscure CPU would be much more difficult for it.
“So, something like Rockstar's Rage engine would be more difficult for it to figure out than something like a game made in Unreal. But… given that a 15-year-old was able to have an AI port GTA 6 to PC, it's clearly not the biggest lift out there.”
All the while, Take-Two is working to take down various homebrew community efforts from GitHub, as the race to release an unofficial GTA 6 PC port appears close to the finish line. There’s even a website tracking the various attempts to recompile, emulate, or port the leaked Xbox Series build to PC.

pool.titulo: Christopher Nolan (56 años) tiene instrucciones para ver La Odisea en tu casa, y son casi tan exigentes como las que da a los cines
pool.resumen:
Si pensabas que ver La Odisea (The Odyssey) en cine tal como quería su director era, en sí mismo, una Odisea, que sepas que tu viaje no ha terminado. Christopher Nolan tiene un consejo para ver su última en casa, y no pasa por la tele. “Soy muy fan de los proyectores”, decía en unas declaraciones a Polygon . Según él, hoy se puede tener en el salón un proyector de bastante calidad por relativamente poco dinero, y montarte así tu propio minicine. Lo cuenta ahora que la peli está en 4K y en digital, y no me sorprende nada. Era cuestión de tiempo que alguien que pone tantas pegas a las proyecciones convencionales de los cines empezara a sacarle falta también a tu casa.
Para ver La Odisea tal y como se rodó hacía falta una de las 41 salas del mundo que pueden proyectar película IMAX de 70 mm en formato 1.43:1, y ninguna está en España, como ya os contamos . Y ni siquiera en esas selectas salas se libraban de sus indicaciones: Pat Caldwell, un veterano proyeccionista de IMAX, resumía en una entrevista con Vulture los consejos del director en una frase: "No hagáis ninguna tontería"

pool.resumen:
El mundo del videojuego está plagado de grandes injusticias ; de juegazos increíbles que por unas u otras razones no terminaron de alcanzar el éxito merecido. La lista es interminable. Tan larga que es fácil olvidarse de algunas de estas joyas. Pero siempre están ahí, y cuando llegan fechas como este Black Friday en el que todas las tiendas digitales ofrecen montones de juegos a precios de risa , te las encuentras por casualidad y casi sin darte cuenta, te pones triste porque no triunfaron. También nostálgico, por supuesto, ya que cuesta resistir la tentación de echarse una nueva partida. Y es justo lo que me ha pasado con Nox , el action RPG con el que nos sorprendía Westwood Studios hace prácticamente 26 años, y que hoy mismo puedes comprar por algo más de un euro.
Este juego de los autores de Command & Conquer, uno de los estudios más legendarios de la historia , tuvo la mala suerte de aparecer en las tiendas apenas unos meses antes que Diablo II , lo que afectó a sus ventas y de paso, le puso encima una etiqueta que no hacía justicia a lo que realmente era Nox. pool.titulo: Acusaron a NVIDIA de mentir a sus accionistas mientras los jugadores sufríamos sus precios altos. Pagará una multa millonaria por ello
pool.resumen:
Aunque hoy en día NVIDIA vive una época dorada gracias a la inteligencia artificial, internamente su situación ha ido dando tumbos en los últimos años hasta chocar contra un muro enorme este mes de noviembre con la salida de Jensen Huang de la compañía . Si bien el CEO de la compañía ha regresado y las aguas parecen haberse calmado, el propio Huang ha sido protagonista de otras polémicas que han puesto en tela de juicio su liderazgo . Hace apenas una década, el ejecutivo encontró otro filón económico en una industria ajena a los videojuegos: la minería de criptomonedas . Un mercado que disparó las ventas de GPU, pero que también llevó a la compañía a los tribunales bajo la acusación de haber engañado a sus accionistas . Ahora, NVIDIA ha acordado pagar una millonada para poner fin a dicha demanda colectiva.
Para entender el origen de esta demanda hay que remontarse a 2017, cuando el auge de criptomonedas como Ethereum convirtió las tarjetas gráficas más potentes de la compañía, destinadas a su uso en equipos gaming, en herramientas para hacer dinero. pool.titulo: New Avengers: Doomsday Teaser Shows Steve Rogers in Latveria, Potentially Names Doom's Son
pool.resumen: Marvel Studios has released yet another Avengers: Doomsday trailer, this one focusing on Steve Rogers doing "what needs to be done" in Latveria.
pool.contenido:
Marvel Studios has released yet another Avengers: Doomsday trailer, this one focusing on Steve Rogers doing "what needs to be done" in Latveria.
The clip, which is doing the rounds on social media, starts with Rodgers and Peggy Carter’s son asking him if he was a superhero, as we saw and heard in the final trailer released earlier this week.
“There were six of us,” he replies. “We were called the Avengers.”
🚨Novo spot de #AvengersDoomsday com cenas inéditas da Disney Turquia. https://t.co/tYiOJDL3ny
— Taverna Marvel (@TavernaMarvel) November 27, 2026
We then get a fun meta joke about Steve Rogers actor Chris Evans having played The Human Torch in the Fox-produced Fantastic Four films — a role he reprised in cameo form in Deadpool & Wolverine.
“So, can you fly?” asks his son, as Thor leaps at Doom for yet another look at that finger block. “Turn into fire,” he continues, as the MCU’s Human Torch, played by Joseph Quinn, hurtles out of a building to spray fire on what looks like a Doom magic-protected device below. “Or shoot lasers out of your eyes?” he adds, referencing Cyclops doing his thing.
“No, I can’t do any of that,” Steve replies with a smirk.
“So, what do you do?”
At this point we see new footage of Steve in Latveria, the fictional Eastern European nation ruled by Doctor Doom. He’s standing by some sort of circular device, with Doom’s name on it, and summons Mjölnir. After it flies into his hand, Steve draws lightning power to seemingly strike the device.
As we wonder what this is all about, Peggy answers: “He does what needs to be done.”
We then see Steve flying up towards the camera, hammer first, via the Bifrost. So, in a way, he can fly!
Let’s go back to the circular device Steve was about to hit with the lightning. From the wording on the side, it looks like a tomb of sorts for Victor von Doom’s family. We see ‘Malachi von Doom,’ who we presume is Doom’s deceased son.
If this is a tomb for Doom’s family, why is Steve about to smack it with Mjölnir? Is he trying to break into the grave? Could he be trying to resurrect Doom’s wife and kid? Is that what Peggy meant by "he does what needs to be done"?
The Avengers: Doomsday teasers are coming thick and fast as we head towards launch. Earlier this week we got a first look at Magneto vs Doom (and a failed attempt to rip Doom’s mask off), news of plans for a special tribute to Patrick Stewart , a first look at Kelsey Grammer's Beast , and fears over Bucky’s fate .

pool.titulo: I Tried to Get Six Stars in GTA 6 With Just One Bullet and Broke the Game
pool.resumen: We tried to get six stars in GTA 6 by firing just one bullet and broke the game.
pool.contenido:
If reaching a six-star wanted level in Grand Theft Auto 6 is your goal, there are many different methods available to you. Raiding the military base for a tank is one way. Committing a horrifying beach massacre is another. But can you get there by firing just a single bullet? We at IGN had a theory that this was absolutely possible, and so spent hours in a fast food joint to find out.
When we say “by firing a single bullet,” we mean that technically speaking. Our theory is that your chosen character only needs to pull the trigger once. That’s because, when roaming around GTA 6’s open world and causing whatever brand of chaos you’ve chosen to, your partner will automatically take up the fight against aggressors, and is both invulnerable and stocked with unlimited ammunition. That means if you decide to walk into a heavily populated area as a couple and fire just one bullet into the crowd, your better half can commit the lion's share of the atrocities themselves, provided you just stay alive.
We tested this out for ourselves, leading Jason and Lucia to the Taco Bomb in Gellhorn as our chosen arena of violence. Taking control of Jason, one bullet was fired into a poor staff member taking a break outside. Bits of brain now covered the forecourt, which somehow still looked like a more appetising alternative to whatever the questionable-looking beef was they were offering inside. Creeping cannibalistic thoughts pushed to one side, we walked back inside knowing our work was done. This public execution, perhaps rightfully, attracted a police patrol car to the restaurant, of which Lucia did not take kindly to their arrival.
Her love for Jason knows no bounds, up to and including unloading full machine gun magazines into any cops who want to arrest him. And who were we to stand in her way? Letting her take control of the situation was then required, honorably moving Jason behind the indestructible cover of an industrial refrigerator. Sporting an armoured vest just in case any stray bullets or shrapnel found their way around the corner, it was then time to hunker down in the kitchen beside that thick metal fridge, out of view of law enforcement. Crucially, this fast food establishment’s kitchen does not have a door leading outside, meaning the threat of flanking cops was neutralised. Luckily, they didn’t seem to spot the drive-thru window, which would’ve handed them a clean shot.
Could a six-star wanted level be achieved by us, the player, firing just one bullet? And there we sat for a good 45 minutes as Lucia angrily gunned down anyone brave enough to step into the restaurant. No more food would be served today, only death. The red of discarded hot sauce packets replaced by the blood of the fallen. The crunch of hard shell tacos drowned out by the crack of broken bones. All in the name of science. Could a six-star wanted level be achieved by us, the player, firing just one bullet?
Well, not this time. We could’ve sat here forever, bravely hiding behind a fridge while our partner slaughtered hundreds. Lucia was invincible, rounds of ammunition sinking into her skin to no effect. She had no shortage of ammo herself; with an unlimited pool of lead to reload from, she could’ve done this all day, and all for us. If that isn’t true romance, I don’t know what is. Day turned to night, and the restaurant workers diligently remained kneeling behind the counter and cowering for the whole sordid ordeal.
The problem is, our aggressors just… stopped. After a period of quiet, we chose to break cover and wander outside, only to be met by several non-aggravated members of law enforcement staring blankly at us. We had seemingly confused them with our methods of madness.
Because we’re so dedicated to the cause here at IGN, we tried all over again. Putting this first attempt down as an unfortunate glitch, we reloaded a save, made our way to Taco Bomb, and fired a single gunshot into our chosen test subject. And so, another hour of hiding behind a fridge commenced while our incredibly committed girlfriend peppered anyone who dared approach us with bullets. Armoured trucks eventually surrounded the exits, and the sound of helicopter blades could be heard above. But the same thing happened again. We even waited long enough for the rest mode settings on our PS5 to almost put the console to sleep.
Could just one grenade be our key to maxing out the wanted level? It seems GTA 6 gets very confused if you decide to start a chain reaction like this, only to go passive for the next 60 minutes. Again, five stars were secured on the wanted level, but that sixth just wouldn’t arrive. The enemy AI’s brain could not comprehend what was happening, so we decided we simply had to intervene. If that sixth star was going to be ours, we’d need to get involved ourselves.
Thus, we thought we’d honor the place we’d called home for the past couple of hours, and end our occupancy of Taco Bomb with an explosion. A bunch of incapacitated, but not dead, cops lay writhing on the floor of the restaurant. Could just one grenade be our key to maxing out the wanted level? There was only one way of finding out. We ended the whole bloody affair with a bang, ripping the pin out of the explosive before hurling it into the mound of bodies. And that’s when it happened. Nirvana. The gates of heaven opened. Six-star paradise was ours to bask in.
So, what was the point of all of this? Well, more than anything, to confirm that you never have to worry about Jason or Lucia dying when roaming around GTA 6’s open world when not controlling them. Unlike in missions, where they can slip off this mortal coil, they can’t die in free-roam, and so you are clear to use them as superpowered distractions or unkillable meat shields if you wish. You don’t have to be as cowardly as we were, but if you have an hour free to watch an action movie scene play out while peeking out from behind the corner of a refrigerator, then that option is available to you.

pool.titulo: Hollow Knight: Silksong - Sea of Sorrow Launch Trailer Finally Confirms Release Date, Teases Fishing
pool.resumen: Team Cherry's latest showcase gives us a release date for Sea of Sorrow, the free DLC expansion coming to Hollow Knight: Silksong, and a launch trailer.
pool.contenido:
Team Cherry has just wrapped up its Cherry Time! showcase, giving us some long-awaited news on the future of Hollow Knight: Silksong.
The big takeaway here is that Hollow Knight: Silksong's first big expansion, Sea of Sorrow, finally has a release date of December 11. Sea of Sorrow will be available to all Silksong players for free. All you need is a copy of the base game, and you can start playing Sea of Sorrow when it goes live on December 11.
This also means Team Cherry has stuck to its promise to get Sea of Sorrow out by the end of the year. Some had feared that today's announcement would be a delay — or an announcement that the DLC was being expanded into a full game, which is famously how Silksong's development began.
In the showcase, we got a new look at Sea of Sorrow's gameplay. This gives us a good preview of what's in store for us, as we see new areas, enemies, and boss fights. Of course, it all looks as challenging as ever, as you'd expect for Silksong's post-launch DLC. And is that a fishing mini-game teased at the end?
We weren't told anything else about the future of Silksong or the Hollow Knight series at large. There was no mention of this being Silksong's only expansion, so it's very possible that Team Cherry plans to support the game beyond Sea of Sorrow.
For now, here's the official blurb on Sea of Sorrow:
In Sea of Sorrow, players will voyage above and beneath Pharloom’s forgotten ocean, across islands, through forts and into deep caverns beneath the waves. We’ve spent the whole year stuffing this adventure full with all the things you’d expect from Hollow Knight: Silksong - crazed characters, high adventure, and epic bosses! It’s also overflowing with more exceptional music by the eternally talented Christopher Larkin! We’re pretty darn excited to get it into all of your hands on December 11, so please look forward to it. Outside of this reveal, Team Cherry used the attention to promote indie games from other studios. Three were shown off: Blockan and the Walking City, which is fully hand-drawn; Radio Rain, which is centred around 1980s-inspired music; and The Botanist and the Translator, which boasts a Sailor Moon-esque vibe.
In a follow-up blog post , Team Cherry confirmed that these new games will release under the new Team Cherry Presents label, which is headed up by the indie developer's fourth team member, Huy Le. Huy is technical director and on-going support for all the Team Cherry Presents games, but has also helped out on Silksong and Sea of Sorrow. "As a long-time team of three people, adding a fourth member is a big deal!" Team Cherry said.

pool.titulo: On Top of Everything Else, GTA 6 Is a Solid Stealth Sandbox
pool.resumen: I came to GTA 6 for its wild car chases and explosive shootouts, but its the really solid stealth that has me hooked.
pool.contenido:
This is an opinion piece from writer Samuel Horti. IGN's opinion columns represent the personal viewpoints of the writer, drawing on their own experiences and research to explore the exciting world of video games.
Grand Theft Auto is a boisterous, brash series full of loud characters and louder explosions. GTA 6 continues that tradition for many of its main story beats, chaining showy set-pieces into lethal car chases, but in my 35 hours roaming Leonda I've found plenty of chances to engage with its surprisingly robust stealth system. In some cases, it even feels like Rockstar specifically designed areas with sneaking and silencers in mind.
Illegal operations are lucrative robbery opportunities dotted around the map that hide cash, jewellery, drugs, and unique items – cars, weapons, watches – guarded by armies of enemies. I struggled with them early on: shooting my way to the valuables attracted GTA 6's menacing police, curtailing my heists before I could grab all the loot and forcing me to flee across entire counties while a chopper buzzed overhead.
Now, I treat these scenarios like stealth vignettes, my goal to remain hidden for as long as possible. I've screwed silencers onto my weapons and prioritized headshot precision over spraying power, carrying a pistol alongside either a tactical rifle or a sniper. My shotgun is purely for backup, just in case.
Skirting around these hideouts reveals hidden entrances. For Janjak's Garage in Vice City, for example, you can mantle a dumpster in a neighbouring alley to reach the garage's sheet metal roof. Out West, on the edge of Port Gellhorn, you can avoid the main gates of the giant Brooks Boatworks and slip through holes in the fence.
Stealth detection is intuitive. Crouching reduces noise, sightlines feel realistic, and you'll be warned by a yellow arrow over an enemy's head before they fully spot you, allowing you a window to nip back into cover. Knives silently slice enemies' open or you can choke them quietly from behind. And if you need space, you can whistle from cover to draw foes over, or throw bottles to distract them. It's classic stealth game fare.
But I've found that guns with silencers are actually the best option because they avoid the risk of an enemy spinning around at the wrong moment and catching you, knife raised. They mask shots almost completely: I've stood close to enemies and shot at others without being detected. Not everything in GTA 6 adopts Rockstar's general pursuit of realism.
Illegal operations feel like the real test of your sneakiness, and I'm relishing each new one that pops up on my map. Clusters of enemies are tricky because as soon as you shoot one, the others will spin and look for you. Here, I use focus mode to slow time and pop a series of headshots, plink, plink, plink. Three bodies thud simultaneously. I feel like prime Sam Fisher.
High ground is vital and from the right vantage I can survey the area, plan my route, and pick off enemies from distance. I always clamber to the loftiest point and use the D-pad to tag visible hostiles, which tracks them through walls. In a pinch, focus mode will highlight enemies through walls too, although only if they're nearby.
Some of the level design feels like it's steering you down this silent route. Back at the Boatworks, the first thing I saw after sneaking in was a platform lift to the roof of the main warehouse, high above every enemy. A drop in the ceiling led me to an empty top floor – I've seen this trick repeated in other hideouts, so I always look for ladders or other ways to reach the roof.
In the bigger compounds, staying silent for longer than a few minutes is a real challenge. No matter how many times I ran the Boatworks (I saved before I tried, and reloaded when I failed) I was always eventually spotted by some unaccounted-for enemy. But I reached a point where I could reliably clear the main warehouse floor-by-floor and empty the safe without anyone spotting me. That gave me a headstart on the police when I was eventually found, and by the time officers arrived I'd slipped back out through the fence, goodies jingling in my stash bag.
This feels like the first time stealth has been a core part of a GTA game. During standard stick-ups of stores and jewellers you can find back entrances, kill the alarm and erase security tapes – but you'll always need to confront staff if you want to grab absolutely everything. For that reason, illegal operations feel like the real test of your sneakiness, and I'm relishing each new one that pops up on my map. They have the feel of Far Cry's outposts: flexible, self-contained diversions that I can tick off whenever I need more cash, or just fancy a change of pace.
I've loved all my time with GTA 6 so far, but the best I've felt is when, this morning, I robbed Sound4Sound Studio in north Vice City. After hopping the fence I systematically cleared the parking lot and slipped inside, carving through the building, headshot after headshot. Nobody saw me coming, the police never arrived, and afterwards I could explore unchallenged, helping myself to every last bundle of cash. I drove off in a unique custom car, orange paint glistening, tens of thousands of dollars to the good.
I'd take a whole game of these scenarios. Thankfully, I've still got 30 left.
One final bonus of stealth: silencers are comically long, so now Lucia walks around Vice City carrying a gun taller than she is.

pool.titulo: How To Get Cheap Game Pass Ultimate This Black Friday – I Got 26 Months for Under £200 With This Neat Trick
pool.resumen: Stack Xbox Game Pass Essential, EA Play and one month of Game Pass Ultimate codes this Black Friday to get around 26 months of Game Pass Ultimate for under £200. Here's how.
pool.contenido:
Microsoft's Game Pass Ultimate has had a bumpy year on the pricing front. The UK price jumped to £22.99 a month last October, then dropped back to £16.99 in April, although the trade-off was that Call of Duty no longer lands on the service on day one. Even at the lower price, a year of Ultimate still comes to £203.88 if you're paying monthly, making it an expensive outlay.
However, there are ways to get it cheaper - much cheaper. The good news is that the old conversion trick, where you buy cheaper subscriptions and let Microsoft turn them into Ultimate time, is still alive, in spite of the ongoing changes Microsoft is making to the service.
Admittedly, it isn't as good as it used to be, and the days of three years of Core becoming three years of Ultimate are long gone, but with Black Friday prices on the codes you need, it's still a very strong saving. I know, because I've just done it myself.
The Current Conversion Rates Before getting into the maths, here are the rates from Microsoft's own website , which were bumped up a little when Ultimate got its price cut:
Game Pass Essential (the old Game Pass Core): 45 percent of remaining time converts to Ultimate. 90 days of Essential becomes 40 days of Ultimate. PC Game Pass: 60 percent converts. 90 days becomes 54 days. Game Pass Premium: 65 percent converts. 90 days becomes 59 days. Game Pass for Console: 50 percent converts. 90 days becomes 45 days. EA Play: 25 percent converts. 90 days becomes 22 days. Microsoft rounds each conversion up to the next full day, though its own examples don't always match the percentages exactly, so don't be surprised if your final total is off by a few days from what you work out on a calculator.
The Most Important Rule I need to flag this before anything else, because it's the one thing that can mess up the whole plan. These rates only apply if your Game Pass Ultimate has fully lapsed. If you've still got Ultimate time on your account when you redeem the codes, the rates are much, much worse.
So if your Ultimate is due to run out in a few days or weeks, wait it out. It's worth the patience, and it's why I waited until mine had properly expired before I started. Also make sure recurring billing is switched off before you begin, so you aren't stuck by any nasty subscription fees when this renewal time is up.
TL;DR: How to get Game Pass Ultimate cheap this Black Friday First up, you'll need to pick up three Xbox Game Pass Essential keys - these are £42.60 from ShopTo with code BLACKFRIDAY, which knocks 5% off its listed price, and saves you around £2 a code. It isn't much, but it's a discount at least.
Then, you'll need three 12 month EA Play keys. These aren't discounted at all from Amazon, but £20 each from Amazon make them a useful secondary means of adding more Game Pass Ultimate months for cheap.
And, to convert it all into Game Pass Ultimate (plus give you another month), you'll need a one month Game Pass Ultimate code. For £11 from Amazon, this is one of the lowest price it's been for some time, so the fact the offer is still on during Black Friday is only a good thing.
Doing the maths on these reveals the following working out:
3x Xbox Game Pass Essential, 12 months, at £42.65 each from ShopTo: £127.95 3x EA Play, 12 months, at £20 each from Amazon: £60 1x Game Pass Ultimate, one month, at £10.99 from Amazon: £10.99 In total, that's £198.94.
What You Actually Get Microsoft caps converted time at 36 months, and three 12-month codes of each type takes you right up to that limit for each subscription, so you don't lose anything on the way in. This is how it all work out, if you were to do it individually.
Game Pass Essential: Three 12-month codes gives you 36 months on your account. At 45 percent, that works out at roughly 16 months of Game Pass Ultimate. Add the extra month of Ultimate you purchase to trigger the upgrade and you've got around 17 months for £138.94, an effective £8.08 a month.
EA Play: Three 12-month codes is also 36 months, and at 25 percent that's about 9 months of Ultimate. Add the month on top and it's 10 months for £70.99, which works out at roughly £7.10 a month. Strange as it sounds, EA Play is actually the cheaper source of Ultimate time per month, even though it has the worse conversion rate, because the codes cost so much less. And because Ultimate already includes EA Play, you aren't paying for the same thing twice. The old time just gets folded into the upgrade.
Both together: Stack the lot and you land on about 26 months of Game Pass Ultimate for £198.94 , which comes out at roughly £7.65 a month. At the full £16.99 a month, 26 months of Ultimate would cost £441.74, so you're saving about £242.80 over the whole run. That's well over half off, and a genuine bargain - you could essentially get over four years for the price Microsoft charges for just over two, if you want to look at it a different way.
As you can see, it's worth combining the two, as it works out to a much more affordable price per month than if you held onto other codes and activated them when you needed them.
On a personal level, I know this holds up - I did it on 10th November (albeit with a slightly different deal), and my Game Pass Ultimate is showing as running until February 2029, working out to around 27 months from the start of November. That's a little over my estimate, but that's easily within the margin you'd expect from Microsoft's daily rounding and the variation in how many days different months contain. Your mileage may vary by a few days either way.
How To Do It In Order: The order matters, so follow it carefully:
Let your Game Pass Ultimate lapse completely. Don't skip this, as you'll otherwise get much worse conversion rates. Redeem all three Game Pass Essential codes one after another on the Microsoft website's Redeem a Code page. Your account will now show Game Pass Essential running a long way into the future. Redeem all three EA Play codes. These stack separately from the Essential time,

pool.titulo: PS5 Consoles Omitted From Sony's Official Black Friday 2026 Sale Lineup

pool.contenido:

After a brutal wave of price hikes, among plenty of other challenges (we see you, AI), PlayStation is heading into this year's holiday shopping season without a single discount on its PS5 consoles - even though the PS5 is now six years old.
If you were waiting to pick up a PS5 for your first taste of Grand Theft Auto 6, you're kind of out of luck for the most part, and now that Black Friday is finally here, it doesn't look like Sony is going to spring any surprises on the base, digital-only, or Pro models of its current-gen console.
PlayStation Black Friday Sale: Retailer Guide Live at Amazon Live at Target Live at Walmart Live at Best Buy Are PS5 Consoles On Sale for Black Friday? Black Friday proper , as I like to call it, is today, and while we wish we had better news for you, there are still no discounts on PS5 hardware.
In fact, we're not all that surprised because PlayStation typically kicks off its Black Friday promotions well ahead of the actual shopping event, so we'd have had a decent indication before now.
In 2026, things have started even earlier. Sony's digital Black Friday sale went live at the beginning of the month, followed by a fresh wave of discounts on physical products, including PS5 games and DualSense controllers , on November 16.
I've been covering PlayStation's Black Friday sales for years now, and based on how these promotions typically work, this is likely as good as it'll get for the PS5 deals.
That's a pretty stark contrast to last year. When PlayStation's Black Friday sale launched on November 19, 2025, it immediately knocked $100 off every PS5 console, including both the disc and digital editions of the PS5 Slim, as well as the PS5 Pro. If you grabbed one then, you're sitting pretty right now.
IGN has reached out to PlayStation to request comment on the state of PS5 console Black Friday deals now and in the future.
Why Aren't There Any PS5 Console Deals for Black Friday This Year? There are a few reasons why we're not seeing the same PS5 discounts this Black Friday, and unfortunately, most of them come down to the state of the console market right now.
First, there's the rather significant matter of Sony's price increases. The company has raised PS5 prices in several markets this year, making the prospect of another $100 discount considerably less appealing from a business perspective. Add in ongoing supply pressures, higher component costs and the wider impact of the global chip market, and Sony has considerably less incentive to slash prices on its hardware.
Then there's demand. The PS5 remains a hugely popular console, and with Grand Theft Auto 6 finally here, there's no shortage of people looking to get their hands on one. Sony knows that, and there's arguably little reason to offer substantial discounts when plenty of customers are willing to pay full price.
It's a frustrating situation if you've been waiting for Black Friday to finally pick up a PS5, but there is another option I'd seriously consider before paying full price.
Refurbished PS5s Remain The Best Deal My advice? Look into a refurbished console direct from PlayStation. You can find a PS5 slim digital edition for $499 , $100 off its MSRP for the standard console. Refurbished disc edition consoles, again in the slim variant, are $549, also $100 in savings , marking probably the only deal you'll find on the white monolith this Black Friday.
While this is something I've been rattling on about for months now, it still remains the best way to get a console, in an almost perfect condition, and still make a saving while doing so.
And, if you're after a PS5 Pro, my advice is to also keep an eye on PlayStation's online store . The gaming giant has been occassionally restocking the sought after console (which adds a few nifty ray tracing upgrades to GTA 6, albeit not 60 frames per second) for $899.
Which, while still expensive, is nothing compared to what these bad boys are going for on the resale market right now (upwards of $1500).

pool.titulo: BioWare Fans Hit Out at EA for Selling New Dragon Age Merch After Killing the Studio
pool.resumen: A new Dragon Age hoodie is available on the BioWare Gear store, as EA continues to sell merch based on BioWare's now dead franchises.
pool.contenido:
EA's decision to shut down BioWare sparked a mix of shock and sadness across the internet , with both fans and developers fondly remembering the many role-playing games the Canadian studio put out over the years.
The Mass Effect community has been especially vocal , given that Mass Effect 5 was cancelled alongside the studio closure . But Dragon Age fans certainly aren't happy either, and they're making it known.
Despite BioWare's closure, the BioWare Gear merch store is still being updated. A bunch of new items were added for N7 Day , but we just got a new Dragon Age merch drop too.
For example, the Dragon Age Inquisition Seven of Swords Nightmare Hoodie features a piece of tarot card art that appears in Dragon Age: Inquisition. Better still, the art depicts fan-favourite character Duncan from Dragon Age: Origins. But given that we're only getting this hoodie after everyone who worked on the Dragon Age series lost their job, it isn't sitting well with fans.
"Do not give #EA the privilege of royalties on IP they have killed, and will not sell or forfeit," one fan said . "If you want your voice heard and want to #SaveDragonAge and #SaveMassEffect, EA needs to reckon with the consequences of their bad financial decisions. #BoycottEA and licensed merch."
"Save Mass Effect. Save Dragon Age. Dragon Age was failed massively by EA. You destroyed what Veilguard could have/should have been because you pushed for it to be live service then backtracked. You never gave Dragon Age the chance it deserved," another person replied to the BioWare Gear Store's post promoting the hoodie .
"No studio, No Game = No money," Olarcadia said on X / Twitter . "What you're doing is a pure lack of respect." "It's so cute how you think putting out merch is going to make us hate you any less," onedcdame agreed. "Keep it. BioWare is closed, we're not giving you any of our money EA," replied SignWithBlood. "You should offer to sell back the IP to the founders, including the BioWare brand and name," added @inkpot__gods. "We bought merch to support the devs who made the games we loved; you fired all the devs and stopped making those games, so there’s no one left for us to financially support," said LouEaglesham.
It appears that the community plans to boycott EA's continued use of BioWare's IPs, at least until it allows a team of devs to make a new game in these universes. Right now, both Dragon Age and Mass Effect are on ice.
Dragon Age fans in particular have a lot to be upset about. The last game in the series, Dragon Age: The Veilguard, largely failed to impress the community. But it has long been known that the game languished in development hell and suffered from various changes in direction.
Former BioWare executive producer Mark Darrah recently shared the original vision for the fourth Dragon Age game , before EA allegedly mandated that it had to be a live service. EA would then go on to allow the game to be retooled as a single-player RPG, but The Veilguard had to be built from the bones of this live service work, meaning the developers didn't have time to return to this original outline.
It remains to be seen what EA does next with the Dragon Age series. EA is not in the habit of selling off IP, but if enough fans are boycotting the merch, it leaves EA without much to do other than just sit on it.

pool.titulo: LEGO’s Project Hail Mary Set Returns to Its Lowest Price Point of $70 at Amazon for Black Friday

pool.contenido:
As a fan of both Andy Weir's novel and the Ryan Gosling-starring film , it felt like a no-brainer for me to pick up LEGO's Project Hail Mary set when it released earlier this year . It actually ended up being one of my favorite builds I've worked on so far, so I'm very quick to recommend it to others who are curious about it. If you're in that boat of wanting to buy it, now is the time to strike: Amazon's knocked $30 off it for Black Friday .
This deal has brought the cost of this brick-built spacecraft down to $69.99 from $99.99, marking a return to its lowest price point so far at the retailer. Last time we saw it this low was during Prime Big Deal Days in October , so it's a real treat to see it on sale again now (and not just for Prime members).
Recommended for adult builders , this set comes with 830 pieces to assemble a microscale replica of the Hail Mary spaceship on a display stand, with a little minifigure of Ryland and Rocky to show off next to it. While the ship itself is very cool to look at, it's the technical elements of it that really blew me away.
By turning a crank at the base of the stand, you can actually rotate the ship to bring out its centrifugal gravity system. It looks very cool in action (and actually flows quite well while spinning), which makes it quite an impressive piece to have up on display.
If you want an even more detailed breakdown of its assembly, it's worth reading through writer Myles Obenza's We Build of this model. In it, he called the set "a mechanical marvel" noting that it's "simple on the surface, but my roughly 2-hour build time with the 830-piece set was some of the most fun I've had doing a build for IGN, and I've done my fair share."
This set could sell out fast, so if you've been thinking this brick-built Hail Mary ship needs to be added to your shelves, this is a great time to buy it. And for even more LEGO deals right now, check out our rundown of Black Friday LEGO deals to see what else has our attention.

pool.titulo: Losing Six Stars in GTA 6 Is Meant to Be Impossible, but Players Are Trying Everything From Interdimensional Portals to Hidden Bunkers
pool.resumen: Losing six stars in GTA 6 is meant to be impossible, but players are trying everything from interdimensional portals to hidden bunkers to escape the cops.
pool.contenido:
GTA 6 's new police system is one of the most interesting things about the game. Instead of omnipresent cops, the police have have various levels of awareness, and you can use guile and cunning to outsmart them and escape.
There are still wanted stars, which represent how much of the police force is dedicated to hunting you down, but a well-considered escape plan can get you out of most kinds of trouble. Just escape the search zone, lose line of sight, and change how you look to get away.
That is unless you cause too much carnage. If you go off the deep end and cause real mayhem, you’ll eventually reach six stars. Six stars in GTA 6 sees almost the entire map become a search zone, and the cops will never stop tracking you down, according to Rockstar. If you need a pointer, here's how to get a six-star wanted level in GTA 6 .
If you hide indoors, the army comes along with a tank. If you jump in a plane, jets are scrambled to shoot you down. If you try to escape by car, attack helicopters perform a strafing run to blow you off the road. Eventually, no matter how hard you try, you will succumb to the pressure. Six stars, it is thought, amounts to a death sentence.
But is that guaranteed? Since GTA 6 came out, players have been looking for creative ways of breaking the rule around the highest wanted level. Using clever tricks, some are exploring ways to escape a six-star police hunt and return to regular gameplay — which should technically only be possible two ways: you die or get busted.
Warning! GTA 6 spoilers follow.
How to lose six-star wanted level in GTA 6 One player used a series of secret bunkers that you can open up to get access to a GTA 6 tank . Here’s the clip:
⭐️ LE PREMIER JOUEUR AU MONDE A RÉUSSIR À SEMER LES 6 ETOILES SUR GTA 6 !
Il est allé dans un sous sol rempli de bunkers pour réussir à semer la police. https://t.co/8Q0nd27eOn
— La Twitchance (@LaTwitchance) November 25, 2026
Another player in the comments said they managed to replicate this by swimming. “Bro, I actually did it yesterday. I managed to escape the 6-star wanted level,” they said . “Just keep diving underwater, and when your oxygen is almost depleted, swim back to the surface. Keep repeating this until you find a jet ski. Then ride it beyond the 6-star search area, and boom! You're free.”
Some players think the underwater cave system in Emerald Springs could be another prime candidate, since cops can’t send diving teams after you. If you head to Emerald Spring and look for signs for the Selkie Hole, there’s diving equipment you can use to explore an underground cave network.
Another player went to more extreme lengths to avoid the cops. After completing the majority of the long Vice City Easter egg in GTA 6 , they left the world through a portal back to the ‘80s. When they came back to present-day Leonida, the cops didn’t care about them or their Tommy Vercetti shirt anymore. Here’s that clip:
世界初？GTA6で手配度6から逃げきることに成功しました https://t.co/0g7pSPJ6UU
— ハイグレ玉夫 (@haiguretamao) November 24, 2026
“The cops in GTA are so overpowered that you can't escape them unless you go to another world,” said one commenter . “Now THAT'S how you escape the six star wanted level. That’s gangsta,” said another .
One fan also claimed to have escaped six stars by swimming into an underwater research station. Unfortunately, the video doesn’t actually show the six stars vanishing, but I guess they technically escaped, as long as they stay there forever.
6 STARS ESCAPE Underwater Research Facility IN GTA 6 (is coded if you get 6 stars they will recognize you no matter what, testes same thing with 5 stars and it worked) https://t.co/jfZZMzdvs4
— fearcb (@Fearcbpr) November 23, 2026
It’ll be interesting to see if any new strategies formulate around losing six stars, although getting the full six isn’t something that generally happens by accident in ordinary gameplay. You have to cause a lot of carnage to bring the full weight of Leonida’s police down on your head.

pool.titulo: Yaga Episode 7 and 8 Recap and Review
pool.resumen: Episodes 7 and 8 of Yaga reveal the incredible and shocking twist we've all been waiting for, executed to perfection with a stunning cast and phenomenal writing.
pool.contenido:
Warning: This review contains full spoilers for Yaga Season 1, episodes 7 and 8. The full season is now streaming on AMC+ in the US and Crave in Canada.
The first part of the two-episode finale of Yaga opens with the Baba Yaga narrator saying, “it always has to be three…” as we see Rapp wandering in the woods at the ritual space. He looks down, puzzled, to see a red cooler on the ground with fish inside, and within that a ceramic jar made by Olena (Laney, as we know her) – and the jar has testicles in it. He blinks, and is still holding the jar and has the cooler, but is standing out on the dock near Carson’s boat at the marina.
We see Henry’s parents for the first time at the coroners, where they are looking at Henry’s body. We find out Henry was brutally murdered one week ago, with chicken feathers shoved down his throat before being burned alive. The pathologist, Jake, confirms he was castrated prior to death, as well.
As Rapp tells Henry’s mother, Dora, that he disagrees with Geena having been the one to murder him – he shares his own clues we’ve seen him gather over the past few episodes regarding Baba Yaga – and it’s clear that everyone in the room thinks he’s crazy. Dora tells him sternly that he had one job to do, and that was to protect Henry – and she fires him on the spot. As she walks away, Rapp tells her, “I know where all your bodies are buried.” Yet, Dora does not seem concerned about the threat.
Read IGN's Previous Yaga Reviews Yaga Episodes 1 & 2 Recap and Review Yaga Episode 3 Recap and Review Yaga Episode 4 Recap and Review Yaga Episode 5 Recap and Review Yaga Episode 6 Recap and Review Carson confronts Eckert about Geena previously sharing how he threatened and physically assaulted her – he only denies it, all while trying to make Carson feel guilty for even thinking something so awful of him. A lovely icing on the cake for someone who seems to be trying to cover their tracks while using manipulation tactics.
We see that Rapp has snuck up into Olena’s room at the hospital to try and pull more information out of her regarding Baba Yaga, as he believes, based on his discoveries, there will be a third murder following Logan and Henry’s. As usual, Olena is being evasive and cheeky, until Rapp pulls out her journal. For the first time, we see her looking legitimately concerned about this being in his hands, as he begins speaking the words written down in Ukrainian.
Olena starts to work with him on this for reasons unknown, and Rapp guesses that not only are there three murders planned, but there are three Yagas. Olena responds with, “Three to live forever,” as Rapp starts to put the puzzle pieces together – the third and youngest Yaga needs to have a baby to continue the cycle.
Right when we think Olena might actually reveal who the youngest Yaga is, she tells Rapp a sacrifice is needed before she divulges that the sacrifice is a kiss for her. All that’s needed is one kiss, but Rapp ends up becoming entranced and begins making out with Olena as he sees flashes of her as a young woman on the bed, surrounded by flowers. She ends up saying the third Yaga is “onuka,” which translates to “granddaughter” – confirming she herself must be the oldest Yaga, but it’s unclear who her granddaughter is. She takes off her top and right as he’s going further with her, Katherine barges into the room and yells, “What are you doing to my mother?!”
Rapp, shocked that Katherine is Olena’s daughter and convinced she is connected to the murders, begs Carson to go with him to Katherine’s house to try and get any other morsel of intel. As they’re sitting at Katherine’s dining table, discussing this (calmly at first), Rapp drops his conclusion, saying, “I think you, your mother, and your daughter are a multigenerational team of serial killers who think they are witches, who are punishing bad men for hurting women.”
“I don’t buy your act. I am ancient, you stupid little boy.” Katherine looks unimpressed, saying, “Well that sounds fucking fantastic.” As this is all happening, Carson looks to be slightly restless, fidgeting every so often while Rapp and Katherine argue through this all. After voices raise, arguments escalate, and Rapp accuses Katherine of murdering Henry and lying about it, Katherine kicks them out of her house. While they are leaving, she also puts Rapp in his place, reminding him that every time he came on to her, he had an ulterior motive. She says to him, “I don’t buy your act. I am ancient, you stupid little boy,” and the line is delivered brilliantly.
Rapp is continuing to try and convince Carson he is correct with his theory, and explaining the pattern of “333” that he’s seen basically everywhere during his time in Whittock. He believes the third victim will be killed the following morning on March 3rd at 3:33am. Before Carson heads to meet with Dora, who has requested a private meeting with her at an upscale bar, she begs Rapp to wait in his hotel room for her until she figures out the next steps they should take. He eventually gives in, and she kisses him goodbye, hoping he will trust her on this.
Immediately, the meeting with Dora seems to have an underlying tone of danger to Carson, as Dora blames Henry’s horrific behavior on his father, saying he came after both her and Alice (Logan’s mother) when they were young – it is unclear if it was consensual or not. We get confirmation that Henry and Logan were in fact half brothers, which is more disturbing after knowing they previously had some type of infatuation with one another… and acted on it.
It’s starts to be pretty clear that Dora’s ulterior motive was wanting to keep the fact that Henry raped Lily under wraps. In turn, she offers a job to Carson “for life” working for the Parks. Carson politely declines, and Dora comments, “If you’re working for Eckert, you’re already working for us.” As this information sinks in, Dora unsurprisingly leaves her with a threat before walking away.

pool.titulo: It Turns Out Jason Might Have a History With Mandy in GTA 6 After All
pool.resumen: Mandy is obsessed with Jason in GTA 6, but there's dialogue that suggests they hooked up at least once.
pool.contenido:
As soon as GTA 6 was in our hands, an early game character quickly became a fan favourite: Mandy.
Warning! Spoilers for GTA 6 follow.
It's not hard to see why. Mandy certainly knows how to make an entrance, as she tries in vain to entice Jason away from Lucia . But alas, it is not meant to be.
Fans then did a little digging and found out that Mandy is almost definitely hiding a dark secret ; she's probably killed people. That makes her advances towards Jason — like insisting they were supposed to be married — look dangerously delusional. Jason might have dodged a literal bullet.
However, there is some easy-to-miss dialogue in GTA 6 that suggests Mandy wasn't basing her infatuation with Jason on nothing. You can come across this dialogue as soon as you take control of Lucia and find a meditation spot . The meditation sequence will play some audio from the character's past, usually centred around their insecurities.
AAAAAAAAAH https://t.co/4xxj8rHZAR
— 𐔌 . ⋮ ιvσɾყ ֹ ₊ ꒱ (@ivysmores) November 25, 2026
In one of Lucia's medititation sequences, she recounts a conversation with Jason that she must have had off-screen after they got back in touch.
"Yeah, okay, we hooked up once, but, you know, barely. And it was a long time ago," we can hear Jason say in Lucia's thoughts. "You don't need to worry about her, Lu. Have you seen you? I know how good I got it. I'm not gonna screw that up again."
Of course, Jason doesn't mention Mandy by name here, but the wording makes it pretty clear it's her. Jason mentions not letting Lucia go again, so it would be after their initial breakup. That means the conversation likely happened after she was released from prison, meaning Lucia was living in the same neighbourhood as Mandy — and was aware of how obsessed she was with Jason.
In fact, another easy-to-miss scene does show that Lucia knows about Mandy. At the end of Chapter 1, during the sequence when you're running away from Jason's house as Lucia, you can find Mandy giving a statement to the cops (and, of course, exaggerating how close she was with Jason).
This game really has everything lol
— Never break kayfabe (@Quadripolar_B) November 25, 2026
If you come out of hiding, Lucia can finally confront Mandy, saying, "Stay the f**k away from Jason, you crazy b*tch."
Better yet, the encounter gives us another clue that Mandy is a killer, as she tells the police she "wanted to light [Jason's] house on fire so many times."
With all of this in mind, it's no wonder that Jason was eager to stay away from Mandy early on in GTA 6 — it doesn't seem that she understood he wasn't looking for anything long term with her. Luckily for him, it sounds like Lucia is ready to run to his defence.
Mandy went viral pretty much as soon as GTA 6 came out, with countless social media posts discussing the character's motivations. Mandy actress Lexie Shoaibi has spoken out about her "bittersweet" newfound fame , pointing out that people keep trying to impersonate her on social media. Shoaibi has also revealed she spent around 10 days on set playing Mandy, but she also did a few other NPC voices while working with Rockstar.

pool.titulo: Silksong is getting a free expansion in 2 weeks
pool.resumen: Sea of Sorrow looks rad.
pool.contenido:
In a "Cherry Time!" presentation , Hollow Knight developer Team Cherry has just revealed a first look at its much-anticipated first content update to Hollow Knight: Silksong. The nautical-themed Sea of Sorrow will come as a free update on December 11.
Team Cherry said that Sea of Sorrow will contain multiple new areas, power-ups, and bosses, while I clocked at least three new friendly NPCs in the trailer: A townsperson, a new shopkeeper, and a ferryman. Area-wise, I made out three distinct tilesets in the trailer: A rain-blasted fishing town on the water, a harrowing climb with an electrical storm element, and a green space reminiscent of the early game Bell Bottom.
At least the first of these areas appears to be built on cut content for Silksong: "Pharloom Bay" is well-documented on the Hollow Knight wiki , and would have been located on the east side of the map, near the thematically-similar Greymoor. Some elements in the trailer correspond to ones documented by the wiki, like an underwater submersible vehicle, or a scientific lab in the electrical storm area.
Which all sounds rad to me, particularly the submersible. Among the all-timer videogame level concepts, "underwater techbase" is one of my very favorites, and Team Cherry seem to be approaching these concepts with a Lovecrafty, Innsmouth flair that reminds me of the Fishing Village zone from Bloodborne.
Silksong is already a massive game, and I'm curious as to how Sea of Sorrow will fit both the map, and the game's overall flow from act to act. We'll find out for sure when the free expansion releases on December 11.

pool.titulo: Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 gets a model painter demo, so you can make a mess of your Orks, Necrons, Space Marines and AdMech before they even hit the battlefield
pool.resumen:
In the grim darkness of the week before the release of Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 , developers King Art and publishers Deep Silver have released a demo model painter. It's your chance to pre-emptively run a brush over units from the new strategy game's four major factions – Orks, Adeptus Mechanicus, Necrons and Space Marines. The Imperial Guard are in the game too, but mostly as a tutorial army. What a slap in the face for the Imperium's vanilla humans.
Deep Silver are calling it "the most powerful Painter in Dawn of War history", which doesn't seem all that dashing a boast given that Dawn of War 3 came out almost 10 years ago and today's PCs have a fair bit more RAM in them. You can opt for Basic Painter mode in order to quickly knock together livery for entire armies, or fire up the Advanced Painter and get stuck into the weeds of individual armour and body parts, with a choice of materials, patterns, decals and weathering. pool.titulo: Keep the lighthouse on and the villagers obedient in Glagstone, an eerie island city-builder with Macintosh-style graphics
pool.resumen:
Glagstone's "1-bit" aesthetic is a homage to Macintosh games of the late 1980s, cut with elements of art deco, Expressionism and film noir, but it looks like that mainly because it began life on lo-fi indie handheld Playdate .
In transplanting this eerie, story-driven city-builder to Steam, developers Valerii Krasnoselskii and Evgenii Kirichenko have fleshed out the tasty throwback art and shored up connections between the game's management and story layers, while leaving the crux of the experience untouched: you are the newly appointed governor of a remote northern island, contested by rival nations. You have come here to harvest the island's rich mineral resources, and now, the island is trying to drive you nuts.

pool.titulo: Pablo Lluch, experto en música, sobre GTA VI: "Si tienes un sobrino o un primo jugando, siéntate a su lado y escucha, es como una creación en directo"
pool.resumen:

En ello tiene mucho que ver la capacidad de los desarrolladores de Rockstar para construir un apartado musical basado en capas independientes que se mezclan y generan en tiempo real, algo sobre lo que Pablo Lluch, compositor y profesor de Operación Triunfo , ha querido poner el foco durante una interesante lección en Hoy por Hoy de la SER.
"En GTA nunca oyes la misma música dos veces"

pool.titulo: Good coffee is one of our last comforts in a cruel universe, which is why I'm tempted by this Black Friday coffee grinder deal
pool.resumen: The PC in PC Gamer stands for "pourover coffee."
pool.contenido:
Timemore's reengineered S5 Pro flagship manual grinder promises an ideal brew through the power of unprecedented burr geometry. It's got a high capacity for a hand grinder, precision external grind adjustment, and a widened crank knob for easier grinding.
Key specs: 30g capacity | 48mm burrs | 15 micron adjustment steps
Chestnut S5 Pro price check: Timemore $179.00 View Deal
I'll be real with you: There are some days where my morning cup of coffee is the only thing maintaining my tenuous mental wellbeing. Sure, the caffeine offers some chemical assistance for weathering our era's daily whirlwind of psychic damage, but it's more about the ritual: The best way to start the day is by doing something nice for yourself, and there are few things nicer than a good cup of coffee. It makes games better, too. I wrote it on a videogame website and that means it's real.
I'm a pourover man myself, but whether you're using a drip machine, moka pot, or French press, nothing will improve the quality of your at-home coffeemaking like grinding your own coffee beans with a respectable grinder like the Timemore Chestnut S5 Pro , currently on sale at 20% off for $143 on Amazon.
We're curating all the Black Friday PC gaming deals right here There are two reasons why a good grinder makes for great coffee: First, coffee starts losing the volatile compounds that contribute to its flavor as soon as it's ground, so grinding your beans just before brewing ensures as many of those compounds are contributing to your cup as possible. Second, if your coffee grounds aren't a uniform size, they make an uneven brew: Inconsistently sized grounds—like those produced by cheaper, blade-based grinders that smash the beans apart—means your coffee can be simultaneously underextracted and overextracted, muddying the flavor with all sorts of undesirable notes.
A proper hand grinder gives you the best of all worlds: Fresh grounds on demand, quality conical burrs that produce more uniform grind sizes, and a cheaper price point than high-end grinders that might be five to ten times as expensive—or more. I'm in the market for a grinder upgrade myself, and that's why this Black Friday deal on the Timemore Chestnut S5 Pro caught my attention.
I've been happily using a cheaper Timemore grinder for a couple of years, so I can already vouch for the brand's quality. The S5 Pro brings some additional features that'd offer some quality-of-life upgrades over my trusty old C2: For one, it's got a bigger capacity. More interesting to me, though, is its precision external grind adjustment with numbered steps. My current grinder's adjustment dial is unlabeled, which can be irritating when I'm switching between coffees. That numbered grind adjustment will make it easier to dial in and keep track of coffee-specific grind sizes.
Timemore also boasts that the S5 Pro's reengineered burrs represent "a new benchmark in grinding." And if there's anything I love, it's progress. If that $143 price tag is too expensive of an ask for starting your coffee grinding journey, however, there are similar deals on Timemore's more affordable options: This $60 Chestnut C2S is a great entry point that'll give you a running start towards better coffee.
And as we all know, better coffee makes for better gaming. Probably. Do your own research.

pool.contenido:
If you’ve ever been enticed by the ridiculous meals in the Persona games, you’re in luck. Atlus partnered with Insight Editions for an official Persona cookbook, collecting 55 recipes from the three most recent games. (Well, remakes.)
The cookbook was released just last year, and has dropped to a new low price in Amazon's Black Friday sale . The discount knocks a whole 50% off the Persona cookbook , bringing the price of Sojiro's coffee secrets down to $14.
Official Persona Cookbook Discount The official Persona cookbook collects 55 recipes from the three most recent remakes: Persona 3 Reload, Persona 4 Golden, and Persona 5 Royal. Sorry P1 and P2 fans. I hope Atlus will (finally) be treating you soon enough .
The recipe adaptations come from Jarrett Melendez , the former chef behind a number of video game cookbooks, including an unofficial GTA guide . Each recipe is broken down into allegedly 'easy' steps with descriptions about the in-game lore. And pages are decorated with real photography of each completed meal, as well as illustrations and screenshots from the Persona games .
All 55 recipes appear in some form across the three games, whether as a character’s favorite food, a potential gift, or a meal you can eat for a quick stat boost. Obviously, in-game restaurants like Café Leblanc are heavily featured.
Some of the recipes are slightly spiced up takes on classics, like Shinjiro’s beloved katsudon, while others are a bit extreme in their in-game accuracy. Looking at you, Big Bang Burger Challenge.
We’ll get our next taste of remastered Atlus food with Persona 4 Revival , coming to consoles next year. But I’m sure we’ll get an entirely new feast with the now officially announced Persona 6 .

The sticks on the DualSense Edge are interchangeable; you can choose domed or convex replacements that come in two different heights. If your analog sticks crap out, you can replace them for $20 .
