pool.titulo: Save 40% Off the Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 Sport Headphones Gift Edition in Amazon Exclusive Rose Gold
pool.resumen: Features bone conduction technology that makes it the best headphones for street runners.
pool.contenido:
If you enjoy listening to music while you run or work out, then you should consider getting a headset that's specifically designed for it. Shokz is one of the best known and well-respected sport headphone brands and, fortunately for you, the Shokz Black Friday Sale has officially kicked off on Amazon .
As part of this sale, Amazon has dropped the price of the Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 open-ear wireless sport headphones in rose gold from $180 to just $119.99 with free shipping. The rose gold color is exclusive to Amazon. This particular set comes in premium gift packaging, in case you want to surprise a lucky someone this holiday season.
40% Off the Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 Sport Headphones Premium gift edition
The OpenRun Pro 2 looks like a neckband style headphone except that a lightweight titanium band connecting the two ear pieces wraps around the back of your head instead of resting on your neck. This design does an excellent job of keeping everything in place, perfect for active exercise.
Instead of the traditional method of sending sound vibrations to your eardrums, the OpenRun Pro uses bone conduction technology to send vibrations through your cheekbones directly to your inner ear. As such, the headphones are actually placed in front of your ear instead of on your ear. The biggest advantage is that you can fully hear your surroundings; if you like running on streets, for example, you'll be aware of everything that's going on around you while your music is playing.
OpenRun Pro 2 is an obvious upgrade over the Open Run Pro The OpenRun Pro 2 is a substantial update over its predecessor. The most noticeable upgrade is arguably the switch from a proprietary magnetic charging cable to the USB Type-C standard. Another significant upgrade is the sound quality.
While the original OpenRun Pro has good bass response, it is slightly hampered by the fact that it produces tiny vibrations that are noticeable and sometimes ticklish or distracting. The new OpenRun Pro 2 utilizes Shok's DualPitch technology to virtually eliminate vibrations. Other smaller changes include increased battery life and improved mic quality.
The Shokz OpenRun are the best earbuds for exercise I have a pair of AirPods Pro that I use regularly, but I always set them aside for the OpenRun Pros when I run. The Transparency mode on the AirPods Pro does work well for most situations, but they still can't compare to the awareness you get without having any buds plugging up your ears. In my experience these headphones stay in place extremely well and the sound quality is great compared to other sport headphones I've tried.

pool.titulo: Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair Dev's Explanation for Skipping Xbox Sparks Backlash
pool.resumen: Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition developer Playtonic has come under fire from Xbox owners after it ruled out an Xbox Series X and S version of the rerelease.
pool.contenido:
Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition developer Playtonic has come under fire from Xbox owners after it ruled out an Xbox Series X and S version of the rerelease.
In a statement published online, the UK studio said it had to prioritize the PlayStation 5 and Nintendo Switch 2 versions because the cost of bringing it to Xbox "just isn't viable for us at this time." The original game, released in 2018, launched on Xbox One at the same time as PlayStation 4 and Nintendo Switch. The next-gen upgrade hits PC, PS5, and Switch 2 only on December 15.
"Unfortunately, we've had to prioritize our efforts given the technical challenges and costs presented in the creation of this updated version of the game and as a result, we are unable to commit to any additional platforms for the forseeable future," Playtonic said.
"We understand the frustration felt by those of you who won't be able to access the Definnitive Edition at launch, but unfortunately the cost of bringing it to more platforms just isn't viable for us at this time. As a small team, we hope you guys can understand the challenges we face. Please know that this wasn't an easy decision to make, and we apologize to any of you affected by this.
"We only wish things were different, and we value every single one of you and your feedback."
Playtonic's statement is light on specifics, but most are reading between the lines here and assuming what the studio is saying here is that it weighed up how much it would cost to port the rerelease to Xbox Series X and S against its potential return, and found the numbers didn't add up.
"This means the game didn’t do meaningful numbers on the Xbox. It doesn’t make any sense otherwise," one person suggested . "They could’ve just said the game sold bad on Xbox and they don’t have enough money or time to justify updating it," another said .
Whatever the reason, Xbox fans certainly aren't happy. "Slap in the face to Xbox fans who’ve supported you from the beginning," one Xbox user said . "Will not support you any longer or buy any future Playtonic games if we’re not gonna be treated equally."
"It's a free upgrade for a game we've already brought. The same as the other platforms but you are treating us poorly," another added . "So no we don't understand. No matter how you slice it, it's a **** you to Xbox buyers."
"So... you can't afford to make a FREE upgrade for Xbox... but you could afford it for every other platform?" one person asked . "Well... won't be buying anything of yours from this point on. So there's even less money for you."
"I could buy this game on PS5 or Switch but it’s clear you don’t want or deserve my support," another said.

pool.titulo: The Shrek Toaster Is the Only Black Friday Deal You Need
pool.contenido:
Do you ever throw some bread in the toaster and think to yourself, "Wow, this toast would taste better with Shrek’s face on it?"
Well, Amazon’s Black Friday deals can make your questionable culinary dream a reality. Uncanny Brands produces a line of retro TV-themed toasters that burn images straight onto your bread. For the season of deals, Amazon gave most of these quirky (and, somehow, officially licensed) toasters a 15% discount , bringing them to their lowest-ever prices.
What Is Going on With These Toasters
Amazon’s discount knocks around $7 off the price of each toaster in these lightning deals, which will disappear once they’re fully claimed. For whatever reason, that seems to be happening surprisingly fast.
The list of themed toasters is about as weird as the concept itself. We’ve got Shrek , of course, but you can also sear into your bread images of Bluey , Sonic , Snoopy , and, um, Bob Ross ? Uncanny Valley also produces a Grinch toaster , but that one isn't getting a discount. Stingy guy, I guess.
According to the official listing , the two-slot toaster features an adjustable thermostat with defrost, quick stop, and reheat functions. Each toaster is emblazoned with an image, dedicated to whatever weird property it prints on bread, in a light-up frame.
I’m going to be honest, I can’t vouch for the quality of the Shrek toaster myself. I use the cheapest possible toaster option from Amazon and have been pretty satisfied with it. Still, maybe I’m not quite as satisfied as users of the Shrek-ster:
"I love this toaster," says the most-upvoted review . "I like that it lights up when you are making toast." Very insightful, I know.
The most legit-looking reviews note that you have to do a little experimentation to find the right settings for maximum image effect, and sometimes that means straight-up burning the bread. Apparently you might also notice a weird smell the first time you use it. Yum!
We're Keeping Track of Normal Black Friday Deals, Too We’re in the thick of Black Friday season. pool.titulo: The canonical USB microphone is still great, and now a total steal for $70
pool.resumen: The Blue Yeti is a household name in microphones for a reason.
pool.contenido:
Blue Yeti USB Microphone: was $99.99 now $69.99
I've used a Blue Yeti for nearly a decade and it would happily serve for a decade more. A classic design, good hardware controls, and zero fuss. It's not for true audiophiles, but its quality and affordability are still hard to match all these years later.
Key specs: USB A | Four pickup patterns | Hardware gain control
Blue Yeti price check: Best Buy $69.99 | Walmart $69.99 View Deal
The Blue Yeti might be the most popular USB microphone ever made, and you know what, it earned it. At its usual price, this is a great USB microphone. At $69.99 (its lowest price ever), it's simply one of the best bangs for your buck in this category.
The original Blue Yeti released in 2009, and in 17 years it has barely changed. I've had mine for a decade, and as I look around, I'm realizing it is the longest-lasting gadget on my desk. That's because it just works: I plug in, adjust the gain, and my voice comes through clear.
These days there are more advanced microphones than the Yeti, like its official sequel the Yeti 2, and certainly mics that are just as competitively priced. Those are good too, and I encourage you to check out cheaper options (like the $26 Amazon Basics mic that we surprisingly love ) before making any decisions.
We're curating all the Black Friday PC gaming deals right here But with the Yeti, you absolutely get what it says on the tin. I also think it's still an attractive mic, but it is quite large, so make sure it'll fit on your desk without blocking the corner of your monitor. I've had mine on a mic arm for the past few years, and while it does feel like I'm cosplaying a podcaster just to chill with friends on Discord, it's very convenient.
At this price, it's firmly on the high end of "budget" territory while still sounding as good as mics that cost twice as much. If you do use it for long sessions and prefer to keep your mic open, play with the gain levels and make sure software noise cancelling is on in your chat app of choice (Discord's is pretty good out of the box).
If that's not enough, consider pairing it with dedicated noise cancelling software like Nvidia Broadcast (assuming your GPU can handle the extra toll).

pool.titulo: Skate is dropping seasons and season passes in favor of 'regular, agile content updates'
pool.resumen: The fifth season of Skate will be its last as developer Full Circle looks to try something new.
pool.contenido:
A little over a year after EA launched Skate into early access—where it remains—developer Full Circle is removing the seasonal structure that has underpinned the game so far, saying that doing so will give the team "the freedom to launch features earlier in their lifecycle."
Skate got off to a bit of a rough start when it went live in September 2025, and while it's turned around the initially iffy response from players, it hasn't gone entirely smoothly since then. An initial promise that no new maps would be locked behind paywalls was chucked out the window in February, and Full Circle laid off employees that same month, saying that cutting headcounts means it can "better support Skate's long-term future and focus the team on the things that matter most to you."
The end of Skate's seasonal structure is less overtly not good than those moves, but it is a sign that things aren't going quite as Full Circle had envisioned, and the message that it's still "committed to keep driving Skate forward" has a certain 'despite everything' tone that doesn't strike me as the sort of thing you say when when all cylinders are firing.
"The game is still a work in progress, and we're using this valuable time to experiment, iterate, and figure out what works best for the long-term health of the game—especially when it comes to social features and progression," the studio wrote. "Ultimately, we want to build Skate in a way that lets us roll out fresh content much faster, even if it's not totally finished yet."
Season 5 will end on December 1, after which Full Circle will move to "regular, agile content updates." The end of seasons also means the end of the season pass; the studio is "rethinking how that kind of progression system works." Here's the bullet-point rundown of what's changing:
No Seasons, but still regular content updates No skate.Pass or skate.Premium Pass and no Tix At the end of Season 5, the last Auto-Exchange will happen. One of my favorite Black Friday deals , the big TCGplayer Cyber Weekend deal , is back for another year, and it couldn’t be easier to buy the cards you want and be rewarded for it.
Whether you’re looking for singles, packs, or even entire booster boxes across just about any trading card game, it’s a great time to invest in your collection.

How TCGplayer’s Black Friday Deal Works If you’re new here, it’s pretty simple to take advantage of the TCGplayer Black Friday deal . Rather than discounting cards or products, the retailer awards buyers 10% of their purchase price back as store credit.
This applies from 9 AM New York time on November 27 to 11 PM New York Time on November 30.
So, buying a $30 card nets you $3, and so on and so forth. Because you can fill your cart with TCGs from all over the world, however, it’s easy to rack up plenty of credit.
For example, if you buy a Play Booster Box of Magic: The Gathering and some preconstructed Riftbound decks, you’ll end up with plenty to spend on, say, some Lorcana cards.

If I wasn’t in the UK, I’d be dipping into my card fund to nab myself Yawgmoth, Thran Physician, and Vorinclex, Monstrous Raider for my Magic collection, knowing the store credit would help me secure some bonus cards, too. Why TCGplayer? We recommend TCGplayer for a few reasons. For one, it’s backed by eBay, so there’s an inherent trustworthiness you might not find elsewhere.

pool.titulo: 8 Classic PlayStation Games That Are Barely Playable Today
pool.resumen: From Tomb Raider to Silent Hill, eight classic PlayStation games whose tank controls, cameras, or lost code make them hard to play today
pool.contenido: If you’ve ever watched someone play an old PlayStation game and wondered why their character keeps spinning around in circles, congratulations, you’ve already met tank controls. If you’re unfamiliar, here’s your quick introduction: With tank controls, pressing up moves your character forward in whatever direction they’re facing, and pressing left or right only rotates them, so with the stick alone, you can’t sidestep or turn on a dime. That’s manageable in a hallway. It’s much less so when you’re sneaking past a guard, lining up a shot, or timing a leap across a pit, which is why the same scheme caused trouble in just about every genre during the PS1 era. These eight classic games are the hardest to go back to, whether the culprit is tank controls or something else entirely.

pool.titulo: 5 Unnecessary Nintendo Switch 2 Accessories to Buy Yourself Before Black Friday Ends

pool.contenido:
Nintendo has been having some of the best Black Friday video game deals this year. Walmart was even dropping $30 first-party Switch 2 game deals at one point, and there's plenty of other discounts worth checking out if you haven't already. But if you already have a Switch 2 and plenty of games, what good are these discounts to you? If you've had your console since day one, you may be looking to add some extra accessories to your collection instead.
I'm not talking about necessary accessories like controllers and gaming headsets , though. I'm talking about the stuff that you don't actually need to enjoy your gaming experience. I'm here to shine a light on the accessories that are truly extra in all the best ways.
Warning : You may not need these items, but you'll probably end up wanting them. And because they are all on sale for Black Friday, the temptation to buy them will be greater than ever. Proceed with scrolling at your own risk.
Retro Switch Game Case Let's start with one of my favorites, this Game Boy-inspired Switch 2 game case. This bad boy can hold up to three cartridges and three microSD Express cards at any given time. So you could likely hold most of your game library in this thing if so inclined. It is definitely less safe to put all of your games on a keychain, rather than an actual protective case, but who cares about safety when you've got that retro gaming style working its magic.
Master Sword Game Card Holder/Sword Grip Of all of the Switch accessories I've seen in my life, this one never fails to make me laugh. It's trying to solve multiple problems that don't actually exist while also attempting to appeal to fans of The Legend of Zelda. The Master Sword design is compatible with the Joy-Con 2 controller and is meant to be used with Skyward Sword HD , Tears of the Kingdom, and Switch Sports Chambara. On top of that, you're able to store 12 games in this thing for no reason at all.
I still think this is a very silly thing, but I almost buy it every time it's on sale. I don't even know where I'd put this thing.
Basecase for Switch 2 Gaming Pillow Now that we've gotten the silly card holders out of the way, let's get to the things that solve those first-world problems. If you've spent a good bit of time playing your Switch 2 in handheld mode, then you likely know about "the tingles". This is that funny feeling at your elbows telling you that your arms are not properly being utilized for their biological purpose. If you want those weird feelings (and existential thoughts) to be banished forever, this Switch 2 gaming pillow is great for that.
My coworker actually tested out a pillow just like this one and said it was surprisingly awesome.
Spigen JoyCon Grips
Have you ever had to use a Joy-Con as an actual controller? If you're used to using a Switch Pro controller , it's just going to feel wrong. My nephew always wants to play Super Smash Bros. whenever the family gets together, but he only has one good controller and the rest of us are left with what is essentially half of a remote to play with. I still usually win, but it's getting more difficult every time. If I had one of these grips, using the Joy-Con in this manner would definitely feel less awkward.
DIY GameCube Shell and Buttons for Switch 2 Pro Controller Last but not least, arguably the least necessary accessory there is — a purely stylistic change. After a full year of the Nintendo Switch 2 being on the market, there's a surprising lack of special edition Switch 2 controllers available to buy. So if you want something that better fits your style, I propose taking the DIY route. This GameCube-inspired shell and buttons will transform your controller into an early 2000s fever dream. The only downside is that you'll need to be able to take apart (and reassemble) your Switch 2 Pro Controller to get the look. Still cheaper than buying a new controller.

pool.titulo: The cancelled Doom 4 was 'actually a fun game', according to a former id Software developer, but it had one big problem
pool.resumen: "The problem is always that it's not Doom."
pool.contenido:
Before id Software created its excellent 2016 reboot of Doom , the studio was working on a more direct follow-up to its earlier demon-blasters. Doom 4 was in production between 2008 and 2011, and much like Doom 3 , followed popular trends of first-person shooters at the time. But after multiple false-starts, id Software went back to the drawing board, resulting in the glory-killing FPS that has defined the series' direction ever since.
But according to one former id Software developer, Doom 4 was by no means a terrible game, and possibly should have even been released in some form. It just had one big problem—it wasn't Doom.
Speaking to FRVR , former id Software principal programmer Dustin Land said that he thought Doom 4 showed a lot of promise. "I never thought there was anything wrong with that game", he explained. Unlike the 2016 reboot, Doom 4 aimed to be more of a narrative and spectacle-driven experience, channeling the approach of concurrent shooters like Call of Duty . "Playing Call of Duty but you're shooting demons is actually a fun game," Land continued. "The problem is always that it's not Doom. And so the question is always 'What's Doom'?"
Yet while Doom 4 may not have been a fit for the series, Land believes that Doom 4 could have stood up on its own merits. "I thought it could've just been a new IP. It could've been sold under some other brand."
Obviously, this didn't happen. After three years of trying, Doom 4 was canned, and afterward id Software spent a good while figuring out what the next Doom should look like. "It was a laborious process," Land says. "It was a couple years trying to find what exactly it should be. And that was the era of cover-based shooters, long-distance poking, health recovery, stuff like that. And so the push-forward combat really subverted people's expectation of what a first-person [shooter] should be, and it's had a large impact on how shooters are designed these days."
This is certainly true for id's own lineage, with every subsequent Doom game since 2016 looking to reinvent how the Doom Slayer fights. What lies in store for id Software next remains unclear, however. While the studio is purportedly working on a new project, in the summer, Xbox laid off a reported 136 developers from id Software. Earlier this month, Land announced the formation of Hidden Horses , a new, democratically governed studio composed of former id Software developers, which is working on a new shooter based on The Running Man and 1990's Smash TV.

Of all the Amazon discounts we've seen on the Pokémon TCG's Mega Evolution – Delta Reign Booster Display Box over the last couple of months, it's taken until Black Friday itself for the box with three dozen boosters to finally fall below $200, even managing to undercut its market price.
Down from its $219.99 list price, you can currently grab the 36-pack Delta Reign Booster Display Box for just $199 at Amazon . With that $20.99 chopped off (so 10% off), also being Amazon’s lowest ever price, you’re now only paying $5.53 per booster pack.
Save on the Pokémon TCG: Delta Reign Booster Display Box For comparison, amongst our Black Friday round-up of Pokemon TCG deals at Amazon , we spotted the six-pack Delta Reign Booster Bundle available for $47.88 — working out to $7.98 per pack.

Whichever you go with, you’re still getting a Delta Reign Display Box for under its $199.95 market price on TCGplayer. pool.titulo: The 14 Best Tech Gifts We Recommend for 2026 and Beyond
pool.resumen: Top (unranked) picks from our staff.
pool.contenido:
Finding the perfect gift for someone who only likes tech stuff can be a challenge. Partially because great tech gifts tend to be inherently expensive. If you're buying something for a tech-savvy person this year, it has the potential to be the only gift that truly gets them excited while also blowing a massive hole in your budget.
There are exceptions to this, of course. Plenty of high-quality tech and gaming accessories are surprisingly affordable and practical. If you're looking for ideas of what to get the tech nerd in your life for Christmas, we've rounded up some of our favorite items, in no particular order, to help you get started.
IGN's Recommended Tech Gifts for 2026
Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 Sport Headphones ( on sale now ) If you enjoy listening to music while you run or work out, then this headset should be on your radar. Instead of the traditional method of sending sound vibrations to your eardrums, the OpenRun Pro uses bone conduction technology to send vibrations through your cheekbones directly to your inner ear. As such, the headphones are actually placed in front of your ear instead of on your ear. The biggest advantage is that you can fully hear your surroundings; if you like running on streets, for example, you'll be aware of everything that's going on around you while your music is playing.
“I have a pair of AirPods Pro that I use regularly, but I always set them aside for the OpenRun Pros when I run. The Transparency mode on the AirPods Pro does work well for most situations, but they still can't compare to the awareness you get without having any buds plugging up your ears. In my experience these headphones stay in place extremely well and the sound quality is great compared to other sport headphones I've tried.” - Eric Song
Nintendo Switch 2 + Mario Kart World Bundle Between this year’s studio closures and Sony’s decision to kill game discs, Sony and Microsoft are having rough years. The only console maker that’s thriving this generation is Nintendo. Not only has the Mario company managed to release a steady stream of excellent first-party games for the Switch 2 since launch, but it’s also the only company to say it’s not planning to increase its hardware price, at least for the foreseeable future. If you want a game console with plenty of good years ahead of it, you can’t go wrong with a Switch 2. - Chris Reed
Asus ROG Xbox Ally The RAM crisis hasn’t been kind to hardware costs this year, and if you’re trying to get your hands on a handheld gaming PC that won’t break the bank, the Asus ROG Xbox Ally is your best bet without trying your luck on the used market. It’s powered by a chip that’s roughly on the same level as the Steam Deck, and should have no problem playing most PC games, as long as you’re willing to tweak with the settings. It doesn’t hurt that it’s incredibly comfortable to hold, as well. - Jackie Thomas
Also see: ASUS ROG Raikiri II Xbox Wireless Controller
Apple AirPods Pro 3 This isn’t the most exciting pick, and it’s certainly not the newest gadget on this list. But I use my AirPods Pro 3 headphones every single day. Whether they’re being used for video calls, phone calls, listening to music while walking the dog, or working out, they are constantly in my ears, and they check all the boxes: they sound great (shout-out to the excellent bass for such tiny in-ear headphones!), have excellent battery life, are comfortable in my ears, and have proven quite durable. It’s not that there aren’t plenty of other great headphones out there, but the AirPods Pro 3 have been refined to near-perfection, and they’re on the very short list of my favorite tech products in my life. - Ryan McCaffrey
Peakdesign Beacon Wallet Tracker Card If you know anything about Peakdesign you know that their name is synonymous with quality and the new Wallet Tracker card continues the trend. One of the thinnest and longest lasting tracker cards around this wirelessly charging credit-card sized device works unfortunately exclusively with Apple to track whatever belongings this gets forgotten in. I put it in my wallet when I go on trips and I put it in my pokemon binder for added security at conventions. It’s a great alternative to Apple’s Airtags, which are sometimes too bulky but still provides peace of mind when needing to FindMy devices. It makes a surprisingly audible noise when searched for from something so compact. Makes for a great stocking stuffer for anyone who’s synonymous with the very fun game “Has Anyone Seen My Wallet?” - Amir Rakib
Twelve South - AirFly Pro 2 The AirFly Pro 2 is my go-to travel essential that lets you pair your own noise-canceling headphones or wireless earbuds with airplane seatback entertainment systems —complete with dedicated dual-pairing buttons for sharing in-flight movies with a seatmate, on-device volume controls, and 25+ hours of battery life. Because it delivers low-latency Bluetooth audio from any 3.5mm jack, it also doubles as a handy adapter for gaming handhelds or a PS5 DualSense controller during layovers and hotel stays, making it a compact, high-utility stocking stuffer. And you can connect it to all of the Bluetooth headphones suggestions in this guide! - Libby Pei
ReMarkable: eink Digital Notebook The ReMarkable digital notebook is the perfect companion for avid notetakers and digital readers. It integrates seamlessly with my current lifestyle and travels almost everywhere with me. Besides the metallic build of the body and the really satisfying matted e-ink screen to write on, the tablet is a pleasure to write on, draw with, and work off of. It integrates with google drive, PDFs and epubs and syncs wirelessly with all my devices. It has auto handwriting recognition to digitize notes, but also lets you screenshot directly any doodles. It's a highly recommended alternative to tablets for any analog tech lovers and artists to embrace. pool.resumen:
Desde su inicio en 1979, la saga cinematográfica de Alien ha cautivado a los aficionados al cine de ciencia ficción con sus aterradoras criaturas extraterrestres y su intrincada mitología. Una saga que con los años ha ido incorporando entregas y nuevos elementos a su universo narrativo en una trayectoria algo irregular , eso hay que reconocerlo, pero que ha servido para cimentar la carrera de directores como Ridley Scott , James Cameron o David Fincher.

Lástima que esta chispa no llegara a incendiar las salas de cine, porque Alien 5 tenía una pinta espectacular .

Fortunately, Star Trek : First Contact understood that bigger could be better, provided the spectacle didn't come at the expense of the characters.
